row.title: Oriented Lorentzian fields, observers and coordinate conventions

items.title: Oriented Lorentzian fields, observers and coordinate conventions
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. These are distinct objects: an observer congruence is a vector field, an adapted chart is a coordinate chart, and a tetrad is a basis field. A tetrad field is not presumed to be a coordinate frame. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

A **worldline** on this Lorentzian manifold means a $C^1$ or piecewise-$C^1$ regular curve with future-timelike tangent and specified interval domain, as defined precisely in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Its parameter is arbitrary; the proper-time and four-velocity constructions of that definition apply under their stated hypotheses. A worldline is a mathematical curve here and does not assert the existence or motion of a physical body.

For coordinate bookkeeping only, when a chart is chosen with all four coordinate values assigned the metre, write $x^0=ct$, where $t$ is assigned seconds and $c>0$ is the corresponding scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Then $g_{ab}$ is recorded as dimensionless. This is a unit convention on a chart, not a claim that the chart is inertial, orthonormal, global, or physically realized; $c$ in this mathematical convention has no asserted measured value.

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The curvature coordinate formula contains one derivative of $\Gamma$ or a product of two $\Gamma$ components, so $R^a{}_{bcd}$ and its Ricci and scalar contractions are recorded in $\mathrm m^{-2}$. These component assignments apply only in length-coordinate charts; other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.
items.strategy: Normalize the supplied future timelike field; construct an adapted tetrad by projected-frame Gram–Schmidt on a neighbourhood; derive connection and curvature length units from the stated coordinate formulas.

items.title: Lorentzian exterior calculus and Hodge star
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian structure and volume form of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. On decomposable $k$-covectors define the induced exterior pairing by

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $I^c$ be its increasing complement, let $s(I,I^c)$ be the sign of the permutation $(I,I^c)$ to $(0,1,2,3)$, and set $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$. Then

$$\star_g e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}.$$

Consequently, on $k$-forms,

$$\star_g^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}.$$

In particular $\star_g^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on two-forms. For a two-form $F$, the component formula in a positively oriented chart is

$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].
items.strategy: Construct the pointwise star in a positively oriented Lorentz-orthonormal coframe, prove its defining identity and uniqueness, then derive smoothness, the star-square sign, the component formula and d-squared.

items.title: Conformal Hodge scaling in every degree
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], let $\Omega:M\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth dimensionless function, and set $\widetilde g=\Omega^2g$ with the same orientation $o$. For every smooth $k$-form $\beta$, $0\le k\le4$,

$$\star_{\widetilde g}\beta=\Omega^{4-2k}\star_g\beta.$$

In degree $2$ the Hodge star is unchanged. This is a statement about the Hodge operators of two conformally related Lorentz metrics; it asserts no conformal invariance of any curvature or field equation.
items.strategy: Scale the inverse metric and oriented volume, substitute into the unique Hodge characterization and use wedge nondegeneracy.

items.title: Observer electric/magnetic reconstruction and invariants
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq M$ be an open set with smooth observer congruence $n$, let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on $U$, and let $c>0$ be the coordinate conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Define covectors

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $c$ is the positive coordinate-conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with SI unit $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ in its length-coordinate convention. The names electric and magnetic distinguish these two covectors; for arbitrary mathematical $F$ no physical field unit or measurement is assigned.

For each $p\in U$, define the **rest covector space** by

$$\mathcal R^*_{n,p}:=\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n_p)=0\}.$$

The musical isomorphism $\flat_p$ maps the vector rest space $n_p^\perp$ onto $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$: $\alpha\in\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ iff $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,n_p)=\alpha(n_p)=0$. Moreover, $g_p^{-1}(v^\flat,w^\flat)=g_p(v,w)$, so the restriction of $g_p^{-1}$ to $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ is positive definite by [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The covectors $E_p$ and $B_p$ annihilate $n_p$; define $\langle E,B\rangle_n(p):=g_p^{-1}(E_p,B_p)$. Then

$$F=n^\flat\wedge E/c+\star_g(n^\flat\wedge B),$$

$$F_{ab}F^{ab}=2\bigl(\langle B,B\rangle_n-\langle E,E\rangle_n/c^2\bigr),\qquad F\wedge F=-\frac{2}{c}\langle E,B\rangle_n\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Equivalently, in any positively oriented future tetrad with $E_0=n$, and with $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ in its oriented spatial triad, the components satisfy $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. These are pointwise mathematical decompositions of an arbitrary two-form; no Maxwell equation or physical observation is assumed.
items.strategy: Use a local observer-adapted tetrad to compute all six independent two-form components, then contract and wedge to obtain the two scalar invariants.

items.title: Lorentz star square and constant two-form
items.design_state: Fully authored draft with complete local argument; independent review remains pending.
items.statement:
On $\mathbb R^4$ take the metric $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and the time-orientation field $N:=\partial_0$. Then $n:=\partial_0$ is an observer because $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)=-1<0$. For constants $c>0$ and $E_0,B_0\in\mathbb R$, let

$$F=-\frac{E_0}{c}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1+B_0\,dx^2\wedge dx^3.$$

This constant two-form has

$$\star_gF=\frac{E_0}{c}\,dx^2\wedge dx^3+B_0\,dx^0\wedge dx^1,\qquad \star_g^2F=-F,$$

$$F_{ab}F^{ab}=2(B_0^2-E_0^2/c^2),\qquad F\wedge F=-\frac{2E_0B_0}{c}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

The calculation concerns the mathematical Lorentzian Hodge operator and a smooth two-form. It does not assert that a physical field was measured or that a Maxwell model was adopted.
items.strategy: Substitute the constant two-form into the proved Lorentzian star, index-raising, wedge and exterior-derivative formulas.

row.title: SI and geometrized Einstein–Maxwell parameters

items.title: SI and geometrized Einstein–Maxwell parameters
items.design_state: reserved-EMG-C01 A definition; explicit SI and geometric parameter dictionary
items.statement:
Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and arbitrary smooth real two-form $F$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. In a chart using the coordinate convention $x^0=ct$ with all four coordinates assigned metres, assign the SI component unit tesla to $F_{ab}$; the two-form $F=\frac12F_{ab}\,dx^a\wedge dx^b$ then has unit weber.

For this conversion dictionary, take $c>0$, $G>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ as numerical input parameters, with SI dimensions

$$[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}},\qquad [G]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}},\qquad [\mu_0]=\mathrm{kg\,m\,C^{-2}}.$$

Define the derived parameters

$$\varepsilon_0:=\frac{1}{\mu_0c^2},\qquad \kappa:=\frac{8\pi G}{c^4},\qquad \alpha:=\sqrt{\frac{\kappa}{2\mu_0}},\qquad \mathcal F:=\alpha F.$$

Thus $\varepsilon_0$ has unit $\mathrm{C^2\,s^2\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\kappa$ has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$, $\alpha$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,s\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$, and the components $\mathcal F_{ab}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. In modern SI, $c$ is fixed exactly by the definition of the metre; $\mu_0$ is not fixed exactly and its numerical value is determined experimentally. Here the equations use only the positive symbolic parameters above, not a selected numerical value.

For a physical mass $M_{\!p}>0$ in kilograms, signed charge $Q_e$ in coulombs, and angular momentum $J_{\mathrm{ang}}$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$, define the geometric length parameters

$$m_{\mathrm{geo}}:=\frac{GM_{\!p}}{c^2},\qquad q_{\mathrm{geo}}:=\sqrt{\frac{G}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}\,Q_e,\qquad a_{\mathrm{geo}}:=\frac{J_{\mathrm{ang}}}{M_{\!p}c}.$$

For a supplied magnetic-flux parameter $\Phi_B$ in webers, also define $p_{\mathrm{geo}}:=\alpha\Phi_B/(4\pi)$ in metres. This is only a conversion of an already specified flux value; it asserts neither a global potential nor a magnetic source. The inverse parameter maps are $M_{\!p}=c^2m_{\mathrm{geo}}/G$, $Q_e=\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4/G}\,q_{\mathrm{geo}}$, $J_{\mathrm{ang}}=M_{\!p}c\,a_{\mathrm{geo}}$, and $\Phi_B=4\pi p_{\mathrm{geo}}/\alpha$.

The mass, charge, angular momentum and flux are inputs to this dictionary; their primitive or derived status in any physical model is framework-specific. No field equation, Maxwell postulate, matter law, or empirical value is part of this definition.

items.title: Exact geometric electrovac normalization
items.design_state: reserved-EMG-C01 A result; complete exact trace and normalization argument
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$, $F$, $\kappa$, $\mu_0$, $\alpha$ and $\mathcal F=\alpha F$ be as in [[def-emg-geometric-scaling]], with curvature tensors defined by [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant. Define the quadratic tensor

$$\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},$$

where indices are raised with $g^{-1}$. Then the following equations for the same metric and two-form are equivalent:

$$G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F),$$

$$G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=2\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F),$$

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g)-\Lambda g_{ab}=2\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F).$$

These are algebraic equivalences between tensor equations. No Maxwell equation, matter model, limiting procedure or physical solution is assumed.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4, author-hosted full-text HTML, Maxwell action, Einstein equation and electromagnetic stress tensor
Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, §§3.4–3.5, 4.3–4.5 and 7.2, curvature contractions, Maxwell equations and electromagnetic stress tensor

items.strategy: Use quadratic homogeneity to change the electromagnetic normalization, then take the four-dimensional trace and reverse the trace equation.

items.title: Four-dimensional conformal Maxwell covariance
items.design_state: reserved-EMG-C01 A result; complete conditional Hodge, current and stress transformations
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ and a smooth real two-form $F$ be as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $\Omega:M\to(0,\infty)$ be a smooth dimensionless function, put $\widetilde g=\Omega^2g$ with the same orientation, let $\mu_0>0$ be constant, and let $j$ be a smooth vector field. The Hodge operator is that of [[lem-emg-conformal-hodge-multiplier]]. Define

$$\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},\qquad T_{ab}(g,F):=\mu_0^{-1}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F).$$

Then $(F,j)$ satisfies the differential-form Maxwell equations

$$dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\,\iota_j\operatorname{vol}_g$$

if and only if $(F,\widetilde j)$ satisfies the same equations for $\widetilde g$, where $\widetilde j:=\Omega^{-4}j$. In addition,

$$\operatorname{vol}_{\widetilde g}=\Omega^4\operatorname{vol}_g,\qquad \iota_{\widetilde j}\operatorname{vol}_{\widetilde g}=\iota_j\operatorname{vol}_g,\qquad \widetilde T_{ab}=\Omega^{-2}T_{ab},\qquad \widetilde T^{ab}=\Omega^{-6}T^{ab}.$$

If $n$ is a $g$-unit timelike vector, then $\widetilde n:=\Omega^{-1}n$ is $\widetilde g$-unit timelike and $\widetilde T(\widetilde n,\widetilde n)=\Omega^{-4}T(n,n)$. On any oriented integration domain where the integral exists, or for a compactly supported action difference, the quadratic integral $\int F_{ab}F^{ab}\operatorname{vol}_g$ is unchanged. These are tensor identities; they do not assert Einstein-equation or matter-model invariance.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §3.1.3, author-hosted full-text HTML, Hodge dual
David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4.5.1, author-hosted full-text HTML, Maxwell field equation and action
Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, §§3.1–3.2 and 4.3–4.5, Hodge dual, Maxwell forms and electromagnetic stress

items.strategy: Apply the degree-two Hodge multiplier, determinant volume scaling, contraction linearity, and the explicit metric scalings of the quadratic tensor.

items.title: Conformal Einstein tensor transformation
items.design_state: reserved-EMG-C01 A result; complete connection-difference and curvature-contraction proof with explicit external mathematical prerequisites
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with the curvature convention and tensors of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Let $\Omega:M\to(0,\infty)$ be smooth and dimensionless, and put $\widetilde g=\Omega^2g$ with the same orientation. Use the metric-selected connection and its tensor derivative of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Define the smooth one-form and its contractions by

$$u:=\Omega^{-1}d\Omega,\qquad H_{ab}:=(\nabla_a u)_b,\qquad \theta:=g^{ab}H_{ab},\qquad s:=g^{ab}u_au_b.$$

Then $H_{ab}=H_{ba}$ and

$$\widetilde{\operatorname{Ric}}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-2H_{ab}-g_{ab}\theta+2u_au_b-2g_{ab}s,$$

$$\widetilde S=\Omega^{-2}(S-6\theta-6s),$$

$$\widetilde G_{ab}=G_{ab}-2H_{ab}+2u_au_b+2g_{ab}\theta+g_{ab}s.$$

All curvature conventions are those stated in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. These are mathematical transformation identities, not an assertion that the Einstein equation is conformally invariant.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4, author-hosted full-text HTML, conformal metric and Einstein equations
Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, §§3.3–3.5 and 7.2, curvature contractions, conformal compactification and Einstein–Maxwell equations

items.strategy: Compute the conformal connection difference, contract its curvature difference, expand both quadratic contractions, and trace to the scalar and Einstein tensors.

items.title: Constant coupled electrovac rescaling
items.design_state: reserved-EMG-C01 A result; complete constant coupled electrovac and source rescaling
items.statement:
Let $g,F,j,\Lambda,c,G,\mu_0,\kappa$ be as in [[def-emg-geometric-scaling]] and the four-dimensional Lorentzian curvature convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Suppose they satisfy the formal sourced Einstein–Maxwell equations

$$G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F),\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\,\iota_j\operatorname{vol}_g,$$

where $\mathcal Q$ is the quadratic tensor of [[thm-emg-field-normalization-equivalence]]. For a positive dimensionless constant $\lambda$, define

$$g':=\lambda^2g,\qquad F':=\lambda F,\qquad \Lambda':=\lambda^{-2}\Lambda,\qquad j':=\lambda^{-3}j.$$

Then $(g',F',j',\Lambda')$ satisfies the same equations with the same numerical constants $c,G,\mu_0$. In particular, a source-free electrovac solution ($j=0$) maps to a source-free electrovac solution. No transformation law for an additional matter stress tensor or matter action is asserted.

Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, §§3.4–3.5, 4.3–4.5 and 7.2, curvature, Maxwell forms and coupled Einstein–Maxwell equations

items.title: Exact small-field coupled residual order
items.design_state: reserved-EMG-C01 A result; exact fixed-background residual only, no solution-error theorem
items.statement:
Let $U$ be a smooth Lorentzian four-dimensional chart domain with metric $g$ as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], and let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be constant. Write $\Omega^k(U)$ for the smooth real $k$-forms on $U$. Here $d:\Omega^k(U)\to\Omega^{k+1}(U)$, $0\le k\le3$, is the exterior derivative with coordinate formula $(d\beta)_{a_0\ldots a_k}=(k+1)\partial_{[a_0}\beta_{a_1\ldots a_k]}$, and $\star_g:\Omega^2(U)\to\Omega^2(U)$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map characterized by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\frac12\alpha_{ab}\beta^{ab}\,\operatorname{vol}_g$ for $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^2(U)$, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both operators are real-linear. Suppose $G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=0$. Let $F_1\in\Omega^2(U)$ satisfy $dF_1=0$ and $d(\star_gF_1)=0$. For any real dimensionless $\varepsilon$, put $F_\varepsilon:=\varepsilon F_1$ and define

$$T^{(1)}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F_1),\qquad \mathscr R_{ab}(g,F;\Lambda):=G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F),$$

using $\kappa,\mu_0,\mathcal Q$ of [[def-emg-geometric-scaling]] and [[thm-emg-field-normalization-equivalence]]. Then $F_\varepsilon$ remains an exact source-free Maxwell field on the fixed metric and

$$\mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\varepsilon;\Lambda)=-\kappa\varepsilon^2T^{(1)}_{ab}.$$

For a smooth covariant two-tensor $S$ and compact $K\subset U$, define the chart component norm of its restriction by $\|S\|_{K}:=\max_{0\le a,b\le3}\sup_{p\in K}|S_{ab}(p)|$ when $K\ne\varnothing$. In this estimate and its applications, use $\sup_{p\in\varnothing}f(p):=0$ for nonnegative component functions $f$; equivalently, the empty restriction has $\|S\|_{\varnothing}:=0$. It is finite for smooth $S$ and satisfies

$$\|\mathscr R(g,F_\varepsilon;\Lambda)\|_K=\kappa\varepsilon^2\|T^{(1)}\|_K.$$

If $\varepsilon\ne0$ and $T^{(1)}$ is not identically zero on $K$, the fixed pair $(g,F_\varepsilon)$ is not an exact coupled Einstein–Maxwell solution on $K$. This is a residual estimate only; it gives no nearby metric, solution-distance bound, point-source solution or backreaction limit.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §4, author-hosted full-text HTML, Maxwell equations and quadratic electromagnetic stress
Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, §§4.3–4.5 and 7.2, Maxwell equations and electromagnetic stress tensor

items.strategy: Use linearity of source-free Maxwell equations and quadratic homogeneity of stress to compute the fixed-metric Einstein residual exactly.

items.design_state: reserved-EMG-C01 B-leaf counterexample; complete local conformal-curvature calculation
items.statement:
Fix positive constants $c,G,\mu_0$ and $\kappa=8\pi G/c^4$ as in [[thm-emg-field-normalization-equivalence]]. On the smooth oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], a **source-free electrovac solution with $\Lambda=0$** here means a metric $g$ and smooth real two-form $F$ satisfying

$$G_{ab}(g)=\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F),\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=0,$$

where $\mathcal Q_{ab}(g,F)=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}$ with indices raised by $g^{-1}$, as in [[thm-emg-field-normalization-equivalence]], and $d,\star_g$ are the operators used in [[thm-emg-conformal-maxwell]]. These equations define a mathematical solution class, without an assertion about nature.

Claim: in four dimensions, conformal covariance of the source-free Maxwell equations implies that every positive conformal rescaling of a source-free electrovac solution is again a solution of the same electrovac Einstein equations with $\Lambda=0$, keeping $F$ and the numerical constants fixed.

items.title: Coulomb field and geometric charge scale
items.design_state: reserved-EMG-C01 B-leaf example; exact exterior Coulomb coefficient conversion
items.statement:
On the exterior region $r>0$ of oriented Minkowski four-space, use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and radial coordinate $r$ in metres. For a signed charge parameter $Q_e$ in coulombs, consider the smooth Coulomb two-form whose only independent spherical component is

$$F_{0r}=-\frac{Q_e}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c\,r^2}.$$

The singular source point $r=0$ is outside the domain; this example records no measurement or distributional source.

items.statement:
Adopt SI units and the following model-local quantity roles. Here the selected Einstein–Maxwell framework combines the stated Lorentzian geometry with a classical electromagnetic two-form and current; this definition itself supplies no gravitational equation, matter action, or empirical claim. A primitive is an input or independent field variable of this formulation; a derived quantity is fixed by a stated construction from its inputs. Neither label is universal across physical theories, and unit choice alone does not determine it.

The spacetime data are a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless four-manifold $M$, a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a smooth time-orientation field, and an independent orientation, exactly as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The metric, its time orientation, and the manifold orientation are separate data. An observer at $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth observer congruence is a smooth field of such vectors. A local tetrad is a smooth basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; an observer congruence, a coordinate chart, and a tetrad are different objects. Tetrads and observer fields need only exist locally; this definition assumes no global inertial chart, global tetrad, or hypersurface-orthogonal congruence.

The electromagnetic field-strength variable $F$ is a smooth real two-form, hence an alternating covariant tensor of type $(0,2)$, on an open subset of $M$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. It is primitive in this formulation. For an observer congruence $n$, its electric and magnetic observer covectors are derived by

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $\star_g$ is the unique Hodge map characterized pointwise by $\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, using the metric and independent orientation, as in [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Both covectors annihilate $n$ and lie in the rest covector space $\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n)=0\}$, whose induced metric is positive definite. In a positively oriented future orthonormal tetrad with $e_0=n$ and $\epsilon_{123}=+1$, their spatial components obey the fixed dictionary $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ from [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. Thus $E$ and $B$ are observer-dependent derived fields, not globally defined observer-independent three-vectors on a curved spacetime. Their tetrad components have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla (T), respectively; the components of $F$ in a length-coordinate chart have unit T. No global potential is assumed; when a local potential $A_a$ is used, its components have unit $\mathrm{T\,m}$ and a scalar potential $\varphi$ has unit V.

For any chosen observer $n$, a smooth four-current is a vector field $j$ whose local decomposition is $j=c\rho\,n+J$, where $\rho:=-g(n,j)/c$ is the observer charge density and $J:=j-c\rho n$ is orthogonal to $n$. In the associated positively oriented orthonormal tetrad its components are $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The units are $[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[J^i]=[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[q]=\mathrm C$ for a charge parameter supplied by a matter model. The current is a prescribed input or is supplied by an explicitly stated matter model; it is not inferred from the Maxwell equation alone.

The SI constants and coordinate units are fixed as follows. The speed of ideal vacuum light $c>0$ is the exact SI defining constant $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; identifying it with the shared ideal-light and clock conversion constant is the adopted Minkowski model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], not a consequence of its unit definition. The elementary charge $e$ is exactly $1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm C$. These unit definitions do not imply that charge is quantized. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI, so no exact numerical value for $\mu_0$ is adopted. Define the electric constant (vacuum permittivity) $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$; hence $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$, and $\varepsilon_0$ has the same relative standard uncertainty as $\mu_0$ because $c$ is exact. The exact component equation $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ is dimensionally consistent: both sides have unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$ in a length-coordinate frame.

In a length-coordinate chart all four coordinate values are assigned metres, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate $t$ in seconds is selected. This is local coordinate bookkeeping, not a global inertial-coordinate claim. In such a chart $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless, the Levi-Civita coefficients $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have unit $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and curvature components have unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Components in other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

For the gravitational sector, take Newton's gravitational constant $G_N>0$ with unit $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$ and the cosmological constant parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ with unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ as primitive parameters of the selected model; no numerical value for either is used here. The coupling normalization $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from these parameters and has unit $\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. This definition records the convention for a later Einstein equation; it asserts no Einstein equation. A separate positive normalization $\kappa_0$ with unit weber (Wb) is a chosen flux conversion reserved for a later explicitly specified $U(1)$ formulation, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication. It is not $\kappa_E$, an electric charge, $\mu_0$, or Planck's constant, and it implies no charge quantization. Test-particle rest mass $m>0$ in kg and charge $q$ in C are externally supplied matter parameters, not quantities derived by classical electromagnetism.

These are SI and model-definition conventions only. They neither assert empirical measurements beyond the stated SI defining constants and measured status of $\mu_0$, nor identify similarly named quantities in another framework.

items.statement:
Adopt the following physical field law for this Einstein–Maxwell model. Let $M$ be a smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ as in [[def-emg-geometry-units]], let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $F\in\Omega^2(U)$ be a smooth real electromagnetic two-form, and let $j$ be a smooth four-current vector field on $U$. Using the Levi-Civita connection $\nabla^g$ of $g$, the SI constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$, and the field/current conventions of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], postulate

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

This is the selected smooth vacuum constitutive law. The first equation is the homogeneous field equation; the second is the sourced field equation with the sign fixed by $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $j=(c\rho,J)$ in a positively oriented inertial tetrad. No global potential is assumed: although $F=dA$ implies $dF=0$ when a smooth potential exists, the postulate applies to the two-form itself and does not assert that such an $A$ exists globally.

The postulate adopts one curved-spacetime continuation as a physical model assumption. The flat Minkowski and special-relativity suppliers [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] fix the inherited SI, inertial, and flat-limit conventions; they do not impose a globally flat metric on $M$ or deduce this curved field law. General-relativity sources describe covariant Maxwell formulations in their own unit and sign conventions; those treatments motivate the chosen formulation but neither mathematical structure nor source authority proves that this is nature's law. No empirical result is adopted here.

The model has no magnetic-charge term and no material excitation pair such as $D,H$. It applies only to smooth $F$ and $j$ on the stated domain; point and sheet sources, distribution-valued fields, and products of distributions require separate definitions and are outside this postulate.

items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ a nonempty open region, and $U=I\times\Omega$ a flat inertial Minkowski model with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and coordinates $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres. Let $E,B:U\to\mathbb R^3$ be jointly $C^1$, with every additional derivative displayed below existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Use $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $j^0=c\rho$, $j^i=J^i$, and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ as fixed by [[def-emg-geometry-units]].

On this flat specialization, the tensor systems from the smooth curved postulate are

$$(\mathrm{TM1})\quad \partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu\quad(\nu=0,1,2,3),\qquad (\mathrm{TM2})\quad \partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}=0\quad(\lambda,\mu,\nu=0,1,2,3).$$

They hold if and only if the four adopted smooth SI vacuum Maxwell equations hold on $U$:

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

Here $\partial_t$ is at fixed spatial position and $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ use the positively oriented Euclidean spatial basis. In addition, for the tensor force density $f^\nu:=F^{\nu\lambda}j_\lambda$, its time and spatial components satisfy

$$f^0=(J\cdot E)/c,\qquad f^i=\rho E_i+(J\times B)_i.$$

Thus they reproduce the adopted power density $J\cdot E$ divided by $c$ and force density $\rho E+J\times B$ of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]. The tensor systems have exactly eight independent scalar equations: four sourced components and four independent homogeneous components. All these are conditional component identities for the selected smooth model; no empirical premise is used. The result checks only the Maxwell subsystem on a flat background and the local force dictionary, not the coupled Einstein equation.

items.statement:
Let $E_0\in\mathbb R$ and $B_0\in\mathbb R$ be constant parameters with units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and tesla, respectively. On $M=\mathbb R^4$ use the flat Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the time orientation in which $\partial_0$ is future-directed, and the orientation for which $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ is positive. Use coordinates $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$ in metres and the future unit observer $n=\partial_0$. Set

$$F:=-\frac{E_0}{c}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1+B_0\,dx^2\wedge dx^3,\qquad j:=0.$$

The covariant components are constant, with $F_{01}=-E_0/c$, $F_{23}=B_0$, and all other independent components zero. The observer electric and magnetic covectors have spatial components $(E_0,0,0)$ and $(B_0,0,0)$, respectively. This is a prescribed-background example of the source-free Maxwell subsystem. It does not assert that the pair $(\eta,F)$ solves the coupled Einstein equation.

items.title: Finite-real supremum and infimum domain

references.title: Infimum and supremum (Wikipedia)
Least-upper-bound property (Wikipedia)
W. Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 1
John K. Hunter, An Introduction to Real Analysis
MIT 18.100A, Complete Lecture Notes

items.statement:
Use the real ordered field of [[def-real-numbers]] and [[def-complete-ordered-field]]. For a nonempty set $S\subseteq\mathbb R$ bounded above, $\sup S$ denotes the unique real upper bound $u$ such that $u\le v$ for every upper bound $v$. Existence is the least-upper-bound property established for these reals by [[thm-reals-cauchy-complete]]; if $u,u'$ both satisfy it, $u\le u'$ and $u'\le u$ imply equality. The notation is restricted to this domain.

For nonempty $S$ bounded below, use [[def-infimum]] and [[thm-infimum-property]]: $\inf S=-\sup(-S)$, where $-S=\{-s:s\in S\}$. Indeed a lower bound $l$ for $S$ gives the upper bound $-l$ for $-S$; negating its least upper bound gives a lower bound for $S$ greater than every other one.

Neither $\sup\varnothing$ nor $\inf\varnothing$ is defined in $\mathbb R$: every real is an upper and lower bound, with no least upper or greatest lower bound. If another construction stipulates the value zero for an empty path family, that stipulation is a separate total definition, not $\sup\varnothing=0$. Infinite values require an explicitly specified extended ordered set; no extended-real field operations are introduced here.

items.title: Real metric and pseudometric convention

references.title: Metric space (Wikipedia)
Ultrametric space (Wikipedia)
W. Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 2
T. Tao, Analysis II, 3rd ed., Ch. 1
Pseudometric space (Wikipedia)
R. Gardner, Introduction to Topology, notes on Munkres Section 20: The Metric Topology (East Tennessee State University)

items.statement:
Let $X$ be a set and use the ordered real field of [[def-real-numbers]], [[def-complete-ordered-field]] and [[def-ordered-field]]. In the convention of [[def-metric-space]], a **real metric** is a function $d:X\times X\to\mathbb R$ satisfying, for all $x,y,z\in X$, separation $d(x,y)=0\iff x=y$, symmetry $d(x,y)=d(y,x)$ and the triangle inequality $d(x,z)\le d(x,y)+d(y,z)$. A **real pseudometric** replaces separation by $d(x,x)=0$ and retains the other two axioms. All values are finite real numbers. Neither definition assumes nonnegativity as an additional axiom.

For either structure, put $B_d(x,r)=\{y\in X:d(x,y)<r\}$ for real $r>0$. The induced topology consists of the subsets $O\subseteq X$ for which every $x\in O$ admits $r>0$ with $B_d(x,r)\subseteq O$. After the nonnegativity deduction in the well-definedness lemma, these balls form a basis: $x\in B_d(x,r)$ by reflexivity, and if $z\in B_d(x,r)\cap B_d(y,s)$, the positive radius $t=\min\{r-d(x,z),s-d(y,z)\}$ has $B_d(z,t)$ contained in that intersection by the triangle inequality. This argument also works for pseudometrics and for empty $X$ (the empty topology). No infinite-distance, semimetric or quasimetric convention is consumed.

items.title: Explicit rational and real power regimes

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I
Radicals and rational exponents (Emory University)
Exponentiation (Wikipedia)
Nth root (Wikipedia)
W. Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 1

items.statement:
For $a>0$, integer $m$ and integer $n\ge1$, define the rational regime by

$$
a^{m/n}:=(a^{1/n})^m,
$$

where $a^{1/n}$ is the unique positive root of $s^n=a$ in [[thm-nth-roots-exist]], and integer powers include reciprocals for negative $m$. This is [[def-rational-power]]; [[lem-rational-power-well-defined]] proves independence of the fraction representative and [[lem-rational-power-laws]] gives the rational exponent laws. For the rational-exponent regime at base zero, retain the convention of [[def-rational-power]] and [[def-integer-power]]: $0^0=1$, $0^r=0$ for rational $r>0$, and $0^r$ is undefined for rational $r<0$. This records the integer zero-exponent convention together with the positive-rational supplementary clause; it does not extend the real-exponent convention.

The separate real-exponent regime is [[def-real-power]]: for $a>0$ and $x\in\mathbb R$, $a^x=\exp(x\log a)$, with the laws of [[thm-real-power-laws]]. For real exponents at base zero, set $0^x=0$ only when $x>0$; $0^0$ and $0^x$ for $x<0$ are undefined, exactly as in [[def-real-power]]. The rational and real exponent operations are separate definitions; at zero base and exponent zero, state which regime is intended: the rational/integer convention gives $1$, while the real-power convention leaves the expression undefined. No arbitrary real power is assigned to a negative base. The real-power laws are supplied by that theorem, not inferred from the rational root formula. Use the real-number structure of [[def-real-numbers]].

In particular $s(q)=q^{1/2}$ for $q>0$ is the unique positive solution of $s(q)^2=q$. Its smoothness and derivative are a separate well-definedness result, not an assumption about fractional notation.

items.title: The positive square-root branch is smooth

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, Theorem 8.5.1 and higher-regularity discussion

items.statement: For $q>0$, let $s(q)$ be the unique positive root specified in [[def-emg-explicit-power-regimes]]. Then $s:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ is smooth and $s'(q)=1/(2s(q))$.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, §3.1: Limits of functions
Limit of a function (Wikipedia)
W. Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis, 3rd ed., Ch. 4 (Def. 4.1)
T. Tao, Analysis I, 3rd ed., §9.3
J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I, §3.1

items.statement: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb R$, let $c\in\mathbb R$ be a limit point of $A$, let $f:A\to\mathbb R$ and $L\in\mathbb R$. Assume the indexed axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. Then the epsilon-delta condition $\lim_{x\to c}f(x)=L$ of [[def-function-limit]] is equivalent to the following: for every sequence $(x_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ with $x_n\in A\setminus\{c\}$ and $x_n\to c$, one has $f(x_n)\to L$. Sequence and sequence convergence mean [[def-sequence]] and [[def-real-limit]]. The forward direction uses no choice; the reverse direction uses only the stated indexed $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, not arbitrary-index choice.

items.title: Boundaryless domain for geometric completeness

references.title: Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry

items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff second-countable manifold **without boundary**, in the sense of [[def-smooth-manifold]]. Let $g$ be a positive definite smooth Riemannian metric as in [[def-riemannian-metric-symmetric-cotangent-connection-and-covariant-hessian]]. Use the Levi-Civita connection of [[def-levi-civita-connection]], whose existence and uniqueness for the supplied smooth Riemannian metric are proved by [[thm-fundamental-theorem-of-riemannian-geometry]]. The coordinate formula is supplied by [[prop-christoffel-formula-for-the-levi-civita-connection]]: its coefficients are $\Gamma^k_{ij}=\frac12g^{kl}(\partial_i g_{jl}+\partial_j g_{il}-\partial_l g_{ij})$. A parametrized affine geodesic is a smooth curve $\gamma:J\to M$ on an interval with nonempty interior satisfying $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma=0$, equivalently $\ddot\gamma^k+\Gamma^k_{ij}(\gamma)\dot\gamma^i\dot\gamma^j=0$, where covariant differentiation along the curve is defined by [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]; the coordinate equation is the expansion of that derivative in a coordinate basis. Its maximal domain is an interval on which it cannot be extended with the same affine parameter as a solution. **Two-sided geodesic completeness** means that every maximal affine geodesic is defined on all of $\mathbb R$.

Independently, for a real metric $d$ in [[def-metric-space]], a sequence $(x_n)$ is Cauchy when for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $N$ with $d(x_m,x_n)<\varepsilon$ whenever $m,n\ge N$. It converges to $x$ when for every $\varepsilon>0$ eventually $d(x_n,x)<\varepsilon$. **Metric completeness** means that every Cauchy sequence converges in the given metric space. In a Riemannian application the metric must be the distance induced by $g$ on a connected component: the infimum of lengths $\int\sqrt{g(\dot\alpha,\dot\alpha)}\,dt$ over piecewise-$C^1$ connecting curves. Its definition and finite metric property are supplied by [[def-riemannian-distance-on-a-connected-manifold]] and [[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]. Specify that induced metric, rather than an arbitrary compatible metric. Distinct components are treated separately; no infinite distance is inserted into a real metric.

These are different completeness conditions. Their equivalence is a Hopf–Rinow theorem requiring its own hypotheses and proof; it is not part of this definition. In particular, a Lorentzian metric is not a positive definite distance, and this convention supplies no Lorentzian Hopf–Rinow implication.

The boundaryless restriction matters: the Euclidean interval $[0,1]$ is metrically complete, while the curve $\gamma(t)=1/2+t$ stays inside it only for $-1/2\le t\le1/2$ and cannot be continued there as a two-sided affine geodesic with velocity $1$. Completeness of this interval follows because a real Cauchy sequence converges in $\mathbb R$ by [[thm-reals-cauchy-complete]] and its limit remains between $0$ and $1$. This boundary example explains the domain restriction; it is not an instance of the boundaryless equivalence.

items.title: Set-sized objects and definable-class schemas

references.title: B. Kaya, MATH 320 Set Theory (METU), §1.1
Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory (Wikipedia)
C. Wilson, A Brief Introduction to ZFC (Chicago REU 2016)

items.statement:
Use the first-order language of [[def-language-of-set-theory]]: all quantified objects are sets, and a **definable class** $\{x:\varphi(x,p)\}$ abbreviates a formula with set parameters $p$. It is not a new set or a domain for unrestricted quantification. Work with the usual set axioms, in particular [[def-axiom-of-power-set]] and [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]], and the ordered pairs, products and functions of [[def-ordered-pair]], [[def-cartesian-product]] and [[def-function]]. The power-set axiom supplies a collecting set; Separation trims it to exactly $\mathcal P(X)=\{Y:Y\subseteq X\}$.

A **small category** has a set $O$ of objects, a set $A$ of arrows, source and target functions $s,t:A\to O$, an identity function $e:O\to A$, and a composition function on the set $\{(a,b)\in A\times A:s(a)=t(b)\}$, where $ab$ denotes $a\circ b$ and the laws are $s(e(x))=t(e(x))=x$, $s(ab)=s(b)$, $t(ab)=t(a)$, $e(t(a))a=a=ae(s(a))$, and $(ab)c=a(bc)$ whenever the displayed compositions are defined. It is **locally small** when each specified hom-collection is a set. A definable large category is a schema of formulas for its objects, arrows and operations, with those laws asserted as formulas; it is not a set of all objects or a category of all large categories. No Grothendieck universe is assumed.

All indexed families in the local bundle construction have a supplied set index $I$. If $U_i\subseteq M$ and $G$ is a set, their tagged disjoint union is the subset $D=\{(i,x,z)\in I\times M\times G:x\in U_i\}$, formed by Separation. Given a set equivalence relation $E\subseteq D\times D$, each class $[u]_E=\{v\in D:(u,v)\in E\}$ is a subset of $D$, and the quotient is the set

$$
D/E=\{C\in\mathcal P(D):\exists u\in D\ \forall v\in D\ (v\in C\iff(u,v)\in E)\}.
$$

Thus the quotient is obtained by Separation in $\mathcal P(D)$, without choosing representatives. Transition-map graphs and connection data are subsets of specified finite products and power sets, not arbitrary proper-class objects.

For the Cauchy-development coding application, fix a set manifold $\Sigma$ and the tensor-bundle total spaces over $\Sigma\times\mathbb R$. A code consists of an open set $D\subseteq\Sigma\times\mathbb R$, graphs of a metric and a two-form on $D$ inside those fixed total spaces, a time orientation, and a fixed initial embedding. All of its coordinates belong to fixed products and power sets. Separation selects the tuples satisfying the specified smoothness, Lorentzian, field-equation and initial-data formulas. Hence these codes form a set. This size assertion does not prove field-equation existence, maximality or uniqueness, and makes no proper-class representative choice.

items.title: Extended pointwise product with zero at infinite factors

references.title: Sheldon Axler, Measure, Integration & Real Analysis, extended-real multiplication convention

items.statement:
Let $\overline{\mathbb R}=\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$ be the ordered set of [[def-extended-reals]]. Define a new total operation $\star:\overline{\mathbb R}\times\overline{\mathbb R}\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ as follows. If $a=0$ or $b=0$, put $a\star b=0$. If both factors are finite, put $a\star b=ab$ using real multiplication. In the remaining cases both factors are nonzero and at least one is infinite; put

$$a\star b:=\begin{cases}+\infty,&\operatorname{sgn}(a)\operatorname{sgn}(b)=1,\\-\infty,&\operatorname{sgn}(a)\operatorname{sgn}(b)=-1,\end{cases}$$

where $\operatorname{sgn}(a)=1$ for $a>0$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(a)=-1$ for $a<0$ in the extended order. The clauses exhaust the domain and agree when a zero factor is finite, so they specify a unique value for every pair. Thus $0\star(\pm\infty)=0$, $(+\infty)\star(-2)=-\infty$, and $(-\infty)\star(-\infty)=+\infty$.

For any set $X$ and maps $f,g:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$, their **extended pointwise product with zero at infinite factors** is the map $f\star g:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ defined by $(f\star g)(x)=f(x)\star g(x)$.

items.title: Lp classes and explicit representatives

references.title: Sheldon Axler, Measure, Integration & Real Analysis, Definition 7.17 and Theorem 7.18

items.statement:
Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space in [[def-measure-space]]. Give $\mathbb R$ the order topology $\mathcal T_{<}$ of [[def-order-topology-on-a-linearly-ordered-set]], which that supplier identifies with the usual real topology, and let $\mathcal B(\mathbb R):=\sigma_{\mathbb R}(\mathcal T_{<})$ be its Borel sigma-algebra as in [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]. A measurable real function is a map $f:X\to\mathbb R$ measurable from $(X,\Sigma)$ to $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B(\mathbb R))$ in the sense of [[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]. For $1\le p<\infty$, let the representative space be $\mathcal L^p(\mu)=\{f:X\to\mathbb R: f\text{ is measurable and }\int_X|f|^p\,d\mu<\infty\}$, exactly the supplier definition [[def-calligraphic-l-p-on-a-measure-space]]. For $p=\infty$, the representatives are the measurable real functions for which $\mu(\{x:|f(x)|>C\})=0$ for some finite $C\ge0$. The level sets used here are measurable by [[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]. This finite-bound condition is exactly $\|f\|_\infty<\infty$ in [[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]] and [[def-l-infinity-on-a-measure-space]]: if such a $C$ exists then the essential supremum is at most $C$; conversely, if the essential supremum is finite, [[prop-essential-supremum-is-attained-as-the-least-essential-bound]] proves that this finite value itself is an essential bound.

For measurable $f,g:X\to\mathbb R$, the difference $f-g$ is measurable by the addition and scalar-multiplication clauses of [[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]. Therefore

$$\{x:f(x)\ne g(x)\}=(f-g)^{-1}(\mathbb R\setminus\{0\})\in\Sigma,$$

because $\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ is open in the stated topology and hence Borel. On either representative space put

$$f\sim g\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mu(\{x\in X:f(x)\ne g(x)\})=0.$$

By [[def-null-subspace-of-almost-everywhere-zero-functions]] and [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]], this is equivalent to $f-g\in\mathcal N(\mu)$, so it is exactly the relation in [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]. The element $[f]\in L^p(\mu)$ is the equivalence class of $f$; an **explicit representative** is a specified measurable function belonging to that class. The quotient norms are

$$\|[f]\|_p=\left(\int_X|f|^p\,d\mu\right)^{1/p}\quad(1\le p<\infty),\qquad\|[f]\|_\infty=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_X|f|,$$

with independence of representative and the norm axioms supplied by [[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]].

A pointwise statement such as $f(x)=0$ concerns the selected representative. A property invariant under almost-everywhere equality, such as $f=0$ almost everywhere, concerns the class. No value of $[f]$ at a particular point is defined by this quotient.

items.title: Local potentials and smooth circle-bundle connection data
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

By [[def-de-rham-cohomology]], $H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)=Z^2(M)/B^2(M)$, where $Z^2(M)$ is the vector space of closed smooth two-forms and $B^2(M)$ is the vector space of exact smooth two-forms. Thus, for closed $F$, the statement $[F]=0$ means exactly that $F=dA$ for a global smooth one-form $A$. This equivalence is the quotient definition; it does not assert that every closed form is exact.

Identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$ by $z=x+iy$ and set $U(1)=S^1:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$. Its topology is the subspace topology. Specify its smooth structure by the four charts

$$V_{x,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon x>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto y,\quad y\mapsto(\epsilon\sqrt{1-y^2},y),$$

and

$$V_{y,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon y>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto x,\quad x\mapsto(x,\epsilon\sqrt{1-x^2}),$$

for $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, with each coordinate range $(-1,1)$. They cover $S^1$; their transition maps are restrictions of the positive square-root branch and coordinate projections, hence are smooth by [[lem-emg-positive-square-root-smoothness]] and [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]. In these coordinates multiplication is the restriction of $(x,y)(u,v)=(xu-yv,xv+yu)$ and inversion is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$, so both are smooth; they are also continuous for the stated topology. Thus this is a smooth Lie group and, in particular, a topological group as required by [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]].

Let $E:\mathbb R\to U(1)$ be $E(t)=e^{it}=(\cos t,\sin t)$; the Cartesian formula is [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The trigonometric derivative identities of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], iterated, show that $E$ is smooth in the $C^\infty$ sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: every derivative of either coordinate is $\pm\sin$ or $\pm\cos$, and these functions are continuous by [[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]. Surjectivity is [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]]. If $E(t)\in V_{x,\epsilon}$, the chart coordinate $\sin t$ has derivative $\cos t=x\ne0$; if $E(t)\in V_{y,\epsilon}$, the coordinate $\cos t$ has derivative $-\sin t=-y\ne0$. The smooth inverse-function theorem [[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]] therefore makes $E$ a diffeomorphism from some open interval about $t$ onto an open circle arc. Every smooth map from an open subset of $M$ to $U(1)$ consequently has, near each point, a smooth real phase lift obtained by composing with such a local inverse.

A **normalized circle-connection datum** on $M$ consists of a supplied countable open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth real one-forms $a_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, and a fixed constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on every triple intersection. Around each point of $U_i\cap U_j$, take any smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$ with $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$; require

$$
a_j=a_i+df_{ij}
$$

on every such phase-lift neighborhood. If $f$ and $\widetilde f$ are two lifts on a connected neighborhood, [[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]] gives $f-\widetilde f\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ pointwise; continuity makes this difference constant, so $df=d\widetilde f$. Thus the compatibility condition is independent of the chosen lift. The globally defined form $\lambda(g):=-i\,g^{-1}dg$ is real, and [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]] together with [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] gives $\lambda(g)=df$ on every phase-lift neighborhood. Hence the equivalent lift-free condition is $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$.

The right principal $U(1)$-bundle convention is as defined in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]: it has a continuous right action and locally trivial equivariant product charts, with free and transitive action on each fibre. The compatible transition functions are the gluing data for such a bundle, in the convention that a point with fibre coordinate $z_i$ in chart $i$ has coordinate $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$ in chart $j$. No global real-valued angle on $U(1)$ is assumed.

The constant $\kappa_0$ is a chosen normalization with units of webers; it is not Planck's constant and is not a unit of electric charge. On a chart whose coordinates have length units, the normalized connection components $a_i$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the corresponding local potential $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and its curvature $F_i:=dA_i=\kappa_0\,da_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. This definition imposes no flux or charge quantization.

items.title: Radial primitives for closed one- and two-forms
items.statement:
Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be an open set star-shaped about $p\in D$, meaning $p+t(x-p)\in D$ for every $x\in D$ and $0\le t\le1$. Let $F=\frac12F_{ab}\,dx^a\wedge dx^b$ be a smooth real closed two-form on $D$. Use Einstein summation over coordinate indices $a,b,c\in\{0,1,2,3\}$. Define

$$
A_b(x):=\int_0^1 t(x-p)^aF_{ab}(p+t(x-p))\,dt.
$$

Then $A=A_b\,dx^b$ is a smooth real one-form on $D$ and $dA=F$. More generally, if $\alpha=\alpha_a dx^a$ is a smooth closed one-form on $D$, then

$$
\chi(x):=\int_0^1(x-p)^a\alpha_a(p+t(x-p))\,dt
$$

is smooth and $d\chi=\alpha$. The first formula gives a local potential for every smooth closed two-form in a star-shaped coordinate chart; it does not assert global exactness.

items.title: Circle gluing, curvature and connection variations
items.statement: Let $M$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable oriented four-manifold, and let $(U_i,g_{ij},a_i;\kappa_0)$ be a normalized circle-connection datum as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Use the set-sized-object and quotient convention of [[def-emg-set-size-and-class-schema]]. Then the chart data construct a smooth Hausdorff second-countable right principal $U(1)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a global smooth real connection one-form $\omega$ on $P$. Its curvature is basic: there is a smooth closed two-form $f\in\Omega^2(M)$ with $d\omega=\pi^*f$ and $f|_{U_i}=da_i$. The local potentials $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ satisfy $dA_i=F$, where $F=\kappa_0 f$ is global. For two connections on the same fixed bundle with the same transition functions, their local-form differences are restrictions of one global base one-form; adding a global one-form to all local representatives stays in that bundle sector.

items.title: Sphere winding, nonexact curvature and flat holonomy
items.statement:
For $b\in\mathbb R$, let $M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$, $r=(x^2+y^2+z^2)^{1/2}$, and define the smooth real two-form

$$
F_b:=\frac{b}{r^3}\left(x\,dy\wedge dz+y\,dz\wedge dx+z\,dx\wedge dy\right).
$$

Give $M$ its canonical Minkowski metric

$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2,$$

of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, the time orientation selected by the smooth timelike vector field $N:=\partial_{x^0}$, and the product orientation $o:=dx^0\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$. Thus $(M,g,N,o)$ is the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold required by [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Its underlying product smooth structure and orientation are the standard ones on this open subset of $\mathbb R^4$.

Use the standard Euclidean inner product and norm on the spatial $\mathbb R^3$ factor in all spatial dot products and radii below.

On the locus $x^2+y^2>0$, define dimensionless polar coordinates by $x=r\sin\theta\cos\phi$, $y=r\sin\theta\sin\phi$, $z=r\cos\theta$, where $0<\theta<\pi$ and $\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$. There $d\phi=(x\,dy-y\,dx)/(x^2+y^2)$; only this differential, not a global real-valued angle, is used on the north-south overlap. The displayed north and south potential formulas are interpreted on angular coordinate neighborhoods and extended across their respective axes as verified in step 2.2.

In a fixed $x^0$-slice, write $S^2:=\{u\in\mathbb R^3:|u|_2=1\}$, where $|u|_2=(u_1^2+u_2^2+u_3^2)^{1/2}$, and give it the outward orientation: its area form is $\omega_u(v,w):=\det(u,v,w)$ for tangent vectors $v,w\in T_uS^2$. This is a compact smooth sphere; compactness follows from closedness and boundedness by [[thm-heine-borel-rn]].

Let $U_N=\{(x^0,x,y,z)\in M:r+z>0\}$ and $U_S=\{(x^0,x,y,z)\in M:r-z>0\}$; these two open sets cover $M$. Then $dF_b=0$ and its flux through the unit sphere with outward orientation is $4\pi b$. If $b\ne0$, $F_b$ has no global one-form potential on $M$. On $U_N$ and $U_S$,

$$
A_N=b(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad A_S=-b(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi
$$

are smooth local potentials with $dA_N=dA_S=F_b$, and $A_S-A_N=-2b\,d\phi$ on the overlap. For a chosen normalization $\kappa_0>0$, these local forms define the normalized circle-connection data of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] precisely when the transition $g_{NS}=e^{-2ib\phi/\kappa_0}$ is single-valued, equivalently $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$. For a smooth loop $g(e^{i\phi})=e^{i\chi(\phi)}$, its winding is $[\chi(2\pi)-\chi(0)]/(2\pi)$, with both circles oriented by increasing angle. Existence of a smooth phase lift, integrality of its endpoint change, and independence of the lift are proved in the phase-lift construction below. The transition winding has sign $-2b/\kappa_0$ in the stated north-to-south convention, while $\int_{S^2}F_b/(2\pi\kappa_0)=2b/\kappa_0$. This is an exact condition for this chosen circle normalization, not a claim that every classical real flux is quantized. When $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$, the compatible two-set data also produce a smooth principal circle-bundle connection, using the actual set-size interface in [A1] and the gluing statement of [[lem-emg-circle-connection-gluing]].

There is also a flat example with nontrivial holonomy. On $M_0=\mathbb R\times S^1\times\mathbb R^2$ with product smooth structure, take $S^1=U(1)$ with the smooth structure defined above. Write $w\in S^1$ for the base-circle coordinate and let $\nu=-i w^{-1}dw$ be its global real angular one-form, normalized by $\int_{S^1}\nu=2\pi$. For dimensionless $a\in\mathbb R$, set $A=\kappa_0 a\,\nu$. On the product bundle $P_0=M_0\times U(1)$ with projection $\pi(x,z)=x$ and right action $(x,z)\cdot\zeta=(x,z\zeta)$, use $\omega=\vartheta+a\pi^*\nu$, where $z\in U(1)$ is the fibre coordinate and $\vartheta=-i z^{-1}dz$ is its real angular form. Holonomy means the fibre multiplier of the horizontal lift around the indicated base loop; gauge trivial means gauge-equivalent to $\vartheta$ under a smooth bundle map $G_u(x,z)=(x,z u(x))$ covering the identity. Then $F=dA=0$ but holonomy around the circle is $e^{-2\pi ia}$, so this connection is gauge trivial exactly when $a\in\mathbb Z$. If $b$ and $\kappa_0$ are assigned physical units, both are measured in webers; the ratio $2b/\kappa_0$ is dimensionless. No general classification of circle bundles is asserted.

items.statement:
Use the conditional, still-escalated draft result [[lem-emg-sphere-flux-holonomy]] with $b=\kappa_0/2$. Its authored supplier status and remaining external closure obligation are recorded below; no independent proof acceptance is asserted. The local potentials are

$$
A_N=\frac{\kappa_0}{2}(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad A_S=-\frac{\kappa_0}{2}(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi.
$$

They have common curvature $F=\frac{\kappa_0}{2}\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$, flux $2\pi\kappa_0$, and transition $g_{NS}=e^{-i\phi}$ of winding number $-1$ under the north-to-south convention. The example is a mathematical circle-connection patch model. It is not an observation of a magnetic monopole and makes no quantum or empirical claim.

items.title: The scaled three-torus as a smooth compact flat spatial manifold
items.design_state: New local prerequisite authored on the A page because no current carrier supplied the exact smooth scaled-torus geometry used by the assigned B example.
items.statement:
Let $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ be real periods, let
$\Lambda:=L_1\mathbb Z\times L_2\mathbb Z\times L_3\mathbb Z\subseteq\mathbb R^3$,
and let $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_L:=\mathbb R^3/\Lambda$ be the quotient
map with the quotient topology. Then $q$ is a smooth local diffeomorphism and
$\mathbb T^3_L$ is a compact,
Hausdorff, second-countable smooth three-manifold without boundary.

The forms $dx^1,dx^2,dx^3$ and coordinate vector fields
$\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$ on $\mathbb R^3$ descend to global smooth
forms and vector fields on $\mathbb T^3_L$. Every smooth $\Lambda$-periodic
function on $\mathbb R^3$ descends to a smooth function on $\mathbb T^3_L$.
Consequently, $M_L:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times\mathbb T^3_L$ has a smooth,
boundaryless four-manifold structure and carries the smooth Lorentzian metric,
orientation, and time orientation

$$g:=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2,\qquad N:=\partial_0,\qquad o:=dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3.$$

In the product charts from the quotient atlas the metric has constant matrix
$\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and its metric-selected Christoffel symbols
vanish.

items.title: Sourced Maxwell sign and current conservation
items.design_state: Complete conditional mathematical proof authored; all inspected current suppliers are published and present.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

items.title: Compact potential and metric variation of the Maxwell action
items.design_state: Complete conditional proof authored; actual batch-2 connection-data carriers match the used interface, but their seven inherited prerequisites remain unavailable; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with the metric
volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and let $c,\mu_0>0$ be fixed
real coefficients. The action density is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EM}}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g=-\frac{1}{2\mu_0c}F\wedge\star_gF.$$

When this density has a global integral, denote it by $S_{\mathrm{EM}}[g,F]$.
On a noncompact domain, every displayed variation below means the finite
action difference supported by the compactly supported variation.

Assume the fixed smooth bundle sector and connection-variation interface in
[A1] below. Then:

**(a) Connection variation.** For every smooth compactly supported global
one-form $\alpha$ allowed by that fixed-sector interface, holding $g$ fixed gives $\delta F=d\alpha$ and

$$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{EM}}[\alpha]=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_M(\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If a differentiable source-sector functional on the same variations satisfies
$\delta_A S_{\mathrm{m}}[\alpha]=c^{-1}\int_Mj^b\alpha_b\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ for a
smooth vector field $j$, then stationarity of
$S_{\mathrm{EM}}+S_{\mathrm m}$ under every such $\alpha$ is equivalent on $M$ to

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

and hence to $d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. This is a conditional variational
calculation; it asserts no matter-action existence or physical adoption.

**(b) Metric variation.** For a smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse
metric variation $q^{ab}:=\delta g^{ab}$, holding the lower components
$F_{ab}$ fixed and preserving Lorentz signature for sufficiently small
parameter, define $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ by

$$\delta_gS_{\mathrm{EM}}[q]=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

This is the tensor obtained by varying the free electromagnetic action; it
contains no stress contribution from a source or matter functional.

items.title: Gauss charge and finite-chain flux balance
items.design_state: Complete finite-chain proof authored from the current-form result and inspected Stokes/flux suppliers.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], let
$F\in\Omega^2(M)$ and $j\in\Gamma(TM)$ be smooth, and fix constants
$c,\mu_0>0$. Assume
$dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, equivalently
$d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. A finite smooth singular $k$-chain means
a finite formal real linear combination of smooth singular $k$-simplices,
with the boundary operation of
[[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]] and
[[thm-stokes-theorem-for-smooth-singular-chains]].

For a finite smooth singular three-chain $\Sigma$, define its charge by

$$Q(\Sigma):=\frac1c\int_\Sigma\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Then:

**(a) Gauss charge formula.** For every such $\Sigma$,

$$Q(\Sigma)=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_{\partial\Sigma}\star_gF.$$

Consequently, if $\partial\Sigma=0$, then $Q(\Sigma)=0$. This is the
compact-cycle neutrality constraint for a smooth everywhere-defined sourced
field.

**(b) Bounding-surface restriction.** For every finite smooth singular
three-chain $V$, the magnetic flux through its boundary vanishes:

$$\int_{\partial V}F=0.$$

The equation $dF=0$ does not imply that the flux through every closed
two-cycle is zero; this item gives a zero-flux conclusion only when the cycle
is the boundary of a finite smooth chain in the field domain. Likewise, the
electric flux formula in (a) identifies charge with flux only for a bounding
surface.

**(c) Charge balance.** If a finite smooth singular four-chain $C$ satisfies
$\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for three-chains
$\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,B$, then

$$Q(\Sigma_2)-Q(\Sigma_1)=-Q(B).$$

Equal charge on the two slices therefore requires zero net side flux. No
asymptotic charge or flux at infinity is asserted; noncompact limits require
separate convergence and boundary-flux hypotheses.

items.design_state: Complete conditional component proof authored; the variational tensor supplier remains conditional on the escalated batch-2 chain and its seven missing inherited inputs.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $U\subseteq M$
be open, let $n$ be a smooth observer congruence on $U$, and let $F$ be a
smooth real two-form. Fix $c,\mu_0>0$ and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Assume the fixed-sector variational hypotheses
and tensor formula supplied conditionally by
[[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]], namely

$$T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}:=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

For the smooth observer covectors $E,B$ of
[[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]], define the rest projector
$h^a{}_b:=\delta^a_b+n^an_b$ and the observer energy flux
$S_n^a:=-c\,h^a{}_bT_{\mathrm{EM}}^{bc}n_c$. Then:

**(a) Tensor symmetries.** $T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}$ is symmetric and
$g^{ab}T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=0$.

**(b) Orthonormal observer components.** In any positively oriented
orthonormal tetrad with $E_0=n$ and spatial orientation
$\epsilon_{123}=+1$, the components are

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{00}=\frac12\left(\epsilon_0\sum_iE_i^2+\frac1{\mu_0}\sum_iB_i^2\right),\qquad T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{0i}=\frac{(\mathbf E\times\mathbf B)_i}{\mu_0c},$$

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ij}=-\left[\epsilon_0\left(E_iE_j-\frac12\delta_{ij}\sum_kE_k^2\right)+\frac1{\mu_0}\left(B_iB_j-\frac12\delta_{ij}\sum_kB_k^2\right)\right].$$

Here $(\mathbf E\times\mathbf B)_i:=\epsilon_{ijk}E_jB_k$. In particular,
$T_{\mathrm{EM},0i}=-T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{0i}$ in this tetrad.

**(c) Observer energy and flux.** The measured energy density
$u_n:=T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}n^an^b$ equals the nonnegative value in part (b), and
the spatial vector $S_n$ has components
$S_n^i=(\mathbf E\times\mathbf B)_i/\mu_0$ and $S_n^0=0$.

**(d) Geometric normalization.** For every smooth real two-form $H$, define

$$Q_g(H)_{ab}:=H_{ac}H_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}H_{cd}H^{cd}.$$

For every real constant $\lambda$, $Q_g(\lambda H)=\lambda^2Q_g(H)$. Fix also a formal constant $G_N>0$, and use the positive square-root convention of [[def-emg-explicit-power-regimes]] to set

$$\alpha:=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad\mathcal F:=\alpha F,\qquad\kappa_E:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}.$$

Then $\alpha>0$ and

$$\kappa_ET_{\mathrm{EM},ab}=2Q_g(\mathcal F)_{ab}.$$

For formal SI dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates $x^0=ct$, take dimensionless $g_{ab}$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}\,A^{-2}}$, and $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$. Then $[T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{m^{-1}\,T^{-1}}$, $[\mathcal F_{ab}]=\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, and both sides of the last identity have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. Components in angular or other scaled coordinates acquire their units through the coordinate Jacobian. A two-form $\mathcal F$ integrated over an oriented two-surface has length units under these assignments. These conventions introduce no measured constant or physical field-law premise.

These are conditional mathematical tensor identities. The batch-2 connection carriers are authored drafts. No independent proof acceptance or native readiness is claimed here.
