items.title: Compact boundaryless Gauss neutrality
items.design_state: Complete explicit compact-torus model and finite-chain verification; geometry, trigonometric regularity, and integration prerequisites are explicit.
items.statement:
Fix periods $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ and use the smooth quotient geometry and global
forms and vector fields supplied by
[[lem-emg-scaled-three-torus-smooth]]. In its coordinates set
$M:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times\mathbb T^3_L$, with
$g=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2$, orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and time orientation
$N=\partial_0$. Fix $c,\mu_0>0$ as real coefficients and put

$$\widetilde f(x):=\cos\left(\frac{2\pi x^1}{L_1}\right),\qquad \widetilde h(x):=\frac{L_1}{2\pi}\sin\left(\frac{2\pi x^1}{L_1}\right).$$

These lifts on $\mathbb R^3$ are independent of $x^2,x^3$ and are
$\Lambda$-periodic. Let $f,h:\mathbb T^3_L\to\mathbb R$ be their unique
smooth descents, so $f\circ q=\widetilde f$ and $h\circ q=\widetilde h$.
The descended global vector field $\partial_1$ satisfies
$\partial_1h=f$ and $dh=f\,dx^1$. On the lifts,
$\widetilde h'=\widetilde f$ and
$\widetilde h(L_1,x^2,x^3)=\widetilde h(0,x^2,x^3)$. Define the smooth
current and field

$$j:=f\,\partial_0,\qquad F:=-\mu_0h\,dx^0\wedge dx^1.$$

Let $\iota_*:\mathbb T^3_L\to M$ be the slice inclusion
$y\mapsto(x^0_*,y)$, and let
$$T_3:=\{s\in\mathbb R^3:s_i\ge0,\ s_1+s_2+s_3\le1\}.$$
Orient the slice by the restriction of the global form
$dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.
Let $\theta:T_3\to\Delta^3$ be the affine identification
$\theta(s)=(1-s_1-s_2-s_3,s_1,s_2,s_3)$. Let $\Sigma$ be the oriented
spatial slice $x^0=x^0_*$, represented as a finite smooth singular chain as
follows. Triangulate the fundamental cube
$[0,L_1]\times[0,L_2]\times[0,L_3]$ by the six tetrahedra indexed by
$\sigma\in S_3$. The ordered vertices of tetrahedron $\sigma$ are
$0$, $L_{\sigma(1)}e_{\sigma(1)}$,
$L_{\sigma(1)}e_{\sigma(1)}+L_{\sigma(2)}e_{\sigma(2)}$, and
$(L_1,L_2,L_3)$. Let $\phi_\sigma:T_3\to\mathbb R^3$ be the affine map
taking $0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ to these ordered vertices; it extends affinely to
$\mathbb R^3$. Define the smooth singular simplex
$\psi_\sigma:=\iota_*\circ q\circ\phi_\sigma\circ\theta^{-1}:\Delta^3\to M$;
in the standard $T_3$ parameter it satisfies
$\psi_\sigma\circ\theta=\iota_*\circ q\circ\phi_\sigma$. It extends
smoothly to a neighborhood of $\Delta^3$ in its affine plane because
$\phi_\sigma$ extends affinely and $q,\iota_*$ are smooth. Put
$\Sigma:=\sum_{\sigma\in S_3}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\psi_\sigma$.
Thus each simplex maps into the slice of $M$. The determinant of the
ordered edge vectors is $L_1L_2L_3\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$, so this
coefficient gives each simplex the cube orientation. The six regions are the
orderings $0\le u_{\sigma(3)}\le u_{\sigma(2)}\le u_{\sigma(1)}\le1$ of
$u_i:=x^i/L_i$; their interiors are disjoint and their union is the cube.
Internal faces cancel in pairs, and opposite cube faces are identified by
period translations with opposite boundary orientations, as verified below.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9]
  \coordinate (O) at (0,0);
  \coordinate (X) at (2,0);
  \coordinate (Y) at (1,0.7);
  \coordinate (XY) at (3,0.7);
  \coordinate (Z) at (0,1.7);
  \coordinate (XZ) at (2,1.7);
  \coordinate (YZ) at (1,2.4);
  \coordinate (XYZ) at (3,2.4);
  \draw[thick] (O)--(X)--(XY)--(Y)--cycle;
  \draw[thick] (Z)--(XZ)--(XYZ)--(YZ)--cycle;
  \draw[thick] (O)--(Z) (X)--(XZ) (Y)--(YZ) (XY)--(XYZ);
  \draw[densely dotted,very thick] (O)--(XYZ);
  \node[below left] at (O) {$0$};
  \node[right] at (XYZ) {$(L_1,L_2,L_3)$};
  \node at (1.35,1.25) {six tetrahedra};
  \node[above] at (1.4,2.75) {$x^3=0\sim L_3$};
  \node[below] at (1.5,-0.42) {$x^1=0\sim L_1$};
  \node[right] at (3.55,1.3) {$x^2=0\sim L_2$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The perspective box depicts the fundamental cube, with opposite faces paired
by the labels. Its dotted body diagonal is the shared edge of the six affine
tetrahedra indexed by coordinate permutations. The drawing is schematic and
is not used in the chain-boundary proof above.

items.design_state: Complete conditional lemma authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with metric-selected connection $\nabla$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth principal $U(1)$ bundle with a smooth connection and global curvature two-form $F$, using the local-potential and fixed-sector conventions of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] and [[lem-emg-circle-connection-gluing]]. Let $\Psi$ be a smooth matter configuration and let $S_m$ be a real differentiable functional of $(g,A,\Psi)$, where $A$ denotes the bundle connection, not necessarily a global one-form.

Fix a configuration at which the matter Euler–Lagrange variation vanishes, meaning $\delta_\Psi S_m=0$ for every smooth compactly supported matter-field variation. Suppose that for all compactly supported metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$ and all compactly supported connection variations $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ in the fixed bundle sector, the remaining first variation is

$$\delta S_m=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T^m_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+\frac{1}{c}\int_M j^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $c>0$, $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and $j$ is a smooth vector field. Assume $S_m$ is invariant under compactly supported gauge transformations and under simultaneous pullback along the local flow of every compactly supported smooth vector field, with the connection and matter field transported by the induced horizontal lift to $P$. Only the local variations at flow parameter $s=0$ are used. Then

$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_a T_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c,$$

where $j_c:=g_{ca}j^a$. These are conditional variational identities; no Maxwell or Einstein field equation, existence theorem, or empirical premise is assumed.

For SI bookkeeping in length coordinates, take $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, and $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$. If $S_m$ is assigned action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$, the displayed variation convention assigns $[T^m]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. These are formal dimensional assignments only; the lemma adopts no matter model or empirical law.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. For a compactly supported metric variation, write $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$, $h_{ab}=\delta g_{ab}=-g_{ac}g_{bd}q^{cd}$, $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, and $V^a=g^{bd}\delta\Gamma^a{}_{db}-g^{ab}\delta\Gamma^d{}_{db}$, where $\delta\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\frac12g^{ad}(\nabla_bh_{cd}+\nabla_ch_{bd}-\nabla_dh_{bc})$; curvature and Einstein tensors are as in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. The local density identity is

$$\delta((R-2\Lambda)w)=w(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab})q^{ab}+\partial_a(wV^a).$$

Fix constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Regard these as formal coefficients; their physical interpretation and units are not assumptions of this mathematical lemma. For smooth metric variations with compact support in the interior, at fixed bundle connection and fixed matter fields, consider the action difference

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}\int_MF_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+S_m,$$

where noncompact action values are used only through compactly supported differences, $F$ is the curvature of a fixed smooth bundle connection, and $S_m$ has Hilbert tensor $T^m$ in the convention of [[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]. Let $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ be the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor supplied by the compact Maxwell variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]], and set $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. Then for every compactly supported inverse-metric variation $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$,

$$\delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M\left(G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})\right)q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently, stationarity under all such metric variations is equivalent to

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}).$$

Any tensor fields satisfying this equation necessarily have $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})=0$ because $\Lambda$ is constant. This is a compatibility condition, not a claim that the coupled field equations have a solution or that matter and Maxwell equations follow from metric stationarity.

For dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates one may assign $[R]=[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T^m]=[T^{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Then every action term has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$ and $\kappa_E T$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. These are formal assignments only; the lemma assumes no measured parameter value or physical field law.

items.title: Classical complex-scalar connection derivative and action
items.design_state: Complete conditional definition authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Set $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with multiplication. A **smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle** is a smooth manifold $P$ with a smooth surjective submersion $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth right $U(1)$ action, and smooth local equivariant product charts $\pi^{-1}(U_i)\cong U_i\times U(1)$; the action is free and transitive on each fibre. This is the smooth version of the right-action convention in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]. A **principal connection** on $P$ is a smooth distribution $H\subseteq TP$ with $T_pP=\ker(d\pi_p)\oplus H_p$ and $dR_z(H_p)=H_{pz}$. Equivalently, it is a smooth real one-form $\omega$ on $P$ that is right-invariant and satisfies $\omega(\zeta_P)=1$, where $\zeta_P(p):=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{0}p\cdot e^{it}$; then $H=\ker\omega$. Choose a fixed smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle with a principal connection $\omega$. In a smooth trivialization $\tau_i:P|_{U_i}\to U_i\times U(1)$, set $\sigma_i(x):=\tau_i^{-1}(x,1)$ and $a_i:=\sigma_i^*\omega$. Choose the normalized local data $(U_i,g_{ij},a_i;\kappa_0)$ as in [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]; the potentials used below are their rescalings $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$. On any overlap neighborhood admitting a smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$, write $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$. Use the dual representation $\rho_k(z):=z^{-k}$ and define charged scalar representatives by the global transition rule $\varphi_j=g_{ij}^{k}\varphi_i$, equivalently $e^{ikf_{ij}}\varphi_i$ on each phase-lift neighborhood; the connection rule there is

$$A_j=A_i+\kappa_0\,df_{ij}.$$

Here $\kappa_0>0$ is the chosen circle normalization with $[\kappa_0]=\mathrm{Wb}$, $k\in\mathbb Z$ is the representation weight, and $\lambda:=k/\kappa_0$ has units $\mathrm{Wb}^{-1}$. Because $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ and $k$ is an integer, the maps $g_{ij}^{k}$ satisfy the scalar transition cocycle. A charged scalar is a family of smooth local functions $\varphi_i$ satisfying this rule; all phase-lift calculations below are local, and no global phase lift is assumed. The constant $c>0$ is the length-to-time conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with units $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Define $F|_{U_i}:=dA_i$; the transition law gives $dA_j=dA_i$, so $F$ is a global curvature two-form. In a global real-potential model on a trivial bundle, one may instead take a global $A$ and any real $\lambda$; no charge quantization is imposed there.

In a local trivialization define the gauge-covariant derivative and its lower-index one-form by

$$P_a:=(D\varphi)_a:=\partial_a\varphi_i-i\lambda A_{i,a}\varphi_i.$$

The transition laws give $P_{j,a}=e^{ikf_{ij}}P_{i,a}$, since $\lambda\kappa_0=k$. For any charged covector $Q_b$ with the same phase transition, define the gauge- and metric-covariant derivative by $D_aQ_b:=\nabla_aQ_b-i\lambda A_aQ_b$ in a local trivialization; for a charged scalar $\eta$, set $D_a\eta:=\partial_a\eta-i\lambda A_a\eta$. Conjugate fields use the opposite gauge sign. Thus $D_aP_b$ is a well-defined charged covariant two-tensor, and $D_aP^a:=g^{ab}D_aP_b$. Consequently $|\varphi|^2$ and $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ are global scalar fields. Let $V:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth on an open set $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the range of $|\varphi|^2$, write $V'$ for its ordinary real derivative, and choose a positive normalization constant $K_\varphi>0$.

The kinetic scalar $g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b$ is real because its complex conjugate equals itself by symmetry of $g^{ab}$. Put

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad S_\varphi:=-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}\int_M L_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

For SI dimensional bookkeeping in length coordinates, take $[\varphi]=1$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[P_a]=\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[V]=\mathrm m^{-2}$, and $[K_\varphi]=\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-1}$; then $S_\varphi$ has units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$. These are formal dimensional assignments, not measured values or physical postulates. On noncompact $M$, the integral is used when finite; otherwise only differences between configurations agreeing outside a compact set are defined, so every variation below is a compactly supported integral.

Allowed first variations are compactly supported smooth complex-section variations $\delta\varphi$, compactly supported real global one-form variations $\alpha=\delta A$ added to every local $A_i$ (so the same bundle transition functions are retained), and compactly supported symmetric inverse-metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$. The formula defines a classical mathematical functional; it asserts no quantum interpretation, value of $\hbar$, or material-response model.

items.title: Classical charged-scalar action, current and stress variation
items.design_state: Complete conditional lemma authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Use the scalar functional of [[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]] on a fixed smooth bundle sector, with $K_\varphi>0$, real $\lambda$, real smooth $V$, and smooth $\varphi,A,g$. Write $P_a:=D_a\varphi$ and define the gauge- and metric-covariant derivative of its one-form by

$$D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b,$$

with the conjugate derivative using $+i\lambda A_a$. For compactly supported variations, define

$$E_\varphi:=D_aP^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\,\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi.$$

Then the scalar-field variation is $\delta_\varphi S_\varphi=\frac{K_\varphi}{c}\operatorname{Re}\int_M\overline{\delta\varphi}\,E_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g$; stationarity in every compactly supported complex scalar direction is equivalent to $E_\varphi=0$. The connection and inverse-metric variations are

$$\delta_A S_\varphi=\frac1c\int_Mj^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad \delta_gS_\varphi=-\frac1{2c}\int_MT^\varphi_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

The following off-shell identities also hold:

$$\nabla_a j^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi E_\varphi),\qquad \nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_\varphi}P_b)+F_{ba}j^a.$$

In particular, the matter equation $E_\varphi=0$ implies current conservation and the exact Lorentz-force exchange identity $\nabla_a(T^\varphi)^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c$. No coupled Einstein–Maxwell solution or empirical matter model is asserted.

Under the formal SI assignments of [[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]], $j^a$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ and $T^\varphi$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$; this dimensional check is not an empirical claim.

items.design_state: Complete conditional lemma authored; current M02/M03 suppliers used at inspected draft statements. Seven declared M01 typed replacement item carriers remain absent and their inherited source closure is open; readiness escalated.
items.statement:
Let $U$ be an oriented open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(U)$ and $j\in\Gamma(TU)$ be smooth, and let $\mu_0>0$. Assume

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,$$

with the sign convention of [[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. Define the Maxwell Hilbert tensor by the compact metric variation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-action-variation]],

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

Then

$$\nabla_aT_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}=-F^{bc}j_c.$$

All fields and derivatives are smooth on $U$. In length-coordinate SI bookkeeping, assign $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$; these are formal units and not observed values. No quadratic stress is assigned to singular point self-fields or distributional sources.

items.statement:
On $\mathbb R^4$ with $x^0=ct$, Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and trivial bundle, set $A=0$, $V(u)=m_s^2u$ with $m_s>0$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and

$$\varphi(t,\mathbf x)=C\exp(-i\omega t+i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x),$$

where $C\ne0$ is dimensionless, $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$ has units $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and $\omega:=c\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+m_s^2}>0$ has units $\mathrm s^{-1}$. For the scalar action of [[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]], this is an exact solution of the local background scalar equation, equivalently stationary under compactly supported scalar variations. The infinite-volume action value need not be finite; only the local equation and compactly supported variations are used. If the coupling $\lambda\ne0$, the same configuration has a nonzero derived current although $F=dA=0$, so it fails the sourced Maxwell equation of [[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]]. It is therefore a background scalar solution, not a solution of the coupled scalar–Maxwell system. No relation to $\hbar$ or empirical data is used.

items.statement:
Let $M$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with metric $g$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ and the curvature convention of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Take a smooth real
two-form $F$ on $U$. For each application, fix one explicitly named smooth
classical matter-model instance
$$\mathcal M=(\mathcal C_m,\mathcal E_m,\mathsf J_m,\mathsf T_m).$$
For each admitted pair $(g,F)$, $\mathcal C_m[g,F]$ is a specified set of
smooth matter-field configurations on $U$, including their field bundles and
regularity; $\mathcal E_m[g,F;\Psi]$ is the explicit system of equations and
constraints that defines the admissible configurations; and
$\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi]$ and $\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi]$ are specified maps from
those configurations to, respectively, smooth vector fields and smooth
symmetric covariant two-tensors on $U$. For an admissible configuration
$\Psi\in\mathcal C_m[g,F]$, set $j:=\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi]$ and
$T^m:=\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi]$. A consuming item must name the selected model and
state the exact field variables, equations, constraints, regularity, and
additional domain or initial-data hypotheses it uses. Those matter equations
and constraints are premises of that model instance; they are not supplied or
proved by this postulate. In particular, arbitrary independent smooth $j$ and
$T^m$ are not a matter-model instance merely because their types match.

There is also a named zero-matter instance $\mathcal M_0$: its configuration
set is the singleton $\{*\}$, it has no matter-field variables or additional
constraints, and $\mathsf J_0(*)=0$, $\mathsf T_0(*)=0$. Whenever a use sets
$j=0$ and $T^m=0$ without additional matter fields, it is this source-free
instance.

For an admissible $\Psi$, adopt $dF=0$ and
$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ under the adopted convention of
[[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]]. This equation-based postulate then adds the
gravitational field law below, independently of any matter action.

Define the Einstein tensor by $G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
-\tfrac12 Rg_{ab}$, using the curvature contractions of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], and define the smooth-field electromagnetic
stress tensor by

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

For constant cosmological parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and
$\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, adopt the additional equation-based gravitational
field law

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E\left(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}\right).$$

Here $c>0$, $G_N>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ have the SI roles and units fixed in
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]; in length coordinates, $G_{ab}$ and
$\Lambda g_{ab}$ have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ and $T^m$
have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $\kappa_E$ has units
$\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. The source-free and sourced Maxwell equations remain
smooth-field postulates: point or sheet sources, distribution-valued products,
material excitation laws, and a global potential are outside this scope.

This is an equation-based adoption. It does not assume or imply the existence
of a matter action and is not derived from an action principle. The sources give
formulations in their own conventions; they motivate comparison but do not
establish a physical law or a solution-existence theorem.

items.statement:
For the action-based Einstein–Maxwell branch, choose one actual smooth matter
configuration space $\mathcal C$ on the spacetime of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle
$\pi:P\to M$, and a real differentiable functional $S_m[g,\omega,\Psi]$ on
its declared domain, where $\Psi\in\mathcal C$ and $\omega$ is a smooth
principal connection on that fixed bundle. Use a supplied cover and fixed
transition data with normalized real local connection representatives $a_i$;
on phase-lift neighborhoods their convention is
$a_j=a_i+df_{ij}$ when $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$. With the fixed normalization
$\kappa_0>0$ of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], the local expression for $\omega$
in a circle coordinate $z\in U(1)$ is $-iz^{-1}dz+a_i$. Define the physical local
potentials $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$. They obey
$A_j=A_i+\kappa_0df_{ij}$, and their local exterior derivatives patch to the
global physical curvature $F$, with $F|_{U_i}=dA_i=\kappa_0da_i$ and
$dF=0$. A global real potential is not assumed. The field class, transition
data, gauge action, matter equations, and compact variation class must be
specified for the chosen matter model.

More precisely, use the matter-field and differentiability definitions in
[[lem-emg-matter-noether-exchange]]: supply a smooth finite-dimensional
fiber bundle $E\to M$, take $\mathcal C=\Gamma^\infty(E)$, and specify a
real functional domain $\mathcal D$ of metric, fixed-sector connection and
section triples. Compact variations are jointly smooth curves in
$\mathcal D$ fixed off a common compact set. Require the freezing of any
two components to remain admissible, admit every compact metric and
connection direction, and require the derivative to depend real-linearly
only on the three tangent directions and to split into the three partial
variations. For each compact real gauge path and each horizontal-lifted
compact base flow, supply the jointly smooth matter-bundle
diffeomorphisms, their inverses on a common interval, and the admissible
transported sections specified in that lemma. These are part of the selected
model data; an arbitrary section bundle has no such transport by default.

If the selected matter model is given by a global physical potential
$A\in\Omega^1(M)$, use the trivial principal bundle $P=M\times U(1)$ with its
global trivialization and normalized representative $a=A/\kappa_0$; its
principal connection is locally $-iz^{-1}dz+a$. This is the trivial-bundle
global-potential branch, and the model may admit any real coupling when its
gauge transformations are specified by compactly supported real lifts. A
nontrivial bundle sector instead uses the stated local transition data and the
model's compatible matter-field transition rules.

The functional is invariant under compactly supported gauge transformations
of the fixed bundle sector and under orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms,
with the connection and matter fields transported together. In particular,
for every smooth compactly supported real gauge parameter $\chi$ with units
Wb, its group map is $g_\chi=e^{i\chi/\kappa_0}$; it acts by
$a_i\mapsto a_i+\kappa_0^{-1}d\chi$ and hence by
$A_i\mapsto A_i+d\chi$, together with the model's specified matter-field
transformation. For a compactly supported
vector field $\xi$, transport by the induced horizontal lift gives the
physical connection variation $\alpha_a=\xi^bF_{ba}$ used by
[[lem-emg-matter-noether-exchange]].

Adopt matter-field stationarity as part of this selected model:
$\delta_\Psi S_m=0$ for every admissible compactly supported matter variation.
For compactly supported inverse-metric variations $q^{ab}=\delta g^{ab}$ and
fixed-sector compact physical connection variations $\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$,
vary the local potentials by $A_i(s)=A_i+s\alpha|_{U_i}$, equivalently the
normalized representatives by $a_i(s)=a_i+s\kappa_0^{-1}\alpha|_{U_i}$.
The transition data remain fixed, this is a variation of the same bundle
connection sector, and $\delta F=d\alpha$. Require the remaining first
variation to have the form

$$\delta S_m=-\frac1{2c}\int_M T^m_{ab}q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g +\frac1c\int_M j^a\alpha_a\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, the Hilbert
stress-energy tensor in the convention of
[[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]], and $j$ is a smooth vector current.
Here $\alpha$ is the physical-potential variation, not the normalized
representative variation; the factor $\kappa_0^{-1}$ above makes the two
conventions explicit. These normalization, connection-variation, and
invariance hypotheses are exactly the formulation interface used by
[[lem-emg-matter-noether-exchange]]. That conditional mathematical result does
not assert that such an action exists for arbitrary proposed matter.

This postulate selects a differentiable action branch and its variation
conventions. It does not determine a unique action, assert a local or global
solution of its Euler–Lagrange equations, extend the model to singular sources,
or establish empirical validity. The separate equation-based model does not
depend on this action assumption.

items.statement:
Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, curvature
convention and SI constants of [[def-emg-geometry-units]] and
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Choose the actual matter functional
$S_m[g,\omega,\Psi]$ and its fixed smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle
$\pi:P\to M$ from [[post-emg-selected-matter-action]]. In its fixed normalized
connection sector, the local representatives are $a_i$, the physical local
potentials are $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$, and their globally defined physical curvature
satisfies $F|_{U_i}=dA_i=\kappa_0da_i$ and $dF=0$. A global real potential is
not required. Write $R:=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ for the scalar
curvature of the metric-selected connection, with the curvature convention
of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. For configurations where the action is
finite, or for compactly supported action differences on a noncompact
manifold, adopt

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}[g,\omega,\Psi] =\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g -\frac1{4\mu_0c}\int_M F_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g +S_m[g,\omega,\Psi].$$

Adopt that a configuration is dynamically admissible in this branch exactly
when the first variation of this total action vanishes independently for
every smooth compactly supported symmetric inverse-metric variation, every
smooth compactly supported fixed-sector physical connection variation
$\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$, and every admissible compactly supported matter-field
variation. The connection variation changes $A_i$ by $\alpha|_{U_i}$,
equivalently changes $a_i$ by $\kappa_0^{-1}\alpha|_{U_i}$, while leaving the
bundle and transition data fixed; thus $\delta F=d\alpha$. If $M$ has a
physical boundary, only variations vanishing on a neighbourhood of that
boundary are included. This makes no claim about a Gibbons–Hawking–York or
other boundary action.

The earlier postulate [[post-em-stationary-action-model]] concerns its stated
flat electromagnetic and prescribed-potential particle sectors. It supplies
no unified matter–gravity action or coupled-solution theorem; the functional
above is an additional, explicitly adopted model. An equation-based
Einstein–Maxwell formulation is a separate alternative, not a premise of this
action branch.

All displayed coefficients are model parameters with the units and
interpretations in [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Compact support is essential:
the Einstein–Hilbert and Maxwell integrations by parts have boundary terms in
general. The postulate asserts neither that its stationary configurations exist
nor that the action describes nature.

items.title: Einstein–Maxwell equations from compact action stationarity
items.physical_scope: Conditional equivalence between compact interior stationarity of the adopted smooth fixed-sector action and its metric, connection, and selected matter Euler–Lagrange equations. It asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity improvement, empirical validity, or boundary variational principle.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §3.2.5, PDF pp. 120–124 (printed pp. 113–117), Maxwell action variation; §4.1, PDF pp. 148–151 (printed pp. 141–144), Einstein–Hilbert variation; §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), stress conventions. The SI coefficients and compact-variation hypotheses are explicit here.

references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.54)–(4.72), PDF pp. 120–125, metric action variation and matter coupling. The assigned equations use the local SI and signature conventions.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g)$, the fixed smooth connection sector, the constants $c,G_N,\mu_0>0$,
constant $\Lambda$, and the selected matter functional $S_m$ be exactly those
of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]]. Write $F$ for the connection curvature,
$j$ and $T^m$ for the current and Hilbert tensor in the selected matter
variation, and define
$G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Rg_{ab}$ using the Ricci and scalar
curvature contractions in the convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Also
set

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad \kappa_E:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}.$$

The homogeneous identity $dF=0$ holds because $F$ is the curvature of the
smooth connection in the fixed sector. The adopted configuration is stationary
under every admissible compactly supported metric, connection, and matter
variation if and only if all of the following hold:

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}),\qquad \delta_\Psi S_m[\zeta]=0\ \text{for every admissible compactly supported }\zeta.$$

The last clause is the selected matter model's Euler–Lagrange condition; an
explicit local matter equation cannot be given until $S_m$ is specified.
These are model deductions from the adopted action and smooth compact
variation hypotheses, not evidence that a coupled solution exists or that the
model describes nature.

items.title: Electromagnetic and matter stress exchange
items.physical_scope: Local stress exchange on smooth solutions of the adopted vacuum Maxwell system and one selected invariant matter action. The result is conditional on the matter fields being on shell. It asserts no global gravitational energy, Killing charge without symmetry and flux hypotheses, or coupled PDE solution.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.2–§4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), Hilbert stress, Maxwell stress, and diffeomorphism identity.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, electromagnetic stress; Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147, on-shell diffeomorphism identity.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with
signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Restrict to $U$ the
fixed smooth principal $U(1)$ bundle and connection selected in
[[post-emg-selected-matter-action]]. In its normalized local representatives
$a_i$, the physical local potentials are $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$; their global
physical curvature satisfies $F|_{U_i}=dA_i=\kappa_0da_i$ and $dF=0$. The
$F$ and $j$ below are the curvature and current of that same connection and
selected action. Let $F$ and $j$ be smooth, and assume
the adopted Maxwell equations $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ of
[[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]]. Let $S_m$ be the selected smooth invariant
matter functional of [[post-emg-selected-matter-action]], satisfying the
section-bundle, real functional-domain, compact-variation splitting, and
supplied smooth pathwise-transport hypotheses of
[[lem-emg-matter-noether-exchange]] for this same connection. Suppose its
matter fields are on shell. Define $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ by the local Maxwell
variation and $T^m$ by the Hilbert variation of $S_m$. Then

$$\nabla_a T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}=-F^{bc}j_c,\qquad \nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c,\qquad \nabla_a(T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}+T_m^{ab})=0.$$

Use the curvature convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]] and define the
scalar curvature by $R:=S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ and the
Einstein tensor by $G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Rg_{ab}$. Set
$\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4>0$ using the SI constants of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]. If, in addition, the pointwise Einstein equation
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab})$$
holds with constant $\Lambda$, the contracted Bianchi identity shows that
the total conservation law is its necessary source-compatibility condition.
This local identity is not a universal gravitational energy statement and
does not imply existence of a solution.

items.title: Restricted smooth charged-dust model
items.physical_scope: A restricted smooth continuum model with constant mass and charge parameters, positive proper number density, unit-normalized timelike velocity, number continuity, and the adopted Lorentz-force equation. It excludes caustics, singular particles and any coupled PDE existence claim.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §§4.5.2–4.5.4, PDF pp. 190–195 (printed pp. 183–188), Hilbert stress and continuum matter examples; the local dust closure and its validity limits are stated here.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147, matter stress and diffeomorphism context; no dust action is inferred.

items.statement:
Let $U$ be an open subset of the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold and use the metric, units, and electromagnetic conventions of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]. A restricted smooth charged-dust configuration
consists of constants $m>0$ in kilograms and $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs, a
smooth future-directed vector field $U^a$ with $g_{ab}U^aU^b=-c^2$, and a
smooth scalar field $\nu:U\to(0,\infty)$. Put $u^a:=U^a/c$, so
$g_{ab}u^au^b=-1$, and at each $x\in U$ define its local rest space by
$H_x:=\{v\in T_xM:g_x(v,u_x)=0\}$. The restriction $\gamma_x:=g_x|_{H_x}$
is a positive-definite inner product. In any basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $H_x$
with linear coordinates $(y^1,y^2,y^3)$, its proper 3-volume density is
$dV_{\mathrm{rest}}=\sqrt{\det(\gamma_x(e_i,e_j))}\,|dy^1dy^2dy^3|$;
this density is independent of the chosen basis. The scalar $\nu(x)$ is the
proper number density measured in this rest space: the local particle-number
measure has density $\nu\,dV_{\mathrm{rest}}$. Thus $[\nu]=\mathrm{m^{-3}}$.
Define the rest-space projector $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+U^aU_b/c^2$.
The associated four-current and matter stress tensor are

$$j^a:=q\nu U^a,\qquad T_m^{ab}:=m\nu U^aU^b.$$

Their length-coordinate SI units are $[U^a]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$,
$[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and $[T_m^{ab}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. The
single-velocity condition means that at every event in the model domain all
dust matter there is assigned the same vector $U_x$; a state with distinct
future unit timelike velocities at one event is outside this model. In this
item, a caustic or multistream breakdown is a point where the material
description can no longer be represented by smooth fields $\nu,U$ with
$0<\nu<\infty$ and one such velocity. The model domain is restricted to open
regions excluding those breakdown points. This is a scope convention, not a
claim that caustics are avoided or that the fields exist globally. As the
continuum closure of this model, adopt on the smooth solution domain

$$\nabla_a(\nu U^a)=0,\qquad m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U),$$

where $\nabla_UU^a:=U^b\nabla_bU^a$ and
$g(F^\sharp(v),w)=F(w,v)$, as in the external-charge convention of
[[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. The latter supplies
test-body sign and normalization context only; it proves neither the
continuum number equation nor a continuum or coupled PDE evolution law.

This definition applies only while $\nu,U,F,g$ remain smooth and the
single-velocity dust description is valid. It makes no claim that such
solutions exist globally or avoid caustics, and it does not assign a
distributional stress tensor to point particles.

items.title: Charged-dust current and stress balance
items.physical_scope: A local deduction for smooth charged-dust fields satisfying the independently adopted number-continuity and Lorentz-force equations. It does not construct dust solutions, prove avoidance of caustics, or extend to singular particles.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §§4.5.2–4.5.4, PDF pp. 190–195 (printed pp. 183–188), stress and continuum-matter conventions. The dust product calculation is carried out under the local adopted closure.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147, covariant stress-balance context. No matter-action existence is assumed in this proof.

items.statement:
For the smooth charged-dust model of [[def-emg-charged-dust-model]], with
constant $m>0$ and $q$, current $j^a=q\nu U^a$, and stress
$T_m^{ab}=m\nu U^aU^b$, every configuration satisfying its adopted closure
obeys

$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^{bc}j_c.$$

This is a model deduction from the continuum equations, not a consequence of
the external test-particle theorem and not a claim that a smooth continuum
solution exists.

items.title: Specified classical charged complex-scalar model
items.physical_scope: One classical smooth charged complex-scalar matter branch using the stated gauge-covariant functional and SI bookkeeping. It makes no quantum, statistical, material-response, empirical, or coupled-PDE existence claim.

references.title: David Tong, Gauge Theory, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §2.5.2, PDF pp. 89–91 (printed pp. 78–80), Abelian gauge field coupled to a complex scalar through a covariant derivative. Quantum and material claims are not adopted.

references.locator: §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), scalar matter action and Hilbert stress in curved spacetime.

items.statement:
On the smooth Lorentzian geometry and SI convention of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], choose a fixed smooth bundle sector and the
classical charged-scalar functional $S_\varphi$ of
[[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]]. A configuration of this model is a
smooth complex scalar section $\varphi$ and the smooth connection and metric
fields in that definition. In the action branch, take this actual functional
as the selected matter action $S_m:=S_\varphi$, with the same fixed-sector
compact variations. The scalar is classical; the dimensionless field
normalization, the positive coefficient $K_\varphi$, the smooth real
potential $V$, and the permitted coupling $\lambda$ are exactly those of
[[def-emg-charged-scalar-functional]].

In its circle-bundle branch, $\lambda\kappa_0=k\in\mathbb Z$ for the selected
representation; in the separate trivial real-potential branch, $\lambda$ may
be any real number. No quantum rest-mass identification, material-response
claim, or existence theorem for the coupled equations is part of this
definition.

items.title: Field equations and balances of the selected scalar coupling
items.physical_scope: Conditional equations for one smooth classical charged-scalar functional coupled to the adopted smooth Einstein–Maxwell action. Current and stress balances hold on the scalar matter equation. No quantum interpretation, empirical matter claim, or coupled PDE solution is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Gauge Theory, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §2.5.2, PDF pp. 89–91 (printed pp. 78–80), Abelian charged-scalar action and covariant derivative. The local current, stress, and balance identities are derived in the mathematical supplier.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §4.1, PDF pp. 148–151 (printed pp. 141–144), metric variation; §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), scalar and Maxwell stress tensors.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, stress variation; Ch. 5, equations (5.33)–(5.38), PDF pp. 143–147, matter-on-shell diffeomorphism identity.

items.statement:
Use the specified model of [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-model]] and the
adopted total action of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]]. Write
$P_a:=D_a\varphi$, $L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2)$ and

$$E_\varphi:=D_aP^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\,\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\varphi}P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b) -\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi.$$

For smooth fields and the compact fixed-sector variations, stationarity of
the selected scalar matter action in every scalar direction is equivalent to
$E_\varphi=0$. Stationarity of the full action in all fields then gives

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab}),$$

with $dF=0$ for the connection curvature. On the scalar matter equation,

$$\nabla_a j^a=0,\qquad \nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=F_{ba}j^a.$$

These are conditional field equations and local balance identities for the
specified classical branch. They assert neither existence of a smooth
solution nor empirical or quantum validity.

row.title: Independent equation-based Einstein–Maxwell coupling — Examples

items.title: Background scalar wave versus coupled source equations
items.physical_scope: Exact smooth plane-wave calculations in the specified classical scalar model on a flat background. They distinguish a matter equation solution from a solution of the coupled equations and make no empirical or quantum claim.

references.title: David Tong, Gauge Theory, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §2.5.2, PDF pp. 89–91 (printed pp. 78–80), classical complex scalar and gauge-covariant derivative.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), scalar-field stress convention; the displayed plane wave is checked locally.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, metric stress convention; the conditional calculation is explicit here.

items.statement:
Take the trivial global-potential branch of the scalar model on
$M=\mathbb R^4$ with global coordinates $(x^0,\mathbf x)$, where
$x^0=ct$ and $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3$, and Minkowski metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use the trivial principal bundle
$P=M\times U(1)$ with its product connection, so the global physical
potential is $A=0$, and take $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$.
Set
$V(u)=m_s^2u$, where $m_s>0$ is a classical inverse-length parameter
$[\mathrm{m}^{-1}]$, not a rest mass. Let $C\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ be
dimensionless and let $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$ have components in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. Define the angular frequency
$\omega:=c\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+m_s^2}$, with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. The smooth field
$\varphi=C\exp(-i\omega t+i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x)$ solves the scalar
equation for every allowed value of $\lambda$, because $A=0$ makes
$D_a=\partial_a$. Its current, however, depends on $\lambda$. The two cases
below show why a solution of the scalar equation on a prescribed background
need not solve the coupled Einstein–Maxwell system.

items.title: A flat Maxwell field need not solve the coupled Einstein equations
items.physical_scope: A smooth exact counterexample showing that a source-free Maxwell solution on a prescribed flat background need not satisfy the coupled action-based Einstein equation. It uses no empirical data or singular field.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §3.2.5, PDF pp. 120–124 (printed pp. 113–117), curved Maxwell equations; §4.5.3, PDF pp. 190–193 (printed pp. 183–186), electromagnetic Hilbert stress.
