items.statement:
Adopt the equation-based Einstein-Maxwell field postulate
[[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] and the smooth material closure of
[[post-emg-strict-charged-fluid-model]], with the SI, signature, and coordinate
conventions of [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Thus the spacetime field equations
are $dF=0$, $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, and
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa(T_{m,ab}+T_{\mathrm{EM},ab}),\qquad \kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4,$$
while the fluid contributes exactly its adopted $T_m,j$ and material balance
equations. No matter action is assumed.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice.
Let $p=p(\epsilon)$ be smooth on an open interval $J$, and let
$K_\epsilon\Subset J$ be a compact interval containing the initial density
values, on which $\epsilon+p(\epsilon)>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$. Take
$\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary, and let
$\mathfrak n$ be its future unit normal. Let $h$ be a Riemannian metric and
let $K\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*\Sigma)$ use the second fundamental
form convention
$$K(X,Y):=g(\nabla_X\mathfrak n,Y).$$
The initial normal bundle is
$\mathcal V:=\mathbb R\mathfrak n\oplus T\Sigma$ with
$$g_0(a\mathfrak n+X,b\mathfrak n+Y):=-ab+h(X,Y).$$
Let $\epsilon_0,Z_0$ be smooth scalar fields, $u_0$ a smooth future unit
timelike section of $\mathcal V$ satisfying $g_0(u_0,u_0)=-1$, and $e,b$
smooth spatial vector fields
representing $E/c$ and $B$ in an oriented orthonormal frame. Their units are
J m$^{-3}$, C, dimensionless, and tesla, respectively; $K$ has units m$^{-1}$.
The components of the smooth initial two-form $F_0$ are defined in every
positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame $(\mathsf e_i)$ by
$$e_i=F_0(\mathsf e_i,\mathfrak n),\qquad b_i=\tfrac12\varepsilon_i{}^{jk}F_0(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k), \qquad \varepsilon_{123}=1.$$
This fixes all six independent components of $F_0$. Set
$j_0=cN(\epsilon_0)Z_0u_0$ and $T_0=T_{m,0}+T_{\mathrm{EM},0}$ from the
adopted model.

Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$,
$\tau:=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$,
$|K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$,
$(\operatorname{div}_hK)_j:=h^{ik}(D_iK)_{kj}$, and $R(h)$ for the scalar
curvature of $h$. Assume the complete Einstein and sourced Maxwell initial
constraints
$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(\mathfrak n,\mathfrak n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)-D_X\tau=\kappa T_0(\mathfrak n,X)$$
for every tangent vector $X$, and
$$\operatorname{div}_h e=-\mu_0g_0(j_0,\mathfrak n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_h b=0.$$

Then the adopted equation-based fluid model has the following conditional
local developments.

**(a) Torus Sobolev branch.** If
$\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ with the periodic
Sobolev spaces of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]], assigning each
spatial period length $2\pi\,\mathrm m$ in the length-coordinate convention of
[F6]. Assume $s\ge5$ is an integer, $h\in H^{s+1}$ and
$K,e,b,\epsilon_0,u_0,Z_0\in H^s$, with the same strict compact
admissibility. Then there is $T>0$ and a solution on
$(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3$ in the harmonic gauge of
[[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], relative to the fixed
background used by [[thm-emg-local-charged-barotropic-development]]. In
periodic charts,
$g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C^0H^s$,
$\partial_tg\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$, and
$F,\epsilon,u,Z\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$. The equations hold
classically, and the reduced solution is unique on common intervals with common
compact admissible bounds.

**(b) Smooth geometric branch.** For smooth data on any $\Sigma$ above, there
is a smooth time-oriented solution on an open variable-width neighborhood of
$\{0\}\times\Sigma$, inducing exactly $(h,K,F_0,\epsilon_0,u_0,Z_0)$. It is
unique near the initial surface up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry matching $F,\epsilon,u,Z$. No uniform time width for noncompact
$\Sigma$, global existence, shock continuation, vacuum/free-boundary solution,
or empirical validity is asserted.

This is a model deduction. It does not assert that the postulates describe
nature.

items.statement:
Choose $w\in(0,1)$, a constant $H>0$ with units m$^{-1}$, and $N_*>0$ with
units m$^{-3}$. Use the Einstein coupling
$\kappa=\kappa_E=8\pi G_N/c^4>0$ from [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with units
m J$^{-1}$. Set
$$J=(0,\infty),\qquad \epsilon_*:=\frac{3H^2}{\kappa},\qquad p(\epsilon):=w\epsilon,\qquad \Lambda:=0.$$
Then $\epsilon_*>0$ has units J m$^{-3}$. Adopt the linear EOS on all of
$J$, use $\epsilon_*$ as the normalization point in the definition of $N$,
and set the advected charge-per-particle field to $Z\equiv0$.

On $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$, assign the
spatial period length $2\pi\,\mathrm m$ in the length-coordinate convention of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], and use the standard smooth quotient structure and
orientation. Take the flat metric $h=\delta$,
prescribe $K=Hh$, set the constant energy density $\epsilon_0=\epsilon_*$,
take fluid velocity $u_0=\mathfrak n$, and set $e=b=0$. The slice is compact
and has no boundary. The equation of state is strict on the open density interval, the
current vanishes, and the Einstein and Maxwell constraints hold exactly. By
the local theorem, these data admit a smooth local development, conditional
on $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, Dependent Choice, the adopted model and the exact mathematical hypotheses used by [[pthm-emg-local-charged-fluid-model]]. This example is a model
calculation, not an observation.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, and let $i:\Sigma\to M$ be a smooth
spacelike embedding. Suppose a smooth future unit normal field $n$ along
$i(\Sigma)$ is supplied. For every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open
neighborhood $U_p\subseteq\Sigma$, a number $\epsilon_p>0$, and an open
$V_p\subseteq M$ such that the restricted map
$\Phi_p:(-\epsilon_p,\epsilon_p)\times U_p\to V_p$ given by

$$\Phi_p(t,x)=\gamma_{i(x),n_{i(x)}}(t)$$

is a diffeomorphism, where $\gamma_{q,v}$ is the maximal affinely
parameterized metric geodesic with initial data $(q,v)$. At its center,

$$d(\Phi_p)_{(0,p)}(a\partial_t+X)=a n_{i(p)}+d i_p(X).$$

The neighborhoods and time widths may depend on $p$; no globally injective
normal exponential map or uniform width is asserted.

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth
time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, and let
$i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be a smooth spacelike Cauchy embedding. If
$F,\bar F\in\Omega^2(M)$ are smooth closed two-forms with
$i^*F=i^*\bar F$, then $F-\bar F$ is exact: there is a smooth
$\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ such that $d\alpha=F-\bar F$.

Here a closed form has zero exterior derivative, and exactness means being the
exterior derivative of a globally defined smooth form, as in
[[def-de-rham-cohomology]].

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty
smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric
$h$, smooth symmetric covariant tensor $K$, and smooth tangent vector fields
$e,b$. Fix $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and use the
signature, SI conventions, and electromagnetic stress tensor of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]] and [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]].
Assume $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ satisfies all four source-free constraints of
[[def-emg-constrained-electrovacuum-data]].

In the periodic case $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi L_0}$ with fixed $L_0>0$ in metres, for an integer $s\ge5$,
also consider smooth data with $h\in H^{s+1}$, $K,e,b\in H^s$, and the
uniform lower eigenvalue bound $h\ge c_0I$ for some $c_0>0$ specified by
[[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Here the length-frame metric and curvature arrays and the orthonormal electric/magnetic arrays are composed with $[\theta]\mapsto[L_0\theta]$ for Sobolev norms on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$; geometric spatial derivatives are $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$. On its common local interval the
field-strength solution has
$g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C^0H^s$,
$\partial_tg\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$, and
$F\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$, with the time coordinate measured in
length units as in [[def-emg-geometry-units]].

For the magnetic data define the smooth two-form
$\beta_b(X,Y):=\operatorname{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$. Assume the following explicit
initial bundle compatibility: there are a countable open cover $(U_i)$ of
$\Sigma$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth local
real one-forms $a_i$, and one constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require
$g_{ii}=1$, $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on triple overlaps, and
$a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$ on every overlap, where
$\lambda(g)=-i g^{-1}dg$; also require $\kappa_0\,da_i=\beta_b$ on $U_i$.
Here $\kappa_0$
has units weber and the normalized local forms have the units in
[[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. This is the fixed
normalized circle-bundle sector of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]];
it imposes no global real-valued potential and no condition on the independent
electric data beyond the stated constraints.

In the action model of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]], choose the
zero-matter branch: the matter configuration space is a singleton and
$S_m\equiv0$, so its current and Hilbert tensor vanish. Then there is a smooth
time-oriented local development of the source-free system on a neighborhood
of the entire initial surface, after restriction to a possibly variable-width
globally hyperbolic Cauchy neighborhood. Its electromagnetic two-form is the
curvature of a smooth connection in the supplied normalized circle-bundle
sector, and its initial electric and magnetic fields are exactly $e,b$.
Any two such developments are related near the initial surface by a
data-fixing, time-orientation-preserving isometry carrying the metric and
two-form to one another. This is a conditional model deduction; it asserts
neither physical validity, a uniform positive time width for noncompact
$\Sigma$, global-time existence, nor a maximal-development result.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty
connected smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary, with smooth
Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$, and smooth tangent vector
fields $e,b$. Fix $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and the SI
Lorentzian conventions of [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Assume the four
constraints of [[def-emg-constrained-electrovacuum-data]]. Define
$\beta_b(X,Y)=\operatorname{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$, and supply a countable cover
$(U_i)$, transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, local real one-forms
$a_i$, and $\kappa_0>0$ satisfying $g_{ii}=1$, $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$,
$a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$, and $\kappa_0 da_i=\beta_b$, where
$\lambda(g)=-i g^{-1}dg$. These are the normalized local data of
[[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] restricted to the initial slice.
Adopt the zero-matter action branch
$S_m\equiv0$ of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]].

Then there is a smooth connected time-oriented globally hyperbolic
development $(M_{\max},g_{\max},F_{\max},i_{\max})$ of the source-free
[[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]] with the complete data $(h,K,e,b)$.
The two-form $F_{\max}=\kappa_0 f_{\max}$ is the physical curvature of a
smooth connection in the bundle sector obtained by transporting the supplied
initial sector over a Cauchy product. Here $f_{\max}\in\Omega^2(M_{\max})$
is its normalized curvature, locally $f_{\max}=da_i$; the supplied constant
$\kappa_0>0$ has units Wb, so multiplication gives the SI physical curvature.
Every other smooth globally hyperbolic development with the same complete data
for which the adopted action is stationary embeds into this one by a
time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding that fixes $\Sigma$ and carries
$F$ to $F_{\max}$. Any two maximal developments are related by exactly one
data-fixing isometry of $(g,F)$. Maximality is within the smooth globally
hyperbolic solution class; it asserts no geodesic completeness, no maximality
among rough or non-globally-hyperbolic extensions, no global-in-time
regularity estimate, and no empirical validity. Here an affinely parametrized metric geodesic solves $\ddot x^a+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\dot x^b\dot x^c=0$ on an interval; maximality of that solution forbids extension to a strictly larger interval with the same affine parameter. Geodesic completeness means every maximal affine geodesic has parameter domain all of $\mathbb R$.

Let $L>0$ be the physical side length of
$\mathbb T^3_L=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, with length coordinates
$(X,Y,Z)$ and flat metric $h=dX^2+dY^2+dZ^2$. Give $\mathbb T^3_L$ the
orientation $dX\wedge dY\wedge dZ$. Fix the normalized circle-flux scale
$\kappa_0>0$ from [[def-emg-geometry-units]], and set
$$B_0:=\frac{2\pi\kappa_0}{L^2},\qquad H:=\sqrt{\frac{\kappa}{3\mu_0}}\,B_0.$$
Take $\Lambda=0$ and define $K=Hh$, $e=B_0\partial_Z$, and
$b=B_0\partial_Z$. The electric and magnetic observer fields are nonzero
and parallel in this initial state.

The magnetic two-form is
$\beta_b=B_0\,dX\wedge dY$. It is compatible with a nontrivial normalized
circle bundle, not just a globally defined potential: on the universal cover
$\mathbb R^3\times U(1)$, with $z\in U(1)$, use the connection one-form
$$\omega=-i z^{-1}dz+\frac{2\pi}{L^2}X\,dY.$$
Let the deck transformations be
$$T_X(X,Y,Z,z)=(X+L,Y,Z,e^{-2\pi iY/L}z),\quad T_Y(X,Y,Z,z)=(X,Y+L,Z,z),\quad T_Z(X,Y,Z,z)=(X,Y,Z+L,z).$$
They commute because $e^{-2\pi i(Y+L)/L}=e^{-2\pi iY/L}$. The one-form
$\omega$ is invariant under these identifications, so it descends to a
connection on the quotient bundle over $\mathbb T^3_L$. Its curvature is
$$d\omega=\frac{2\pi}{L^2}dX\wedge dY,$$
hence the physical curvature $\kappa_0d\omega$ is exactly $\beta_b$.

The diagram shows one fundamental square in the $X,Y$ directions. The
opposite vertical edges are glued with the displayed $U(1)$ transition; the
horizontal edges are glued without a fiber twist. It records the quotient
convention but is not used in the verification.

items.design_state: Definition and global real-potential system, smooth well-definedness, tensor types and SI dimensions authored. The actual batch-4 scalar functional and batch-6 electrovacuum convention suppliers remain unaccepted drafts.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with its metric-selected Levi–Civita connection and independent orientation as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and the curvature and Hodge conventions of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]] and [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. Fix $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and put $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$.

The **trivial-potential sector** consists of a global smooth real one-form $A\in\Omega^1(M)$ and a global smooth complex scalar field $\varphi\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb C)$. It defines the exact real two-form $F:=dA$ and the charged derivative

$$\pi_a:=(D\varphi)_a:=\nabla_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi,$$

where $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is an arbitrary fixed coupling. Define $D_a\pi_b:=\nabla_a\pi_b-i\lambda A_a\pi_b$, with the conjugate derivative using $+i\lambda A_a$, and $D_a\pi^a:=g^{ab}D_a\pi_b$. Let $\mathcal U\subset\mathbb R$ be open with $|\varphi|^2(M)\subset\mathcal U$, let $V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U;\mathbb R)$, and fix $K_\varphi>0$. Define

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{\pi_a}\pi_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad S_\varphi:=-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}\int_M L_\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g,$$

where on a noncompact $M$ the integral is used when finite and otherwise only compactly supported action differences are used. The scalar equation, current vector, and scalar stress tensor are

$$D_a\pi^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi=0,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi\pi^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\pi_a}\pi_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi.$$

Put

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T_{ab}:=T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab}.$$

The associated **classical charged-scalar Einstein–Maxwell system** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad D_a\pi^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi=0.$$

Here $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Rg_{ab}$; all indices are raised with $g^{-1}$. This is a definition of a mathematical system, not an adopted physical postulate or a claim about nature. It is restricted to a trivial real-potential sector: $F$ is exact, no nontrivial $U(1)$ bundle is included, and $\lambda$ is not quantized. The scalar is classical, and neither $K_\varphi$ nor $\lambda$ is tied to a Planck constant.

For formal SI bookkeeping in length coordinates, assign $[g_{ab}]=1$, $[x^a]=\mathrm m$, $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $[G_N]=\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $[\mu_0]=\mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}$, $[\Lambda]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-2}}$, $[\varphi]=1$, $[\lambda]=\mathrm{Wb^{-1}}$, $[\pi_a]=\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, $[V]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, and $[K_\varphi]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$. These give $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_{ab}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\kappa T_{ab}]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, and $[S_\varphi]=\mathrm{J\,s}$. They are dimensions, not measured values.

items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented four-manifold without boundary. Its smooth
structure is retained throughout. A **classical finite-regularity
trivial-potential configuration** consists of a time-oriented $C^3$
Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, a global real $C^2$ one-form
$A$, and a global complex $C^2$ scalar $\varphi$. Fix
$c,G_N,\mu_0,K_\varphi>0$, $\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and
$V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U;\mathbb R)$ for an open
$\mathcal U\subset\mathbb R$ containing $|\varphi|^2(M)$. Set
$\kappa_E=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The curvature sign, length-coordinate convention
$x^0=ct$, and SI assignments are those of
[[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]]; only these formulas and
conventions are imported, not that item's smooth-field restriction.

The Levi-Civita connection and curvature here are defined by their coordinate
formulas for this $C^3$ metric. Define

$$F_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,\qquad P_a:=\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi,$$

$$\mathcal D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b,\qquad E_\varphi:=g^{ab}\mathcal D_aP_b-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,$$

$$L_\varphi:=g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2),\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}L_\varphi,\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

Conjugate charged derivatives use the opposite gauge sign. All indices are
raised with $g^{-1}$. Thus $F,P$ are $C^1$, $j,T^\varphi,T^{\mathrm{EM}}$
are $C^1$, $E_\varphi$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}$ are continuous, and the
Einstein tensor $G$ is $C^1$. The **classical charged-scalar equations** are
the pointwise equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad E_\varphi=0,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab}).$$

Here $dF=0$ already follows from $F=dA$ with $A\in C^2$. These are equations
for the declared classical fields; they do not assert existence, smoothness
improvement, or a weaker distributional theory.

For a continuous compactly supported real top form $\omega$, define
$\mathcal I_M(\omega)$ by a finite smooth cutoff localization near its
support and the signed Riemann integrals of the resulting chart
coefficients, extended by zero. The construction and its independence are
proved below. For a complex top form extend $\mathcal I_M$ by integrating
its real and imaginary parts separately. For a configuration
$X=(g,A,\varphi)$ put

$$\mathscr L(X):=\left[\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}(R(g)-2\Lambda)-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}F_{ab}F^{ab}-\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}L_\varphi\right]\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

If $X_1=X_0$ outside a compact set, its **relative total action** is
$S(X_1;X_0):=\mathcal I_M(\mathscr L(X_1)-\mathscr L(X_0))$. The scalar
and Maxwell relative actions are defined by their respective summands. No
subtraction of divergent global integrals is intended. When the separate
global integrals are defined and finite, this agrees with their difference.

Allowed independent directions are smooth compactly supported symmetric
inverse-metric tensors $q^{ab}$, real one-forms $\alpha$, and complex scalars
$\eta$. Near zero parameter use

$$g_\varepsilon^{-1}=g^{-1}+\varepsilon q,\qquad A_\varepsilon=A+\varepsilon\alpha,\qquad\varphi_\varepsilon=\varphi+\varepsilon\eta.$$

The parameter interval is restricted to preserve signature, time orientation,
and the potential domain. Stationarity means that the derivative of the
relative total action vanishes for every such direction. These definitions
include the original smooth trivial-potential system as a subclass, with its
same action coefficients and tensors. They do not change the separate
nontrivial-circle-bundle formulation or impose an integer condition on the
real coupling $\lambda$.

Use the classical finite-regularity configuration, relative actions and compact
smooth directions of
[[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]]. In particular
the underlying manifold is smooth, $g\in C^3$, $A,\varphi\in C^2$,
$F=dA$, $P=\mathcal D\varphi$, and the constants and potential have exactly
that Definition's hypotheses. Then all compact first variations exist, and

$$\delta S=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\mathcal I_M\!\left(\left[G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa_E(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab})\right]q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g\right)+\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\mathcal I_M\!\left((\nabla_aF^{ab}+\mu_0j^b)\alpha_b\mathrm{vol}_g\right)+\frac{K_\varphi}{c}\operatorname{Re}\mathcal I_M\!\left(\overline\eta E_\varphi\mathrm{vol}_g\right).$$

The scalar and free Maxwell summands separately have first variations

$$\delta S_\varphi=-\frac{1}{2c}\mathcal I_M(T^\varphi_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g)+\frac1c\mathcal I_M(j^a\alpha_a\mathrm{vol}_g)+\frac{K_\varphi}{c}\operatorname{Re}\mathcal I_M(\overline\eta E_\varphi\mathrm{vol}_g),$$

$$\delta S_{\mathrm{EM}}=-\frac{1}{2c}\mathcal I_M(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}q^{ab}\mathrm{vol}_g)+\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\mathcal I_M((\nabla_aF^{ab})\alpha_b\mathrm{vol}_g).$$

Thus compact stationarity is equivalent to all the pointwise classical
charged-scalar equations in that Definition. The homogeneous equation
$dF=0$ holds identically in the global-potential domain.

Without assuming the Einstein, Maxwell or scalar field equations, one also
has the classical identities

$$\nabla_a j^a=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi E_\varphi),\qquad \nabla_a(T^\varphi)^a{}_b=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{E_\varphi}P_b)+F_{ba}j^a,$$

$$\nabla_a(T^{\mathrm{EM}})^a{}_b=\mu_0^{-1}F_{ba}\nabla_cF^{ca}.$$

Consequently the scalar equation implies current conservation, and the scalar
and sourced Maxwell equations together imply
$\nabla_a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}+T^\varphi)^a{}_b=0$ before any Einstein equation
is used. These conclusions are valid for the stated classical fields with
continuous coefficients; they claim no lower roughness threshold, smoothing,
physical adoption or coupled-solution existence.

items.title: Temporal-gauge first-order reduction of the charged scalar equation
items.design_state: Complete conditional scalar principal-block calculation authored, including the compatibility substitution that removes mixed time derivatives. The actual charged-system and symmetric-hyperbolic-definition suppliers retain their current draft or pending-precheck statuses.
items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ be a coordinate region with $x^0=s$ a length coordinate, and let $g$ be a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $U$. Write $g^{ab}$ for its inverse and $\Gamma^c{}_{ab}$ for its Levi–Civita coefficients. Assume throughout the region that

$$g^{00}<0,\qquad (g^{ij})_{i,j=1}^3\text{ is positive definite}.$$

Let $A_0=0$, let $A_i$ be real, let $F_{0i}$ be real, and let $\varphi$ be complex. Treat $\pi_0,\pi_i$ as independent complex variables, and set

$$D_a\pi_b:=\partial_a\pi_b-\Gamma^c{}_{ab}\pi_c-i\lambda A_a\pi_b,$$

where $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $D_a\pi^a:=g^{ab}D_a\pi_b$. The temporal-gauge scalar first-order system is

$$\partial_s\varphi=\pi_0,\qquad \partial_sA_i=F_{0i},$$

$$\partial_s\pi_i-\partial_i\pi_0=-i\lambda A_i\pi_0-i\lambda F_{0i}\varphi,\qquad D_a\pi^a=V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi.$$

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in the periodic coefficient convention of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]. Use the three spatial compatibility equations to eliminate $\partial_s\pi_i$ from the scalar divergence equation. Then multiply the resulting scalar row by $-1$ and the compatibility rows by $g^{ki}$. For the variable block $(\pi_0,\pi_i)$, the resulting principal matrices are

$$A^0=\begin{pmatrix}-g^{00}&0\\0&g^{ij}\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^k=\begin{pmatrix}-2g^{0k}&-g^{kj}\\-g^{ik}&0\end{pmatrix}\quad(k=1,2,3).$$

The matrices on the complex variables mean the same real matrices on each real and imaginary component. They are symmetric and $A^0$ is positive definite. The transport equations for $\varphi$ and $A_i$ add only identity time blocks and no spatial derivative blocks. All remaining coefficients depend smoothly on $(g,g^{-1},\partial g,A,F,\varphi,\pi)$ wherever the stated metric inequalities and the open domain of $V$ hold. Thus this scalar-potential reduction is symmetric hyperbolic in the coefficient sense of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]].

items.title: Charged-scalar compatibility, Maxwell constraints and Einstein gauge propagation
items.design_state: Complete conditional metric, scalar, potential, sourced-Maxwell, stress-conservation and Einstein-gauge propagation authored. Batch-4, batch-6 and batch-7 drafts and imported GR suppliers retain their exact unresolved proof statuses.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the imported Sobolev and finite-domain integration results. Let $\Sigma=\{s=0\}$ be a spacelike slice in a smooth time-coordinate region $U\subset I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, with future unit normal $n$ and induced metric $h$. Use the global-potential system of [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] in temporal gauge $A_0=0$, including $\partial_sA_i=F_{0i}$ and the scalar first-order equations of [[lem-emg-temporal-scalar-positive-symmetric-reduction]]. Treat $\pi_a$ and $F_{ab}$ as independent evolution variables. Write $\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$ and $\mathcal D_a\pi_b:=\nabla_a\pi_b-i\lambda A_a\pi_b$ for the charged derivatives of the model suppliers. In this item $D$ denotes only the spatial Levi-Civita derivative of $h$; thus $D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi$ on a scalar, while $\mathcal D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi-i\lambda A_i\varphi$.

Fix a smooth background metric $\bar g$ and define

$$H^a:=g^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc}\bigr)$$

as in [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Let $D$ be the Levi–Civita derivative of $h$, let $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$, and put $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK$. Define the scalar and magnetic-potential residuals

$$C_i:=\pi_i-\partial_i\varphi+i\lambda A_i\varphi,\qquad B_{ij}:=F_{ij}-(\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i).$$

Assume the reduced scalar, sourced Maxwell, and harmonic-reduced Einstein evolution equations hold on $U$. The metric is in the admissible region of [[lem-emg-temporal-scalar-positive-symmetric-reduction]], with $g^{00}<0$ and positive definite $(g^{ij})$. The Maxwell field-strength evolution equations are the normal contractions $\iota_n(dF)=0$ and $\iota_n(d\star_gF-\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g)=0$, with the algebraic current source added to the Maxwell block. If $\partial_s=\alpha n+\beta^i\partial_i$, their coordinate-time contractions can contain shift multiples of the all-spatial residuals; no coordinate-time residual is set to zero before those spatial constraints are recovered. Assume initially

$$C_i=0,\qquad B_{ij}=0,\qquad D_i b^i=0,\qquad D_i e^i=\mu_0j^0,\qquad H|_\Sigma=0,$$

where in a positively oriented future orthonormal frame $F_{0i}=-e_i$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$, $\epsilon_{123}=1$, and $j^0=-n_aj^a$. Assume also the total-stress Einstein constraints

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)-D_X\tau=\kappa T(n,X)\quad(X\in T\Sigma),$$

where $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(X):=h^{ij}(D_{\partial_i}K)(\partial_j,X)$. The momentum constraint is an equality of covectors, independent of the choice of spatial coordinates or orthonormal frame.

For the metric first-order state $p_{ab}=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}=\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}$, require their initial values to equal the corresponding metric derivatives.

Then on a neighborhood of every initial point:

1. $C_i=0$ and $B_{ij}=0$ persist, so $\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi$ and $F=dA$.
2. The scalar equation gives $\nabla_a j^a=0$, and the sourced Maxwell evolution together with the two initial Gauss constraints gives $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$.
3. Before Einstein-equation recovery, $\nabla^a(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^\varphi_{ab})=0$.
4. The metric first-order derivative variables remain derivatives of the metric, and harmonic gauge propagates; hence the reduced Einstein equation is the full Einstein equation.

These statements hold for smooth solutions. They also hold for the classical finite-regularity system of [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]], with $g\in C^3$, $A,\varphi\in C^2$ and the evolved $F,\pi\in C^2$ supplied at periodic Sobolev order $s\ge5$. Smooth underlying coordinates and background are retained; smoothness of the physical fields is not inferred.

items.title: Local classical Einstein–Maxwell–charged-scalar development
items.design_state: Complete conditional periodic and general smooth local-development proof authored. Its exact analytic, geometric and subsidiary suppliers remain at their inspected draft/pending-verification statuses.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice $\mathrm{DC}$ ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix an integer $s\ge5$, constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $K_\varphi>0$, $\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and a real $V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U)$ on an open $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the attained values of $|\varphi|^2$. Use the system and units of [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] for smooth fields and its explicit classical extension [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]] for the finite-Sobolev branch.

Write $\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$ and $\mathcal D_a\pi_b:=\nabla_a\pi_b-i\lambda A_a\pi_b$ for the charged derivatives of the model suppliers. In this item $D$ denotes only the spatial Levi-Civita derivative of $h$; thus $D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi$ on a scalar, while $\mathcal D_i\varphi=\partial_i\varphi-i\lambda A_i\varphi$.

For any initial three-manifold $\Sigma$ with Riemannian metric $h$ below, use the abstract initial Lorentzian bundle $\mathcal V_\Sigma:=\mathbb R n\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $g_\Sigma(an+X,bn+Y):=-ab+h(X,Y)$ for $a,b\in\mathbb R$ and $X,Y\in T\Sigma$, as in [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]. Here $n$ is the distinguished future unit generator, realized as the future unit normal in any spacetime development; the data definition does not presuppose that development. For the periodic Cauchy result let $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and orient it by its ordered periodic coordinates, as in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Prescribe a real symmetric metric $h\in H^{s+1}$ whose continuous representative satisfies $h\ge c_0I$ for some $c_0>0$, a symmetric tensor $K\in H^s$, spatial vector fields $e,b\in H^s$, a global real spatial one-form $A_\Sigma\in H^s$, a complex scalar $\varphi_0\in H^{s+1}$, and an independent complex datum $\pi_n\in H^s$ for the normal component of the charged derivative, realized by $\mathcal D_n\varphi|_\Sigma=\pi_n$. All Sobolev spaces are real componentwise spaces with complex fields split into real and imaginary parts, as in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Let $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ be any positively oriented $h$-orthonormal spatial frame. The associated initial two-form $F_\Sigma$ on $\mathcal V_\Sigma$ is defined invariantly by

$$F_\Sigma(X,n)=h(e,X),\qquad F_\Sigma(X,Y)=\mathrm{vol}_h(b,X,Y)\quad(X,Y\in T\Sigma).$$

Thus, writing $e_i=h(e,\mathfrak e_i)$ and $b_i=h(b,\mathfrak e_i)$, its frame components are $F_\Sigma(\mathfrak e_i,n)=e_i$ and $F_\Sigma(\mathfrak e_i,\mathfrak e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$, with $\epsilon_{123}=+1$. Require $F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$, $\pi_i=(\mathcal D_i\varphi_0)=\partial_i\varphi_0-i\lambda A_{\Sigma,i}\varphi_0$, and $A(n)=0$. Fix a smooth positive reference metric $\gamma$ and the product comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\gamma$ near the initial slice. The harmonic-gauge vector is $H^a:=g^{bc}(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc})$; prescribe the following initial metric jet relative to this fixed smooth background:

$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\quad g_{00}=-1,\quad g_{0i}=0,\quad \partial_0g_{ij}=2K_{ij},\quad \partial_0g_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK,\quad \partial_0g_{0i}=h_{ij}h^{k\ell}(\Gamma(h)^j{}_{k\ell}-\Gamma(\gamma)^j{}_{k\ell}).$$

Let $D$ be the Levi–Civita derivative of $h$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK$, and $T=T^{\mathrm{EM}}+T^\varphi$ be evaluated on the complete initial data. Define $j^0:=-n_aj^a$ in the normal frame and assume the sourced Maxwell and total-stress Einstein constraints

$$D_i b^i=0,\qquad D_i e^i=\mu_0j^0,\qquad R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)-D_X\tau=\kappa T(n,X)\quad(X\in T\Sigma),$$

where $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(X)=h^{ij}(D_{\partial_i}K)(\partial_j,X)$, $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$, and $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ in a spacetime realization. The constraint expressions are interpreted using their continuous representatives at the stated Sobolev orders. On the reduced coordinate domain require $g^{00}<0$ and the inverse spatial block $(g^{ij})$ to be positive definite. The real first-order state consists of the metric variables $(g_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi})$ relative to a fixed smooth background, the six Maxwell variables $(e_i,b_i)$, the three potential components $A_i$, and the real and imaginary parts of $\varphi,\pi_0,\pi_i$. For fixed reference scales $L_0>0$ metres and $F_0>0$ tesla, replace each first metric derivative $v$ and each $\pi_a$ by $L_0v$ and $L_0\pi_a$, each $e_i,b_i$ by $e_i/F_0,b_i/F_0$, and each $A_i$ by $A_i/(L_0F_0)$; $g_{ab}$ and $\varphi$ are already dimensionless. These fixed invertible rescalings make the componentwise real Sobolev state dimensionless and add no equations. Let $u_0$ be the resulting state in the sense of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]], and suppose its continuous range is a compact $K_0$ contained in the interior of a compact $K_1$ inside an open admissible state set $O$, with $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ and $R\ge0$. On an open time interval $I\ni0$, the complete periodic coefficient maps are smooth jointly on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ as in [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]; the potential range lies in $\mathcal U$, and the combined time matrix is positive definite throughout $O$.

Then there is $T_*>0$ and a local solution on $(-T_*,T_*)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ of the full Einstein, sourced Maxwell, and classical charged-scalar equations. Its first-order metric and matter state has the $L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ regularity of [[thm-emg-symmetric-hyperbolic-research-supplier]]; the metric satisfies $g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$ and $\partial_0g\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$, while $F,\pi,A_i\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$. The constraints and first-order metric, scalar, and potential compatibility conditions propagate. Smooth data give a smooth development on the same local interval.

More generally, let $\Sigma$ be any smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary. Prescribe a smooth positive-definite metric $h\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*\Sigma)$, a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $K\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*\Sigma)$, smooth spatial vector fields $e,b\in C^\infty(\Sigma;T\Sigma)$, a smooth global one-form $A_\Sigma\in C^\infty(\Sigma;T^*\Sigma)$, a complex scalar $\varphi_0\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\mathbb C)$, and an independent complex datum $\pi_n\in C^\infty(\Sigma;\mathbb C)$ realized by $\mathcal D_n\varphi|_\Sigma=\pi_n$ on $\mathcal V_\Sigma$. Define $F_\Sigma$ on $\mathcal V_\Sigma$ by the same $h,e,b$ convention in local positively oriented orthonormal frames, without requiring a global frame. Require $F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$, $\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi_0$, $A(n)=0$, and the sourced Maxwell and total-stress Einstein constraints displayed above at every point of $\Sigma$. Restrict to neighborhoods where $|\varphi|^2\in\mathcal U$. Then the data have a smooth local development near each initial point. Any two developments of this same fixed model and complete data are related near the initial surface by a data-fixing, time-orientation-preserving isometry and a global-potential gauge transformation

$$A\mapsto A+d\chi,\qquad \varphi\mapsto e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi,$$

for a smooth real $\chi$ with $\chi=0$ on the initial surface; under the formal units of [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]], $[\chi]=\mathrm{Wb}$ so $\lambda\chi$ is dimensionless. No nontrivial bundle sector, singular source, global-in-time existence, uniform noncompact time width, or geodesic completeness is asserted.

items.design_state: The zero-field reduction and exact-potential converse are proved directly; the local-existence instance is conditional on the assigned development theorem.
items.statement: Use [[def-emg-trivial-potential-charged-scalar-system]] and suppose $0\in\mathcal U$ and $V(0)=0$. Let $\varphi\equiv0$ and $\pi_a\equiv0$. Then the scalar equation, current, and scalar stress vanish, and the full coupled field equations reduce exactly to the source-free Einstein–Maxwell equations. Conversely, any smooth source-free Einstein–Maxwell solution on this region that admits the global potential $F=dA$ is a solution of the defined charged-scalar system with $\varphi=0$. The condition $V(0)=0$ is essential for the zero scalar stress conclusion. In particular, source-free initial data in this exact-potential sector that satisfy the local-development theorem's hypotheses have a smooth local realization in this branch.

items.statement:
Use a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable underlying oriented four-manifold
with a time-oriented $C^3$ Lorentzian metric, signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, Levi-Civita connection, curvature convention, and SI length-coordinate
units of [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Use the explicit classical domain of [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]]. Let $A$ be a $C^2$, globally defined real
one-form with components in tesla-metres, and set $F:=dA$, so $F$ is a $C^1$
exact real two-form. The globally defined potential is the selected
**trivial-potential sector**: it excludes bundles with no global potential and
does not impose an integer charge condition.

Let $\varphi:M\to\mathbb C$ be a $C^2$ dimensionless classical scalar field. Smooth configurations remain a subclass.
Choose $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ with units $(\mathrm{T\,m^2})^{-1}$, a constant
$K_\varphi>0$ with units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$, and an open set
$\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the range of $|\varphi|^2$ together
with a smooth real function $V:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R$ whose values are in
$\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. No sign, polynomial-degree, or smallness condition is
imposed on $V$.

Define the gauge-covariant scalar derivative and charged covector by
$P_a:=D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$. For a charged
covector $P_b$, define $D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b$, where $\nabla$
is the Levi-Civita derivative, and set $D^aP_a:=g^{ab}D_aP_b$. The adopted
classical matter action is

$$S_\varphi[g,A,\varphi]= -\frac{K_\varphi}{2c}\int_M\left(g^{ab}\overline{P_a}P_b+V(|\varphi|^2)\right)\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

With the stated SI dimensions, $S_\varphi$ has unit joule-second. For a gauge
function $\chi$ in $A\mapsto A+d\chi$, assign $[\chi]=\mathrm{T\,m^2}=\mathrm{Wb}$,
so $d\chi$ has the same unit as the components of $A$ and $\lambda\chi$ is
dimensionless.

On a noncompact domain the integral is used when finite; otherwise the
formulation concerns compactly supported action differences. Variations are
smooth and compactly supported in the fixed global-potential sector. Adopt this
functional as a classical matter model. In particular, this item does not
assert that the model describes nature, that its coupled equations have a
solution, or that the scalar is a quantum field.

The scalar action is adopted in this global real-potential domain. The
Einstein–Hilbert and free Maxwell coefficients below agree with the smooth
action convention of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]], but the present
model is declared directly: an arbitrary real $\lambda$ is not required to
define an integer-weight representation of a principal circle bundle.
For the declared classical class, separately adopt the same total functional on the domain and compact smooth directions of [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]]:

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\frac{c^3}{16\pi G_N}\int_M(R-2\Lambda)\,\mathrm{vol}_g-\frac{1}{4\mu_0c}\int_MF_{ab}F^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g+S_\varphi.$$

Every integral here is a relative compact action when a global integral is not finite. Adopt independent stationarity for all smooth compact symmetric inverse-metric, real one-form and complex scalar directions. [[lem-emg-classical-charged-scalar-compact-variation]] proves all first variations and their pointwise equation equivalence at $g\in C^3$, $A,\varphi\in C^2$. This declares the classical action model, including all its smooth configurations, without requiring a circle-bundle matter representation. The separate smooth circle-sector action formulation is not a prerequisite for this global-real-potential branch.

Its gauge action is
$A\mapsto A+d\chi$, $\varphi\mapsto e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi$ for a smooth
real function $\chi$; direct substitution gives
$D'_a\varphi'=e^{i\lambda\chi}D_a\varphi$, so the scalar action density is
gauge invariant. It is also invariant under orientation-preserving
diffeomorphisms because its integrand is a scalar multiplied by the metric
volume form. These are properties of the selected functional, not evidence
that it describes nature.

For clarity, the mathematical supplier [[lem-emg-charged-scalar-variation]]
gives the compact first variations and defines

$$E_\varphi:=D^aP_a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}\left(g^{cd}\overline{P_c}P_d+V(|\varphi|^2)\right).$$

Here $E_\varphi=0$ is the scalar Euler–Lagrange equation, $j$ is the current
from varying $A$, and $T^\varphi$ is the Hilbert stress tensor from varying the
inverse metric. Those formulas are mathematical consequences of the action
under the cited supplier's hypotheses; they are not extra physical laws. For smooth fields those formulas use the cited smooth variation result; for the declared classical fields the identical formulas and compact stationarity equivalence are proved in [[lem-emg-classical-charged-scalar-compact-variation]]. Both are mathematical deductions, separate from adoption of the physical model.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice (DC). No
stronger choice principle is assumed. Use a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable,
boundaryless, oriented underlying four-manifold with a time-oriented $C^3$
Lorentzian metric $(M,g,N,o)$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$,
curvature convention, length coordinates $x^0=ct$, and SI assignments of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Fix $c,G_N,\mu_0,K_\varphi>0$,
$\lambda,\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and a real $V\in C^\infty(\mathcal U)$ on an
open interval $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing the attained values
of $|\varphi|^2$. The classical domain is [[def-emg-classical-charged-scalar-finite-regularity-system]]: the model uses a $C^2$ complex scalar $\varphi$ and a
globally defined real $C^2$ one-form $A$ with $F=dA$. The smooth configurations are retained as a subclass. In length coordinates
$[A_a]=\mathrm{Wb\,m^{-1}}$, $[\lambda]=\mathrm{Wb^{-1}}$,
$[K_\varphi]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}$, and $[V]=\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.

Adopt the explicit classical compact-interior stationary total action of
[[post-emg-trivial-classical-charged-scalar-model]]. The same declared classical action includes smooth configurations; no integer-weight circle representation is assumed for arbitrary real $\lambda$.
Write $\mathcal D_a\varphi:=\partial_a\varphi-i\lambda A_a\varphi$ and
$P_a:=\mathcal D_a\varphi$. For a charged covector set
$\mathcal D_aP_b:=\nabla_aP_b-i\lambda A_aP_b$, where $\nabla$ is the
spacetime Levi-Civita derivative; indices are raised with $g^{-1}$. The scalar
equation, current and Hilbert tensor are

$$E_\varphi:=\mathcal D_aP^a-V'(|\varphi|^2)\varphi=0,\qquad j^a:=K_\varphi\lambda\operatorname{Im}(\overline\varphi P^a),$$

$$T^\varphi_{ab}:=K_\varphi\operatorname{Re}(\overline{P_a}P_b)-\frac{K_\varphi}{2}g_{ab}\bigl(g^{cd}\overline{P_c}P_d+V(|\varphi|^2)\bigr).$$

Set $T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd})$,
$T^{\mathrm{tot}}:=T^{\mathrm{EM}}+T^\varphi$, and
$\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The equations of the adopted action model are

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{tot}}_{ab},\qquad E_\varphi=0.$$

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth spacelike initial hypersurface, $h$ its induced
Riemannian metric, $n$ its future unit normal, and
$\mathcal K(X,Y):=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ its second fundamental form. Let
$\nabla^\Sigma$ denote the Levi-Civita derivative of $h$ and
$\tau:=\operatorname{tr}_h\mathcal K$.
Let $i_\Sigma:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be the inclusion. The complete scalar
data are $\varphi_0:=\varphi|_\Sigma$,
$\pi_i:=(\mathcal D_i\varphi)|_\Sigma$, and the independently prescribed
$\pi_n:=n^a\mathcal D_a\varphi|_\Sigma$. In a spatial chart this means
$\pi_i=\partial_i\varphi_0-i\lambda A_{\Sigma,i}\varphi_0$. The globally
defined spatial potential is $A_\Sigma:=i_\Sigma^*A$, with exact-potential
compatibility $F|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$. Use the temporal potential
gauge $A_0:=A(\partial_0)=0$ in local normal coordinates with $\partial_0=n$
initially, so $A(n)=0$ on $\Sigma$ and $\pi_0=\pi_n$ initially.

For the periodic high-regularity branch take
$\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ with
dimensionless periodic coordinates $y^i$, and fix $L_0>0$ metres so that the
length coordinates are $x^i=L_0y^i$. Sobolev norms use $y$; tensor components
and derivative units use the length coordinates $x$. Let $s\ge5$ be an integer. Prescribe a
Riemannian metric $h\in H^{s+1}$ whose continuous
representative satisfies $h\ge c_0I$ for some $c_0>0$, a symmetric
$\mathcal K\in H^s$, spatial vector fields $e,b\in H^s$, a global real
$A_\Sigma\in H^s$, $\varphi_0\in H^{s+1}$, and an independent complex
$\pi_n\in H^s$. Here the Sobolev spaces are componentwise real, with complex
components split into real and imaginary parts. For the periodic state, let
$(\mathsf e_A(h))_{A=1}^3$ be the positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame
obtained by Gram–Schmidt from the ordered global length-coordinate frame, as
specified in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Put
$\widehat e_A:=h(e,\mathsf e_A(h))$ and
$\widehat b_A:=h(b,\mathsf e_A(h))$. The initial two-form convention below
then gives $F_\Sigma(\mathsf e_A(h),n)=\widehat e_A$ and
$F_\Sigma(\mathsf e_A(h),\mathsf e_B(h))=\epsilon_{ABC}\widehat b_C$, with
$\epsilon_{123}=+1$. Thus $\widehat e_A=E_A/c$ and
$\widehat b_A=B_A$ in the observer convention of [[def-emg-geometry-units]],
and both components have unit tesla. Sobolev regularity of the vector fields
$e,b$ refers to their components in the fixed periodic coordinates; the
orthonormal-frame state components are those specified by the named convention.
The initial two-form $F_\Sigma$ is fixed by
$F_\Sigma(X,n)=h(e,X)$ and
$F_\Sigma(X,Y)=\mathrm{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$ for spatial $X,Y$. Assume
$\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi_0$ and
$F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$. With $j,T^{\mathrm{tot}}$
evaluated on the complete initial fields, impose the Maxwell constraints

$$\nabla^\Sigma_i b^i=0,\qquad \nabla^\Sigma_i e^i=\mu_0j^0,\qquad j^0:=-n_aj^a,$$

and the Einstein constraints in the stated sign convention,

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|\mathcal K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{tot}}(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_h\mathcal K)(X)-\nabla^\Sigma_X\tau=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{tot}}(n,X)\quad(X\in T\Sigma).$$

Here $(\operatorname{div}_h\mathcal K)(X):=h^{ij}(\nabla^\Sigma_{\partial_i}\mathcal K)(\partial_j,X)$, so the momentum equation is an equality of covectors and does not mix coordinate and orthonormal components.

Fix a smooth positive reference metric $\gamma$ on $\Sigma$ and the product
comparison metric $\bar g:=-(dx^0)^2+\gamma$ near the initial slice. Define
$H^a:=g^{bc}(\Gamma(g)^a{}_{bc}-\Gamma(\bar g)^a{}_{bc})$ and
$Q^i:=h^{jk}(\Gamma(h)^i{}_{jk}-\Gamma(\gamma)^i{}_{jk})$. Use the initial
harmonic metric jet

$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\quad g_{00}=-1,\quad g_{0i}=0,\quad \partial_0g_{ij}=2\mathcal K_{ij},\quad \partial_0g_{00}=-2\tau,\quad \partial_0g_{0i}=h_{ij}Q^j.$$

Let $\bar\nabla$ be the Levi-Civita derivative of $\bar g$ and put
$p_{ab}:=\bar\nabla_0g_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}:=\bar\nabla_i g_{ab}$ for the
first-order metric derivative variables. For a fixed field scale $F_0>0$
tesla, form the real first-order state from
$(g_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi})$, the six orthonormal-frame Maxwell components
$(\widehat e_A,\widehat b_A)$, the three spatial potential components $A_i$,
and the real and imaginary parts of $\varphi,\pi_0,\pi_i$. Rescale each first
metric derivative and each $\pi_a$ by multiplying by $L_0$, each
$\widehat e_A,\widehat b_A$ by dividing by $F_0$, and each $A_i$ by dividing
by $L_0F_0$; $g_{ab}$ and $\varphi$ are already
dimensionless. These fixed invertible scales are bookkeeping choices, not
extra equations. Denote the resulting componentwise-real periodic state by
$u_0$. Suppose its continuous range is a compact $K_0$ contained in the
interior of a compact $K_1$ inside an open admissible state set $O$, that the
coefficient maps are smooth on $O$, the potential range lies in $\mathcal U$,
and the combined time matrix is positive definite throughout $O$. Require
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ for some finite $R\ge0$. Thus
$u_0\in\mathcal S_s(K_0,R)$ in the componentwise real periodic Fourier and
weak-derivative convention used by the CP04 supplier.

Under the stated mathematical hypotheses of the current authored supplier
[[thm-emg-local-classical-charged-scalar-development]], these periodic data
have a local solution of the full Einstein, sourced
Maxwell, and classical charged-scalar equations on
$(-T_*,T_*)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Here $T_*>0$ is a width in the length
coordinate $x^0=ct$ (so the corresponding time width in seconds is $T_*/c$).
In its coordinate gauge, the first-order state lies in
$L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ with time derivative in
$L^\infty H^{s-1}$; the metric has
$g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$ and
$\partial_0g\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$, while
$F,\pi,A_i\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ and
$\varphi\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C H^s$. The Maxwell, scalar-potential,
metric-derivative, and harmonic constraints propagate. More generally, for
smooth data $(h,\mathcal K,e,b,A_\Sigma,\varphi_0,\pi_n)$ on any smooth
oriented three-manifold without boundary, define $F_\Sigma$ by
$F_\Sigma(X,n)=h(e,X)$ and
$F_\Sigma(X,Y)=\mathrm{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$ for spatial $X,Y$. The current authored supplier states local smooth development near each initial point, provided
$h$ is positive definite, $A_\Sigma$ is global,
$F_\Sigma|_{T\Sigma}=d_\Sigma A_\Sigma$,
$\pi_i=\mathcal D_i\varphi_0$, $A(n)=0$, the sourced Maxwell and
total-stress Einstein constraints hold, and $|\varphi|^2$ remains in
$\mathcal U$. Its uniqueness conclusion is local near the initial surface, up
to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry and electromagnetic
gauge $A\mapsto A+d\chi$,
$\varphi\mapsto e^{i\lambda\chi}\varphi$ with $\chi|_\Sigma=0$ and
$[\chi]=\mathrm{Wb}$. This is a local conditional deduction in the adopted action
model. It asserts no nontrivial bundle sector, singular source, global-in-time
existence, geodesic completeness, empirical validity, or quantum field.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and no boundary. Write $\Omega^k(M)$ for the smooth real sections of $\Lambda^kT^*M$. The classical electromagnetic field type is a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$. In length-coordinate charts its components have SI unit tesla; its integral over an oriented smooth two-surface has unit weber. The exterior derivative is denoted $d$. A field is **closed** when $dF=0$. Closedness is a field condition, not the same condition as having a global potential.

For an open set $U\subseteq M$, a **local potential** for $F$ on $U$ is a smooth real one-form $A_U\in\Omega^1(U)$ satisfying $dA_U=F|_U$. It is a **global potential** when $U=M$. In a length-coordinate chart the components of $A_U$ have unit tesla metre. This classical real-field description chooses $F$ itself and requires no bundle or global $A$.

An **optional circle-normalized connection sector** adds the mathematical data of a smooth right principal $U(1)$ bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and a connection, using the local-potential and circle-data conventions of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. Here $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ with multiplication. Concretely, supply a countable open cover $\{U_i\}$ and smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$ satisfying $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$. On overlap pieces with smooth real lifts $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$, the normalized local connection one-forms $a_i$ satisfy $a_j=a_i+df_{ij}$; in local fibre angles the convention is $\theta_j=\theta_i-f_{ij}$, so $d\theta_i+a_i$ patches. The local curvature forms $da_i$ agree. Fix an independent constant $\kappa_0>0$ with unit weber, and set $A_i=\kappa_0a_i$ and $F|_{U_i}=\kappa_0da_i$. Thus $a_i$ has component unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ in length coordinates, while $A_i$ has component unit tesla metre. Choosing $P$ and $\kappa_0$ is extra model data; no claim is made that every smooth closed real $F$ is the curvature of such a fixed-normalization connection.

The selected **topological sector** is the fixed pair consisting of the bundle $P$ and the normalization $\kappa_0$; its connection is data on that fixed bundle. Changing $P$ or $\kappa_0$ selects a different sector.

In a trivialization, a **gauge transformation** is a single-valued smooth map $h:U\to U(1)$; its local real lifts may differ by integer multiples of $2\pi$. A connection on a trivial bundle is **gauge trivial** when one such global map takes its normalized connection form to zero. For a closed piecewise-$C^1$ loop $\gamma$ lying in a trivialization, horizontal transport is defined by $\dot\theta=-a(\dot\gamma)$; the endpoint fibre rotation is its **holonomy**. When $a$ is one global one-form along the loop this is $\exp(-i\int_\gamma a)$. These definitions introduce no quantum state or quantum phase. The constant $\kappa_0$ is not identified with Planck's constant or a unit of electric charge.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real field with the SI conventions of [[def-emg-topological-sector]]. Assume the smooth branch of the adopted curved Maxwell postulate [[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]] applies on $M$, with no singular source in its domain. Only its homogeneous clause $dF=0$ is used below; no Einstein equation or coupled solution is asserted.

If $U\subseteq M$ is a nonempty star-shaped coordinate domain with chart image $V\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ star-shaped about a point $p$ (that is, $p+t(x-p)\in V$ for every $x\in V$ and $0\le t\le1$), then $F|_U$ has a smooth local potential. Use a length-coordinate chart for the following formula; its coordinates have unit metre. The components can be taken to be

$$A_\nu(x)=\int_0^1 t(x-p)^\mu F_{\mu\nu}(p+t(x-p))\,dt.$$

For an explicit global example, take $M_* =\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$ with Minkowski metric $-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, and $x^0,x,y,z$ measured in metres. Let $r>0$ be spatial radius, let $\theta,\phi$ be dimensionless spherical angles, and for $b\in\mathbb R$ with unit weber set

$$F_b=b\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi.$$

For each fixed $(x^0,r)$, let $S^2_r$ have its outward orientation, let $N,S$ be its north and south poles, and set $U_N=S^2_r\setminus\{S\}$, $U_S=S^2_r\setminus\{N\}$, and $O=U_N\cap U_S$. The corresponding open patches in $M_*$ are $\widetilde U_N=\{r+z>0\}$ and $\widetilde U_S=\{r-z>0\}$, whose restrictions to each $S^2_r$ are $U_N$ and $U_S$. The angular coordinate $\phi$ is defined modulo $2\pi$ on $O$, while $d\phi$ is a global one-form there. The form $F_b$ is smooth and closed on $M_*$, with outward sphere flux $\int_{S^2_r}F_b=4\pi b$. For $b\ne0$ it has no global smooth one-form potential on $M_*$. It has local north/south potentials

$$A_N=b(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad A_S=-b(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi.$$

For the fixed circle normalization $\kappa_0>0$ of [[def-emg-topological-sector]], these patch as the stated normalized $U(1)$ connection exactly when $2b/\kappa_0\in\mathbb Z$: on the overlap, $A_S-A_N=-2b\,d\phi$ and the transition is $g_{NS}(\phi)=\exp(-2ib\phi/\kappa_0)$. This integrality is a restriction of the selected connection sector; the classical real-field description permits every real $b$.

There is also a flat-connection example on the smooth base $M_0=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times S^1\times\mathbb R^2$. Write $w\in S^1\subset\mathbb C$ for the circle coordinate and $\nu=-iw^{-1}dw$ for its global angular one-form, normalized by $\int_{S^1}\nu=2\pi$. For dimensionless $a\in\mathbb R$, the global one-form $A=\kappa_0a\,\nu$ has $F=dA=0$, while its normalized connection has holonomy $e^{-2\pi ia}$ around the positive circle. It is gauge trivial for integer $a$ and is not gauge trivial for noninteger $a$. On an angle chart $w=e^{i\phi}$, $\nu=d\phi$. This is a classical connection statement on a smooth base, not a claim about a quantum phase or an Einstein solution. The punctured point in the sphere example is outside the field domain; no physical magnetic monopole or quantum electric-charge quantization is asserted.

Use the oriented sphere field $F_b=b\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$ on the punctured spacetime of [F1]. For $b=\kappa_0/2$, its flux is $2\pi\kappa_0$ and its transition map is $e^{-i\phi}$. This map is single-valued on the equatorial circle and has winding number of absolute value one. For $b=\kappa_0/(2\sqrt2)$, the real field is still smooth and closed on the punctured domain, but $2b/\kappa_0=1/\sqrt2$ is not an integer, so these north/south potentials do not define a connection with that fixed circle normalization. For $b=0$, the field and the chosen connection can both be zero.

Separately, on $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times S^1\times\mathbb R^2$, the normalized flat connection $a\,d\phi$ has holonomy $e^{-2\pi ia}$. At $a=1/2$ this is $-1$, so the connection is not gauge trivial; at $a=1$ the single-valued map $e^{-i\phi}$ removes it. The distinction is a classical statement about connection data and does not use a quantum wavefunction.

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth ($C^\infty$), Hausdorff, second-countable,
boundaryless, oriented, time-oriented four-manifold with Lorentz metric of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and oriented volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Use SI units:
$c>0$ has exact defining value $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; its
identification as the vacuum light/clock conversion is adopted in this
framework, not derived here. The constant $\mu_0>0$ has units
$\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI; set
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$. The manifold
orientation is independent of the time orientation. Let $\mathcal D\subseteq M$
be the open field domain. Let $F$ be a smooth real two-form with components in
tesla, and let $j$ be a smooth vector field whose components have units
$\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, both on $\mathcal D$. An **observer field** is a smooth
future-directed vector field $n$ with $g(n,n)=-1$; no
hypersurface-orthogonality or global inertial chart is assumed. On decomposable
$k$-covectors define
$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j))$ and extend bilinearly. Define the Hodge star by
$\alpha\wedge *\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ and define
insertion by $(i_X\omega)(Y_1,\ldots,Y_{k-1})=\omega(X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_{k-1})$.
The observer fields are the spatial covectors
$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b=-c(i_nF)_a$ and
$B_a:= -(*F)_{ab}n^b=(i_n*F)_a$. Antisymmetry makes both covectors spatial,
that is, they annihilate $n$. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with
time axis $n$ (an ordered basis with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$), let $\delta_{ij}$ be the Euclidean spatial metric and let
$\varepsilon_{ijk}$ be the alternating symbol with $\varepsilon_{123}=+1$;
at an event write $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\varepsilon_{ijk}B_k$ for the
tetrad components at that event. Define the local
charge and current densities by $\rho:=j^0/c$ and $J^i:=j^i$, so
$[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$ and $[J^i]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. For spatial
components define $\nabla\cdot X:=\sum_i\partial_iX_i$ and
$(\nabla\times X)_k:=\varepsilon_{kij}\partial_iX_j$. Coordinates are
lengths, with $x^0=ct$ and $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$; $E_i$ has units
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and $B_i$ has units tesla.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as stated in [A2] and the adopted
curved vacuum Maxwell equations in [A1] on $\mathcal D$, with $\nabla$ the
Levi-Civita connection of $g$. A **point-normal
Lorentz chart at $p\in\mathcal D$** means a positively oriented chart in
$\mathcal D$ with $g_{ab}(p)=\operatorname{diag}
(-1,1,1,1)$, $\partial_cg_{ab}(p)=0$, and coordinate time axis $n(p)$.
In this chart define $\widehat E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$\widehat B_i(x):=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$; at $p$ these are the
components measured by $n(p)$. Derivatives in the pointwise formulas below
act on these chart-component functions, not on components of a varying
observer congruence. Then
$\nabla_a j^a=0$. At each event $p$, in a positively oriented point-normal
Lorentz chart whose time axis is $n(p)$, the component equations at $p$ are

$$\nabla\cdot\widehat{\mathbf E}=\rho/\epsilon_0,\qquad \nabla\times\widehat{\mathbf B}-c^{-2}\partial_t\widehat{\mathbf E}=\mu_0\mathbf J,\qquad \nabla\cdot\widehat{\mathbf B}=0,\qquad \partial_t\widehat{\mathbf B}+\nabla\times\widehat{\mathbf E}=0.$$

These four component equations hold throughout a fixed Minkowski inertial
chart with constant observer $n=\partial_0$. For $k\ge0$, let
$\Delta^k:=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_k)\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,\sum_i t_i=1\}$.
A **smooth singular $k$-simplex** is a smooth map $\Delta^k\to\mathcal D$; a
**finite smooth singular $k$-chain** is a finite real linear combination of
such simplices, with boundary the alternating sum of their oriented faces. A
smooth singular three-simplex is **spacelike** when its differential has rank
three and its pullback metric is positive definite on its interior; a
spacelike three-chain has this property on each simplex and is oriented by
its future-directed unit normal. For a finite smooth oriented spacelike
three-chain $\Sigma$ in the field domain, define its source charge by
$Q(\Sigma):=c^{-1}\int_\Sigma i_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ (in coulombs). If
$\partial\Sigma$ is its finite smooth boundary chain, then

$$Q(\Sigma)=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_{\partial\Sigma}*F.$$

The component identities at a general event are local observer measurements;
they do not assert that an arbitrary observer field supplies a global inertial
coordinate system or a preferred foliation.

items.title: Global Gauss flux and compact-slice neutrality
items.design_state: complete-conditional-argument; current-supplier-interface-and-proof-status-inspected
items.statement:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth ($C^\infty$), Hausdorff, second-countable,
boundaryless, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, with oriented metric volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Use SI
constants $c>0$ with exact defining value $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
and $\mu_0>0$ in $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ (experimentally determined in the
revised SI); define $\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$.
Let $\mathcal D\subseteq M$ be the open field domain. Let $F$ be a smooth real
two-form with components in tesla and let $j$ be a smooth current vector field
with components in $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ on $\mathcal D$. Assume
Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as
stated in [A2] and the adopted Maxwell equations in [A1].

Use the Lorentzian Hodge star $\star_g$, the unique smooth bundle map defined
by [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]: on decomposable $k$-covectors its
induced pairing is
$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g
:=\det(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j))$, extended bilinearly, and
$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$.
In four dimensions with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, that supplier also proves
$\star_g^2=-\mathrm{id}$ on two-forms. Write $*$ for $\star_g$ when the
metric is fixed.

For $k\ge0$, let $\Delta^k:=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_k)\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,
\sum_i t_i=1\}$. A **smooth singular $k$-simplex** is a smooth map
$\Delta^k\to\mathcal D$, and a **finite smooth singular $k$-chain** is a
finite real linear combination of such simplices; $\partial$ is the
alternating sum of their oriented faces. A smooth singular three-simplex is
**spacelike** when
its differential has rank three and its pulled-back metric is positive
definite on its interior; a spacelike three-chain has this property on each
simplex. Orient spacelike simplices using their future-directed unit normal.
Define insertion by
$(i_j\omega)(X_1,\ldots,X_{k-1})=\omega(j,X_1,\ldots,X_{k-1})$. For every
finite smooth singular three-chain $C$, set
$\Phi_j(C):=c^{-1}\int_C i_j\mathrm{vol}_g$; for a spacelike slice $\Sigma$
write $Q(\Sigma):=\Phi_j(\Sigma)$, in coulombs.

For every finite smooth oriented four-chain $V$ whose boundary decomposes as
$\partial V=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$, where $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$ are finite
spacelike three-chains and $B$ is the finite side chain, the source-current
flux satisfies

$$Q(\Sigma_2)-Q(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_j(B).$$

For every compact boundaryless oriented smooth spacelike slice $\Sigma$ in
the domain, represented by a finite smooth three-cycle,
$Q(\Sigma)=0$. For every finite smooth three-chain $W$,
$\int_{\partial W}F=0$; where $j=0$ throughout $W$,
$\int_{\partial W}*F=0$. These conclusions concern bounding surfaces. A
closed surface is **nonbounding in the field domain** when it is a finite
smooth two-cycle $C$ with no finite smooth three-chain $W$ in that domain such
that $C=\partial W$; no zero-flux conclusion is made for such a surface. The
field topology is the global real closed-form model of [F2]; an optional
normalized $U(1)$ connection sector with chosen flux normalization $\kappa_0$
is extra structure, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication,
and no electric-charge quantization is inferred.

**Punctured-Minkowski example (a separate specialization of the general
setup).** For $b\ne0$ with $b$ measured in webers, let
$M_{\mathrm{punct}}:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$ be the
open punctured spacetime, with metric
$g_{\mathrm{punct}}:=-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$, standard orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, future time orientation given by
$\partial_{x^0}$, and field domain $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{punct}}:=M_{\mathrm{punct}}$.
Take $j_{\mathrm{punct}}=0$; in this example, “source-free” means that the
adopted equations [A1] reduce to $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=0$. Write
$r_{\mathrm{punct}}:=(x^2+y^2+z^2)^{1/2}$, and define on this domain

$$F_b:=\frac{b}{r_{\mathrm{punct}}^3}\left(x\,dy\wedge dz+y\,dz\wedge dx+z\,dx\wedge dy\right).$$

The coordinates $x^0=ct,x,y,z$ and $r_{\mathrm{punct}}$ are in metres. This
is one particular instance of the arbitrary $M,g,\mathcal D,F,j$ fixed above;
the following example claims concern this instance only. For every radius
$R>0$, the sphere $S^2_R$ at fixed $x^0$, with outward orientation, has
$\int_{S^2_R}F_b=4\pi b\ne0$. Its Hodge-dual source-free field
$-\star_{g_{\mathrm{punct}}}F_b$ has
$\int_{S^2_R}\star_{g_{\mathrm{punct}}}(-\star_{g_{\mathrm{punct}}}F_b)=4\pi b\ne0$
as well. The sphere is nonbounding in this punctured domain; this example
makes no claim about a source or field value at the excluded origin.
items.physical_scope: Finite-domain charge and flux identities under the smooth curved vacuum Maxwell postulate, including side-flux balance and neutrality of compact boundaryless smooth slices. Noncompact decay, singular boundaries, and empirical claims are outside scope; nonbounding cycles are not assigned zero flux by Stokes.

items.statement:
Let $p$ be an event in an open neighborhood $U$ on which a smooth
future-directed unit timelike observer field $n$ is defined. At $p$ choose a
positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n(p)$ and signature
$(-,+,+,+)$. Let $E_0\in\mathbb R$ have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and
$B_0\in\mathbb R$ have units tesla. For the pure-electric
observer field $\mathbf E=(E_0,0,0)$, $\mathbf B=0$, the SI stress components
of [F1], with the stated Countable Choice background premise [A2], are

$$T^{00}=\frac{\epsilon_0E_0^2}{2},\qquad T^{0i}=0,\qquad (T^{ij})=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(-\frac{\epsilon_0E_0^2}{2}, \frac{\epsilon_0E_0^2}{2},\frac{\epsilon_0E_0^2}{2}\right).$$

For the pure-magnetic observer field $\mathbf E=0$,
$\mathbf B=(0,0,B_0)$, they are

$$T^{00}=\frac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{0i}=0,\qquad (T^{ij})=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0}, \frac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0},-\frac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0}\right).$$

In each case $T^a{}_a=0$. The entries display anisotropic spatial stress in the
chosen observer frame; no perfect-fluid identification is made.

items.title: Smooth formal matter, EM tensors and observer quantities
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, boundaryless oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $N$ is the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, and $o$ is an independent orientation. Let $\nabla$ be the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature sign and contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$. The geometric and observer conventions are those of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. The tangent-bundle smooth structure inherits only the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix formal parameters $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $G_N>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, all four coordinates have units metres and $g_{ab}$ is dimensionless. These are mathematical parameters with the displayed SI bookkeeping; they assert no measured value, exactness of $\mu_0$, or physical law.

A field strength $F$ is a real $C^2$ antisymmetric covariant two-tensor field. Its metric-raised components are $F^{ab}=g^{ac}g^{bd}F_{cd}$. For a future unit observer $n$ ($g(n,n)=-1$), the rest space is $n^\perp$ and the projection is $h_n(v)=v+g(n,v)n$. The observer electric and magnetic covectors are $E_{n,a}=cF_{ab}n^b$ and $B_{n,a}=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$, with the oriented Lorentzian Hodge convention of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. They annihilate $n$ and use the positive metric induced on the rest covector space. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

For such an $F$, define

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

For any symmetric covariant tensor $S_{ab}$ and unit observer $n$, its observer energy density is $S_{ab}n^an^b$. Its observer energy-current vector is $-S^a{}_bn^b$; the spatial energy flux measured by $n$ is the projection $h_n(-S^a{}_bn^b)$ into $n^\perp$. A nonzero causal vector is future-directed when it has negative inner product with $N$; future timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, and future null means the vector is nonzero and $g(v,v)=0$.

In four dimensions, define the **weak energy condition** (WEC) for $S$ by $S_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; the **null energy condition** (NEC) by $S_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; and the **dominant energy condition** (DEC) by requiring $-S^a{}_bv^b$ to be future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$. Define the **strong energy condition** (SEC) by the WEC for $S_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}S_{cd})g_{ab}$. These are definitions of tensor inequalities only; no general matter positivity premise is included.

A matter tensor $T_m^{ab}$ is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant two-tensor field; a current $j^a$ is a $C^1$ vector field. The **formal sourced Maxwell equations** are $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$. The **matter exchange equation** is $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The **formal Einstein equation** is

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr).$$

Here $T_{m,ab}$ is obtained by lowering both indices with $g$. Each displayed equation is a pointwise mathematical condition on the supplied fields with the regularities stated above. A formal Einstein–Maxwell–matter solution is a tuple satisfying whichever of these equations are explicitly assumed on the stated open domain; no existence or uniqueness of such a tuple is asserted.

Two matter forms used below are defined as follows. A **charged-dust form** has $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$, where $\rho,\sigma\in C^1$, $\rho\ge0$, and $U\in C^2$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ its charge-to-mass ratio is $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$; it is not defined by division on $\{\rho=0\}$. A **perfect-fluid form** has

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},$$

where $\epsilon,p\in C^1$ and $U$ has the same timelike normalization. No equation of state, conductivity law, entropy law, or matter evolution theorem is part of this definition. A current may additionally be written $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$; an Ohmic relation $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, $\chi\ge0$, is a separately imposed constitutive hypothesis, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$.

On an open set $V$, a **local potential** for $F$ is a supplied smooth one-form $A$ with $dA=F$. Such a potential need not exist globally. A local gauge change is $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$ for a supplied smooth scalar $\lambda$; this leaves $F$ unchanged. No global bundle, potential, or point-source construction is asserted.

In the stated length-coordinate SI interpretation, $[F_{ab}]=\mathrm T$, $[A_a]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[j^a]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, $[T_m]=[T_{\mathrm{EM}}]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, $[\rho]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $[\sigma]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[\epsilon]=[p]=\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $[\chi]=\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$. The equalities $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ make the displayed tensor equations dimensionally consistent. No distributional product or stress tensor for a singular point source is defined.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an open subset of the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian domain of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $ho,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega,\mathbb R)$ with $ho>0$, and let $U\in C^2(\Omega,T\Omega)$ be future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Set $T_m^{ab}=ho U^aU^b$, $j^a=\sigma U^a$, and $a^b=U^a
abla_aU^b$. Assume the formal matter-exchange equation $
abla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. Then this equation is equivalent on $\Omega$ to

$$
abla_a(ho U^a)=0,\qquad ho a^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c.$$

On $\Omega$, define $\alpha=\sigma/ho$. Under the continuity equation, charge-current conservation $
abla_aj^a=0$ is equivalent to $U^a
abla_a\alpha=0$. Thus the equation constrains the derivative of $\alpha$ along the dust flow; it does not impose spatial constancy of $\alpha$. The claim is a pointwise conditional identity and supplies no coupled-field existence theorem or Maxwell equation.

items.title: Perfect-fluid exchange projections and conduction heating
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an open subset of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $\epsilon,p,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega,\mathbb R)$ and let $U\in C^2(\Omega,T\Omega)$ be future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Set

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab},\qquad a^b=U^a\nabla_aU^b,\quad D=U^a\nabla_a,\quad \theta=\nabla_aU^a,\quad h^b{}_c=\delta^b{}_c+\frac{U^bU_c}{c^2}.$$

For a current $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$, define $f^b=F^b{}_cj^c$ and assume the mathematical exchange equation $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=f^b$. Then it is equivalent to the longitudinal and rest-space equations

$$D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\theta=-U_bf^b,\qquad \frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}a^b+h^{ba}\nabla_ap=h^b{}_cf^c.$$

The rest electric field of $U$ is $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$. If $q^a=\chi E_U^a$ for a specified scalar $\chi\ge0$, then the electromagnetic contribution to the comoving energy balance is $-U_bf^b=\chi\,g(E_U,E_U)\ge0$. For $q=0$ it is zero. The Ohmic relation is an additional constitutive hypothesis; no equation of state, entropy law, or fluid existence result follows.
