items.title: Pointwise Maxwell and matter energy-condition vocabulary
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, metric $g$, and future cone of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Here timelike means $g(v,v)<0$, null means $v\ne0$ and $g(v,v)=0$, causal means timelike or null, and a nonzero causal vector is future-directed when $g(v,N)<0$, as in that supplier. A future unit observer is a vector $n$ with $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)<0$. At a point $p$, let $T_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous real symmetric bilinear form, represented by the covariant tensor $T_{ab}$. Define its metric trace by $\operatorname{tr}_g T:=g^{ab}T_{ab}$ and its raised mixed tensor by $T^a{}_b:=g^{ac}T_{cb}$.

- The **weak energy condition (WEC)** holds at $p$ when $T_{ab}v^av^b\ge0$ for every future timelike $v\in T_pM$.
- The **null energy condition (NEC)** holds at $p$ when $T_{ab}\ell^a\ell^b\ge0$ for every nonzero future-directed null $\ell\in T_pM$.
- The **strong energy condition (SEC)** holds at $p$ when the WEC holds for the trace-reversed tensor $T_{ab}-\tfrac12(\operatorname{tr}_gT)g_{ab}$.
- The **dominant energy condition (DEC)** holds at $p$ when, for every future-directed timelike $v\in T_pM$, the vector $J^a:=-T^a{}_bv^b$ is future causal or zero.

These are pointwise algebraic conditions. They are independent of an Einstein equation or an assertion that a physical material realizes $T$. The continuous regularity suffices for the definitions; any differentiability needed for a conservation identity is a separate hypothesis.

For a future unit observer $n$, observer energy density means $T_{ab}n^an^b$. The observer energy-current vector is $-T^a{}_bn^b$, and its spatial energy flux is the projection of this vector into the positive rest space $n^\perp$.
items.strategy: Record the exact pointwise WEC, NEC, SEC, and DEC predicates before the selected energy-condition theorem.

items.statement:
Use the energy-condition definitions of [[def-emg-pointwise-energy-conditions]] and the matter and Maxwell tensor definitions of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. At every point of an oriented time-oriented Lorentzian domain, the Maxwell tensor $T_{\mathrm{EM}}$ of that definition is symmetric, trace-free, and satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC and DEC. Its observer energy density and energy flux in a positively oriented orthonormal rest frame are

$$u=\frac{|E|^2/c^2+|B|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad \frac{E\times B}{\mu_0c},$$

and the DEC flux is future causal or zero. A charged-dust tensor with $\rho\ge0$ satisfies all four conditions. For a perfect-fluid tensor with rest energy density $\epsilon$ and pressure $p$, the exact pointwise conditions are

$$\mathrm{WEC}\iff \epsilon\ge0\text{ and }\epsilon+p\ge0,\quad \mathrm{NEC}\iff\epsilon+p\ge0,$$

$$\mathrm{SEC}\iff\epsilon+p\ge0\text{ and }\epsilon+3p\ge0,\quad \mathrm{DEC}\iff\epsilon\ge|p|.$$

At a point, finite sums of tensors satisfying any one of these conditions still satisfy that condition; in particular $T_{\mathrm{EM}}+T_m$ satisfies all four for nonnegative dust. No general matter positivity assumption is made, and adding $T_{\mathrm{EM}}$ to an arbitrary fluid need not repair a violated fluid inequality.

items.title: Covariant acceleration along a $C^2$ curve
items.design_state: Complete locally authored definition or conditional proof with all stated hypotheses and explicit dependencies.
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with an affine connection $\nabla$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be any interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]), and let $z:I\to M$ be continuous. We say that $z$ is **$C^2$ on $I$** in this definition when the following chartwise conditions hold. At each interior parameter value $\tau_0\in\operatorname{int}I$, there are a chart $x:U\to x(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ around $z(\tau_0)$ and an open interval $J\subseteq\operatorname{int}I$ containing $\tau_0$, with $z(J)\subseteq U$, such that $x\circ z$ is twice continuously differentiable on $J$. At each included endpoint $\tau_0\in I\setminus\operatorname{int}I$, there are such a chart and a relative neighborhood $J=I\cap(\tau_0-\delta,\tau_0+\delta)$, with $\delta>0$ and $z(J)\subseteq U$, for which the first and second derivatives on $J\cap\operatorname{int}I$ extend continuously to $\tau_0$; their endpoint values are the corresponding one-sided derivatives. Here $n=\dim M$, and differentiability of $x\circ z$ is componentwise as a map of one real variable. Smooth chart transitions and $C^2$ composition make this condition independent of the chosen chart ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]); at an included endpoint, the first- and second-derivative chain-rule expressions have the corresponding continuous one-sided limits. On a time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, this is exactly the curve regularity specified in clause (a) of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]; that definition's causal conditions are not part of the present regularity convention.

The parameter $\tau$ is an arbitrary real parameter here; no causal or nonzero-velocity condition is imposed. Put $U(\tau):=z'(\tau)$, using the one-sided derivative at included endpoints. A **vector field along $z$** assigns $V(\tau)\in T_{z(\tau)}M$ to each $\tau\in I$; it is **continuous** when its component functions are continuous in every chart along $z$. In a chart $x=(x^1,\ldots,x^n)$ covering a segment of $z$, write $U^a(\tau):=\frac{d}{d\tau}(x^a\circ z)(\tau)$ and let $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$. The components $U^a$ transform by the tangent-map Jacobian on chart overlaps, by the chain rule, so $U$ is a vector field along $z$. All indices range from $1$ to $n$, and repeated upper/lower indices are summed. Define the **covariant acceleration of $z$** on this segment by the component formula

$$\bigl(\nabla_UU\bigr)^a(\tau):=\frac{dU^a}{d\tau}(\tau)+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(z(\tau))U^b(\tau)U^c(\tau).$$

The local $C^2$ regularity makes $U^a$ continuously differentiable, including one-sided endpoint derivatives, so these components are continuous on the relative parameter interval. The name and notation extend the pullback covariant derivative of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] from smooth curves; the coordinate expression is well-defined on overlaps by [[lem-emg-c2-curve-covariant-acceleration-well-defined]].

items.title: Killing exchange current and gauge-compensated charged first integral
items.design_state: Complete conditional proof authored. The current Maxwell-stress supplier is a draft with escalated readiness through its action-variation and batch-2 local-potential proof chain; this result remains explicitly conditional and escalated.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an oriented open subset of the time-oriented Lorentzian domain of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $F$ and $j$ be smooth, let $T_m^{ab}$ be smooth and symmetric, and suppose

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b,\qquad \nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c.$$

Let $T_{\mathrm{EM}}$ be the tensor of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]] and assume the exact conditional identity of [[lem-emg-maxwell-stress-divergence]], $\nabla_aT_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}=-F^b{}_cj^c$, under its stated smoothness and source-sign hypotheses. For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on $\Omega$, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, define

$$J_\xi^a=(T_m^{ab}+T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab})\xi_b.$$

Then $\nabla_aJ_\xi^a=0$. If $C$ is a finite smooth singular $4$-chain in $\Omega$ with $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$ for smooth singular $3$-chains, and $\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma)=\int_\Sigma\iota_{J_\xi}\mathrm{vol}_g$, then

$$\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)-\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)=-\mathcal Q_\xi(B).$$

In particular the two slice fluxes are equal when the side flux $\mathcal Q_\xi(B)$ vanishes.

There is also a local test-particle identity. Let $V\subseteq\Omega$ be open, let $A$ be a supplied smooth one-form on $V$ with $F=dA$, and let $\chi$ be a smooth scalar with $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\chi$. If $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is any interval with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and a $C^2$ curve $z:I\to V$ in the sense of clause (a) of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]] has velocity $U=dz/d\tau$ (one-sided at included endpoints), $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and satisfies $m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U)$ with the C$^2$-curve covariant acceleration of [[def-emg-c2-curve-covariant-acceleration]], for constants $m>0,q\in\mathbb R$, where $F^\sharp(U)^a=F^a{}_bU^b$, then

$$C=m g(U,\xi)+q\bigl(A(\xi)-\chi\bigr)$$

is constant along the curve. This is a conditional mathematical identity for a supplied field and an existing curve; it constructs no particle trajectory, global potential, Einstein solution, or point-source self-field.

The transformation law for these antisymmetrized components follows by the chain rule, since the second-derivative chart-transition terms cancel by equality of mixed partials. Define $(\Box A)_b:=g^{ac}
abla_a
abla_c A_b$, $(\operatorname{div}A):=
abla^aA_a$, and $(PA)_b:=\Box A_b-\operatorname{Ric}_b{}^cA_c$. Then

$$

items.title: Finite WKB Maxwell residual, null rays and polarization quotient
items.design_state: Complete finite-parameter proof from the explicit null, transversality, transport and gauge constraints; no WKB-series convergence or exact-solution error is claimed.
items.statement:
Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, metric, connection, curvature sign, length-coordinate SI convention and constants of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Let $\theta\in C^4(U,\mathbb R)$ be dimensionless, set $k:=d\theta$, and assume that $k$ is nowhere zero and $g^{-1}(k,k)=0$. Define the metric dual vector field $k^\sharp$ by $g(k^\sharp,X)=k(X)$ for every tangent vector $X$; in coordinates, $(k^\sharp)^a=g^{ab}k_b$. Let $a_0,a_1\in C^3(U;T^*M\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$; this means that the real and imaginary parts of their coefficients are $C^3$ in every smooth chart. Complex tensor operations and $\nabla$ are extended componentwise and complex-linearly. Define

$$ (\Box a)_b:=g^{ac}\nabla_a\nabla_c a_b,\qquad (Pa)_b:=(\Box a)_b-\operatorname{Ric}_b{}^c a_c,\qquad d_1:=\nabla^a(a_1)_a, $$

and define the first-order operator

$$ (La)_b:=2k^c\nabla_c a_b+(\nabla_c k^c)a_b. $$

Assume pointwise on $U$ that

$$ g^{-1}(k,a_0)=0,\qquad La_0=0,\qquad iLa_1+Pa_0=0,\qquad ik^a(a_1)_a+\nabla^a(a_0)_a=0. $$

These are finite-order ansatz constraints; they assert neither initial data nor a global solution of the transport equations or convergence of a longer series. For $0<\epsilon\le1$, set

$$ A_\epsilon:=\epsilon e^{i\theta/\epsilon}(a_0+\epsilon a_1),\qquad F_\epsilon:=dA_\epsilon. $$

Here $dA_\epsilon$ uses the complex-linear extension of the $C^3$ coordinate definition in [[lem-emg-potential-maxwell-wave-identity]], so $F_\epsilon$ has $C^2$ components. On a $C^2$ two-form $F$, define $dF$ by the $C^1$ three-form components $(dF)_{abc}:=\partial_aF_{bc}+\partial_bF_{ca}+\partial_cF_{ab}$; the antisymmetrized chain rule and equality of mixed second partials make this coordinate definition chart-independent ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]).

Then $dF_\epsilon=0$ and the exact Maxwell divergence residual is

$$ \nabla^a(F_\epsilon)_{ab} =e^{i\theta/\epsilon}\left[-i\epsilon k_b d_1+ \epsilon^2\bigl((Pa_1)_b-\nabla_b d_1\bigr)\right]. $$

The field-strength expansion is also exact:

$$ F_\epsilon=e^{i\theta/\epsilon}\left[ik\wedge a_0+ \epsilon(da_0+ik\wedge a_1)+\epsilon^2da_1\right]. $$

The acronym WKB means Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin; here “finite WKB ansatz” means exactly the phase-amplitude family $A_\epsilon$ just defined, subject to the four pointwise constraints above, and asserts no convergence of a longer series.

For units, take $[k]=\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[a_0]=[a_1]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[d_1]=\mathrm T$, $[Pa_1]=[\nabla d_1]=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$, and $[\epsilon]=[\theta]=1$. Fix a smooth chart $(V,y)$ and a compact set $K\subseteq y(V)$ in its coordinate image. Define

$$ \|S\|_{\infty,K}:= \begin{cases} \max_I\max_{x\in K}|S_I(x)|,&K\ne\varnothing,\\ 0,&K=\varnothing, \end{cases} $$

where $I$ ranges over the finitely many components of the real or complex tensor in that chart. If $K\ne\varnothing$ and finite constants $K_0,D_0,C_0,B_0,B_1\ge0$ satisfy

$$ \|k\|_{\infty,K}\le K_0,\quad \|d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le D_0,\quad \|Pa_1-\nabla d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le C_0,\quad \|da_0+ik\wedge a_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_0,\quad \|da_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_1, $$

then

$$ \|\nabla^a(F_\epsilon)_{ab}\|_{\infty,K} \le\epsilon K_0D_0+\epsilon^2C_0,\qquad \|F_\epsilon-e^{i\theta/\epsilon}ik\wedge a_0\|_{\infty,K} \le\epsilon B_0+\epsilon^2B_1. $$

Taking real parts gives real potentials and fields with the same bounds. Here a local integral curve of $k^\sharp$ means a $C^2$ curve $\gamma:J\to U$, with $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ an open interval, satisfying $\dot\gamma(\lambda)=k^\sharp_{\gamma(\lambda)}$. In length coordinates the parameter $\lambda$ has unit $\mathrm m^2$. An affinely parametrized null geodesic here means a $C^2$ curve with $\dot\gamma(\lambda)\ne0$, $g(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)=0$, and $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma=0$; every such local integral curve is one and lies in a level set of $\theta$. Along each such curve, choose any $\lambda_0\in J$ and any nonzero dimensionless complex initial value $\mathcal A_0\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, and define the scalar transport amplitude

$$ \mathcal A(\lambda)=\mathcal A_0 \exp\left(-\frac12\int_{\lambda_0}^{\lambda}(\nabla_c k^c)(\gamma(s))\,ds\right),\qquad \lambda\in J. $$

The integral is well-defined on each compact segment between $\lambda_0$ and $\lambda$, and $\mathcal A$ is nowhere zero because $\mathcal A_0\ne0$ and the exponential is nonzero. The one-form $e:=a_0/\mathcal A$ is therefore well-defined and satisfies $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}e=0$ and $g^{-1}(k,e)=0$ along the curve; these equations express parallel transport and transversality, respectively. At each $p\in U$, define $k_p^\perp:=\{a\in T_p^*M\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C:g_p^{-1}(k_p,a)=0\}$. Define the leading polarization at $p$ to be the class $[a_0(p)]$ in $k_p^\perp/\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{k_p\}$. This quotient is a two-dimensional complex vector space with the positive Hermitian form induced by $g_p^{-1}$, and for every $\beta\in\mathbb C$ replacing $a_0(p)$ by $a_0(p)+\beta k_p$ leaves $k_p\wedge a_0(p)$ unchanged. If $a_0(p)$ is proportional to $k_p$, the leading field vanishes at $p$. No convergence of a formal series extending the finite ansatz, existence of amplitudes satisfying the constraints, exact-solution error estimate, or extension of the local rays or transport amplitude beyond their stated domains is asserted.

items.statement:
Use the field, stress, matter, unit and curvature conventions of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be constant, and define the Einstein residual for the source-free field model by

$$ \mathscr R_{ab}(g,F;\Lambda):=G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F). $$

Suppose $G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $F_0$ be a smooth real two-form with $dF_0=0$ and $\nabla_a(F_0)^{ab}=0$, the source-free form of the Maxwell equations in [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. For every real dimensionless $\delta$, the field $F_\delta:=\delta F_0$ obeys those same source-free equations and

$$ \mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)=-\kappa\delta^2 T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F_0). $$

This is an exact residual identity on the fixed metric. If $\delta\ne0$ and $F_0$ is nonzero at a point, its observer energy there is positive and the residual is nonzero there; this does not estimate the distance to a different coupled solution.

Separately, let $\rho,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega)$ and a $C^2$ future timelike field $U$ with $g(U,U)=-c^2$ define charged dust on an open $\Omega\subseteq U$, with $\rho>0$, $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$, $j^a=\sigma U^a$, and the formal matter-exchange equation of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. For any dimensionless $\eta>0$, replacing $(\rho,\sigma)$ by $(\eta\rho,\eta\sigma)$ multiplies $T_m$ and $j$ by $\eta$, leaves $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$ unchanged, and leaves the dust acceleration equation $\rho U^a\nabla_aU^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c$ unchanged when the prescribed $F$ and $U$ are held fixed. The sourced Maxwell equation must still match the changed current. If both $F$ and $j$ are scaled by $\eta$, Maxwell's equations remain linear but the electromagnetic stress scales by $\eta^2$, whereas the dust stress scales by $\eta$; no general coupled-solution family follows.

For a flat background with $\Lambda=0$ and $T_m=0$, a nonzero source-free Maxwell field cannot solve the exact Einstein equation with the unchanged Minkowski metric, because its observer energy density is positive somewhere.

Finally, take $M=\mathbb R^4$ with length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and $\mathbf x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$, Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, standard orientation, and future direction $\partial_0$. Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$, and use the Euclidean norm $|\mathbf x|_2=(\sum_{i=1}^3(x^i)^2)^{1/2}$ and Lebesgue volume $d^3x$ in these Cartesian coordinates. Consider only the prescribed Coulomb profile on the finite annulus $\mathcal A_\ell:=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3:\ell<|\mathbf x|_2<2\ell\}$, where $\ell>0$ is a length and $Q\ne0$ is a charge parameter with units $\mathrm C$. Put $r:=|\mathbf x|_2$, $\mathbf e_r:=\mathbf x/r$, $\mathbf E(\mathbf x)=Q(4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2)^{-1}\mathbf e_r$, and $\mathbf B=0$. Its Maxwell energy on that annulus is

$$ \mathcal E_\ell=\int_{\mathcal A_\ell}\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|\mathbf E|^2\,d^3x =\frac{Q^2}{16\pi\varepsilon_0\ell}. $$

Thus this fixed-charge Coulomb cutoff family has diverging shell energy as $\ell\downarrow0$. This finite-annulus calculation asserts no point-source construction, self-field evaluation, or obstruction theorem for arbitrary regularizations.

items.title: Controlled weak/slow charged test trajectory comparison
items.design_state: Complete conditional weak/slow finite-time comparison under explicit uniform metric, field, speed, existence and compact-containment hypotheses; no coupled Einstein–Maxwell family is claimed.
items.statement:
Use the mathematical Lorentzian and SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Fix a length scale $L>0$, a speed $c>0$, a charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ with units $\mathrm C$, and a mass parameter $m>0$ with units $\mathrm{kg}$; set $\alpha:=q/m\ne0$, with units $\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$. Choose $0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_*\le1$. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $\mathcal K\Subset\Omega$ be a compact convex set. Use the Cartesian coordinate domain $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times L\Omega$ with standard orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and use $x^0=ct$, $x^i=LX^i$ with dimensionless $X\in\Omega$. Assume a smooth stationary (independent of $x^0$) Lorentzian metric $g^{(\epsilon)}$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on an open neighborhood of $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times L\mathcal K$ in this domain, with $\partial_0$ chosen future timelike and $t$ increasing along the considered curves, whose components have the form

$$ g_{00}^{(\epsilon)}(X)=-(1+2\epsilon\phi(X))+r_{00}^{(\epsilon)}(X),\qquad g_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}(X)=(1-2\epsilon\phi(X))\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}(X),\qquad g_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}(X)=r_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}(X). $$

Here $\phi$ is dimensionless and smooth. A spatial multi-index is $\beta=(\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3)\in\mathbb N_0^3$, with $|\beta|=\beta_1+\beta_2+\beta_3$ and $\partial_X^\beta:=\partial_{X^1}^{\beta_1}\partial_{X^2}^{\beta_2}\partial_{X^3}^{\beta_3}$. For each such $\beta$ with $|\beta|\le2$, assume the uniform bounds

$$ |\partial_X^\beta r_{00}^{(\epsilon)}|+ \max_{i,j}|\partial_X^\beta r_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}| \le C_g\epsilon^2,\qquad \max_i|\partial_X^\beta r_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}|\le C_g\epsilon^{3/2} $$

on $\mathcal K$, with a fixed finite nonnegative $C_g$. Let $\mathbf e,\mathbf b:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be smooth dimensionless fields whose values and first derivatives are bounded on $\mathcal K$. Since $\mathcal K$ is compact, the fixed smooth function $\phi$ and its derivatives used below are also bounded there. Prescribe a smooth stationary (independent of $x^0$) real two-form $F^{(\epsilon)}$ by its Cartesian components

$$ F_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}=-E_i^{(\epsilon)}/c,\qquad F_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k^{(\epsilon)},\qquad \alpha\mathbf E^{(\epsilon)}(X)=\frac{\epsilon c^2}{L}\mathbf e(X),\qquad \alpha\mathbf B^{(\epsilon)}(X)=\frac{\sqrt\epsilon\,c}{L}\mathbf b(X). $$

No Maxwell or Einstein equation for this prescribed background field or metric is assumed. Define the dimensionless potential $\phi$ comparison system on $S\in[0,S_*]$ by

$$ \frac{d\mathbf X_N}{dS}=\mathbf W_N,\qquad \frac{d\mathbf W_N}{dS}=-\nabla_X\phi(\mathbf X_N)+\mathbf e(\mathbf X_N)+\mathbf W_N\times\mathbf b(\mathbf X_N), $$

where $(\mathbf u\times\mathbf v)_i:=\sum_{j,k}\epsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$. Let $f(\mathbf X,\mathbf W)$ denote the six-component right-hand side of this system. Assume that on a compact convex state set $\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathcal K\times\mathbb R^3$, containing both trajectories, its derivative satisfies $\|Df\|_{1\to1}\le L_f$ for a finite nonnegative $L_f$. Here $\|(\mathbf X,\mathbf W)\|_1$ is the sum of the absolute values of its six real components, and $\|Df\|_{1\to1}$ is the operator norm induced by this $\ell^1$ norm.

For each $\epsilon$, let $z_\epsilon$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve, parameterized by proper time $\tau$ as in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]], that solves the prescribed external Lorentz equation

$$ \nabla_U U=\alpha F^{(\epsilon)\sharp}(U),\qquad g^{(\epsilon)}(U,U)=-c^2,\qquad U=\frac{dz_\epsilon}{d\tau}. $$

Write its coordinate velocity as $\mathbf w=d\mathbf x/dt$ and assume $|\mathbf w|\le C_v\sqrt\epsilon\,c$ on $[0,S_*]$ for a fixed finite $C_v$. Suppose the relativistic scaled trajectory $(\mathbf X_\epsilon,\mathbf W_\epsilon)$ and the comparison trajectory $(\mathbf X_N,\mathbf W_N)$ exist throughout $[0,S_*]$, remain in $\mathcal Q$, and have the same initial data, where

$$ \mathbf X:=\mathbf x/L,\qquad \mathbf W:=\mathbf w/(\sqrt\epsilon\,c),\qquad S:=\sqrt\epsilon\,ct/L. $$

Then, after choosing $\epsilon_*>0$ sufficiently small in terms of the stated uniform constants, the exact relativistic trajectory satisfies

$$ \frac{d\mathbf X_\epsilon}{dS}=\mathbf W_\epsilon,\qquad \frac{d\mathbf W_\epsilon}{dS} =-\nabla_X\phi(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf e(\mathbf X_\epsilon) +\mathbf W_\epsilon\times\mathbf b(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf r_\epsilon(S), \qquad \|\mathbf r_\epsilon(S)\|_1\le C_r\epsilon, $$

where $C_r$ depends only on the displayed uniform bounds and the fixed coefficient bounds on $\mathcal K$, and is independent of $\epsilon$. Consequently,

$$ \sup_{0\le S\le S_*}\left(\|\mathbf X_\epsilon(S)-\mathbf X_N(S)\|_1+ \|\mathbf W_\epsilon(S)-\mathbf W_N(S)\|_1\right) \le C_r\epsilon S_*e^{L_fS_*}. $$

The estimate is conditional on existence and common compact containment through the specified finite scaled interval. It does not construct such a long-time family, solve Maxwell's equations for the prescribed fields, or produce a coupled Einstein–Maxwell family. In particular the $\sqrt\epsilon$ magnetic scaling can fail a coupled Einstein stress hierarchy unless additional matter scales are supplied.

items.title: Exact finite-frequency transverse Maxwell field
items.design_state: Complete exact ideal plane-wave component calculation and source-free Maxwell verification; the unchanged flat metric is explicitly not claimed to solve the coupled equation.
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ have length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,z)$, Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dz$, and future direction $\partial_0$, with $x^0=ct$. Choose constants $\nu>0$ with units $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $A_*\ne0$ with potential-component units $\mathrm{T\,m}$. For $0<\epsilon\le1$, set

$$ \theta=\nu(x^0-z),\qquad a_0=A_*\,dx^1,\qquad a_1=0,\qquad A_\epsilon^{\mathbb R}:=\operatorname{Re}\left(\epsilon e^{i\theta/\epsilon}a_0\right). $$

Then the real potential and field are

$$ A_\epsilon^{\mathbb R}=\epsilon A_*\cos(\theta/\epsilon)\,dx^1,\qquad (F_\epsilon)_{01}=-\nu A_*\sin(\theta/\epsilon),\qquad (F_\epsilon)_{31}=+\nu A_*\sin(\theta/\epsilon), $$

with all other independent field components zero. Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$, $\mathbf x=(x^1,x^2,z)$ and $t=x^0/c$. The corresponding smooth spatial fields $\mathbf E,\mathbf B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ are

$$ \mathbf E(\mathbf x,t)=c\nu A_*\sin\!\left(\frac{\nu(ct-z)}{\epsilon}\right)\mathbf e_1,\qquad \mathbf B(\mathbf x,t)=\nu A_*\sin\!\left(\frac{\nu(ct-z)}{\epsilon}\right)\mathbf e_2, $$

where $\mathbf e_1=(1,0,0)$ and $\mathbf e_2=(0,1,0)$, with units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm T$, respectively. These are the SI fields of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. This is an exact source-free Maxwell field for every fixed $\epsilon$. For $A_*\ne0$ it has nonzero electromagnetic stress on an open set, so it is not a fully coupled source-free Einstein–Maxwell solution on unchanged Minkowski space with $\Lambda=0$.

items.title: Constant magnetic slow-orbit error
items.design_state: Complete exact constant-magnetic relativistic orbit and finite-time scaled comparison; the field is a prescribed test background.
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ with global length coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,z)$, $x^0=ct$, Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dz$, and future direction $\partial_0$. Use the SI convention of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Write $\mathbf e_z:=(0,0,1)$ and use the Euclidean product $\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v:=\sum_{j=1}^3u_jv_j$, norm $|\mathbf u|_2:=\sqrt{\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf u}$, and orthogonality convention $\mathbf u\perp\mathbf v$ iff $\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v=0$. Let $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$ and $I=\mathbb R$, and write $\mathbf x=(x^1,x^2,z)$. Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a charge parameter with units $\mathrm C$ and $m>0$ a mass parameter with units $\mathrm{kg}$; set $\alpha:=q/m\ne0$, with units $\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$. Let dimensionless $b_0\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and length $L>0$. For dimensionless $0<\epsilon\le1$, define smooth fields $\mathbf E,\mathbf B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ by

$$ \mathbf E(\mathbf x,t)=0,\qquad \alpha\mathbf B(\mathbf x,t)=\frac{\sqrt\epsilon\,c}{L}b_0\mathbf e_z,\qquad 0<\epsilon\le1. $$

Here $[\mathbf E]=\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and $[\mathbf B]=\mathrm T$; the corresponding smooth two-form on $\mathbb R^4$ is specified by $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$.

Choose a dimensionless initial velocity $\mathbf W_0\perp\mathbf e_z$ with $\epsilon|\mathbf W_0|_2^2\le\tfrac12$, and put $\mathbf w_0=\sqrt\epsilon\,c\mathbf W_0$. Let the exact relativistic trajectory and the weak/slow comparison trajectory have the same initial position and velocity at $S=0$. On every finite interval $0\le S\le S_*$, where $S=\sqrt\epsilon\,ct/L$ and both trajectories are followed, their dimensionless velocities and positions satisfy

$$ |\mathbf W(S)-\mathbf W_N(S)|_2 \le |b_0|\epsilon|\mathbf W_0|_2^3S,\qquad |\mathbf X(S)-\mathbf X_N(S)|_2 \le \frac12|b_0|\epsilon|\mathbf W_0|_2^3S^2. $$

Here $\mathbf X=\mathbf x/L$, $\mathbf W=\mathbf w/(\sqrt\epsilon c)$, a prime denotes $d/dS$, and the comparison equation is $\mathbf X_N'=\mathbf W_N$, $\mathbf W_N'=b_0\mathbf W_N\times\mathbf e_z$. For $\vartheta\in\mathbb R$, define $R_z(\vartheta):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\vartheta&-\sin\vartheta&0\\\sin\vartheta&\cos\vartheta&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$. The uniform magnetic field is a prescribed test background: these orbit calculations do not assert an exact coupled Einstein–Maxwell solution on unchanged Minkowski space.

items.title: Positive-scalar conformastatic chart data
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $H:D\to(0,\infty)$ be of class $C^3$, meaning that every partial derivative of total order at most three exists and is continuous. Set $\mathcal M:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$, an open subset of $\mathbb R^4$, with global coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$; each coordinate is assigned length units, with $x^0=ct$ when a time coordinate is wanted. The function $H$ depends only on $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and is dimensionless.

Give $\mathcal M$ the coordinate orientation determined by $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

Define the symmetric coordinate tensor $g_H$ by
$$g_H=-H^{-2}(dx^0)^2+H^2\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2,$$
where $H^{-1}:=1/H$ and $H^{-2}:=(1/H)^2$. This exact coordinate form is called the positive-scalar conformastatic chart tensor in this item; no field equation or physical solution property is part of the definition.

For this $C^3$ chart tensor, a **time orientation** means a continuous selection at each $p\in\mathcal M$ of one of the two connected components of $\{v\in T_p\mathcal M:g_H(v,v)<0\}$, with the topology from the coordinate identification $T\mathcal M=\mathcal M\times\mathbb R^4$. Specify the selection globally by
$$C_p^+:=\left\{v=v^0\partial_0+\sum_{i=1}^3v^i\partial_i:g_H(v,v)<0,\ v^0>0\right\}.$$
Here the selection is continuous in the explicit sense that the fiberwise linear coordinate map $(p,v)\mapsto(p,v^0/H(p),H(p)v^1,H(p)v^2,H(p)v^3)$ is a continuous bundle isomorphism carrying $C^+$ to the constant cone $\{(u^0,\mathbf u):u^0>\|\mathbf u\|_2\}$; this map and its inverse are $C^3$. That cone and its negative are convex and nonempty, and a timelike vector has nonzero $u^0$, so they are exactly the two timelike components. Define a nonzero causal vector by $g_H(v,v)\le0$ and call it **future-directed** when $v^0>0$. Set $N_H:=H\partial_0$, a $C^3$ vector field (smooth if $H$ is smooth). The Lorentzian lemma below verifies $g_H(N_H,N_H)=-1$, so $N_H\in C_p^+$ everywhere. No smoothness beyond $C^3$ is required for this definition.


Because $H>0$, the functions $H^{-1}$ and $H^{-2}$ are compositions and products of $H$ with positive-base powers of exponents $-1$ and $-2$. The derivative formula for these powers, repeated through any finite order, and closure of $C^k$ functions under composition and finite products show that the displayed coefficients are $C^3$ when $H$ is $C^3$, and smooth when $H$ is smooth.

For later component formulas define $H_i:=\partial_iH$, $H_{ij}:=\partial_i\partial_jH$, $q:=\sum_{i=1}^3H_i^2$, and $\Delta H:=\sum_{i=1}^3H_{ii}$.

items.title: The positive-scalar conformastatic chart tensor is Lorentzian
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement: For every $D,H,g_H$ in [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]], the coordinate tensor $g_H$ is a C3 nondegenerate Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Its inverse components are $g^{00}=-H^2$ and $g^{ij}=H^{-2}\delta_{ij}$, its determinant is $-H^4$, and $\sqrt{|\det g|}=H^2$. The vector fields $n:=H\partial_0$ and $e_i:=H^{-1}\partial_i$ form a global orthonormal frame with $g(n,n)=-1$, $g(n,e_i)=0$, and $g(e_i,e_j)=\delta_{ij}$. The chosen time orientation makes $n$ future-directed, and the frame $(n,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is positively oriented.

items.title: Exact smooth superharmonic counterpoised dust family
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in [[def-countable-choice]], as required by the currently inspected general geometric convention in [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $H\in C^\infty(D,(0,\infty))$ satisfy $\Delta H\le0$. Use $\mathcal M=\mathbb R\times D$, its coordinate orientation, and the time orientation for which $n:=H\partial_0$ is future, all as fixed in [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]] and verified in [[lem-emg-conformastatic-chart-is-lorentzian]]. Use the metric $g_H$ and coordinates $x^0=ct,x^i$ of [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]]. Fix formal constants $c,\mu_0,G_N>0$, put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$, and define the positive charge-to-mass parameter $Q_s:=\sqrt{4\pi\epsilon_0G_N}$ using the positive root of [[def-emg-explicit-power-regimes]]. For a sign $s\in\{-1,+1\}$ set
$$A:=s\frac{c}{Q_s}H^{-1}dx^0,\qquad F:=dA,\qquad U:=cH\partial_0,\qquad \rho:=-\frac{c^2\Delta H}{4\pi G_NH^3},\qquad \sigma:=sQ_s\rho,\qquad j:=\sigma U,\qquad T_m^{ab}:=\rho U^aU^b.$$
Let $a^b:=U^a\nabla_aU^b$ be the covariant four-acceleration of the timelike field $U$. Then $U=cn$ is future timelike with $g_H(U,U)=-c^2$, all displayed fields are smooth, and $\rho\ge0$. On $\{\rho>0\}$ the charge-to-mass ratio is $\sigma/\rho=sQ_s$; no ratio is defined by division at $\rho=0$. The tuple satisfies the formal sourced Maxwell equations $dF=0$, $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, the dust matter exchange equation $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$, and the formal Einstein equation with $\Lambda=0$,
$$G_{ab}=\kappa\bigl(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}\bigr),$$
where $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ is exactly the tensor of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Its total stress satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC, and DEC. The coordinate four-acceleration of the static dust field is $a^0=0$, $a^i=-c^2H_i/H^3$, and its Lorentz force per unit mass balances it wherever $\rho>0$; the undivided exchange identity also holds where $\rho=0$.

This is a conditional mathematical solution family for the stated formal equations. It makes no claim of physical realization, equilibrium stability, or coupled-field existence for arbitrary initial data.

items.title: Globally regular sphere, proper integrals and dilute bounds
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as stated in [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $a,b>0$ have length units, let $s\in\{-1,+1\}$, and on all of $\mathbb R^3$ set
$$r^2=(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2,\qquad \Psi(x):=\sqrt{r^2+b^2}>0,\qquad H(x):=1+\frac a{\Psi(x)}.$$
Use the constants and exact formal coupled family of [[thm-emg-smooth-counterpoised-dust]]. The function $H$ is smooth, positive, and satisfies
$$\Delta H=-\frac{3ab^2}{(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}}<0,\qquad \rho(x)=\frac{3c^2ab^2}{4\pi G_NH(x)^3(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}}.$$
On the slice $x^0=\text{constant}$ the induced spatial metric is $h=H^2\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j$. Define the candidate proper mass and signed charge by
$$M_{\mathrm{prop}}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho H^3\,d\lambda_3,\qquad Q_{\mathrm{prop}}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sigma H^3\,d\lambda_3.$$
The proof establishes that the first is a finite nonnegative Lebesgue integral and the second is a finite signed Lebesgue integral. They equal
$$M_{\mathrm{prop}}=\frac{c^2a}{G_N},\qquad Q_{\mathrm{prop}}=sQ_s\frac{c^2a}{G_N}.$$
The scalar curvature is $S_g=-2\Delta H/H^3>0$, the total stress satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC, and DEC, and the smooth matter density is positive at every point and has infinite spatial extent. For $a=\delta b$ with $0<\delta\le1$, put $h_0(x):=b/\sqrt{r^2+b^2}$ and
$$\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}(x):=\frac{3c^2\delta b^3}{4\pi G_N(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}}.$$
The same exact coupled solutions obey the pointwise Cartesian-coordinate bounds
$$\left|g_{00}+\bigl(1-2\delta h_0\bigr)\right|\le3\delta^2,\qquad \left|g_{ij}-\bigl(1+2\delta h_0\bigr)\delta_{ij}\right|\le\delta^2,\qquad 0\le1-\frac{\rho}{\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}}\le3\delta.$$
These are ideal mathematical estimates, not measurements or stability statements.

items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $b>0$ have length units, let $\mathbf{x}=(x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^3$, and define its Euclidean radius by $r:=\sqrt{(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}$. Take $a=b$ and $s=+1$ in the exact family of [[thm-emg-smooth-counterpoised-dust]], and define $H(\mathbf{x})=1+b/\sqrt{r^2+b^2}$ on all of $\mathbb R^3$. For the family field strength $F$, set $n:=H\partial_0$, $e_i:=H^{-1}\partial_i$, and define the static-frame electric components by $E_i:=cF(e_i,n)$ for $i=1,2,3$. This is an everywhere regular smooth solution with center values
$$H(0)=2,\qquad \nabla H(0)=0,\qquad \Delta H(0)=-\frac3{b^2},\qquad \rho(0)=\frac{3c^2}{32\pi G_Nb^2},\qquad S_g(0)=\frac3{4b^2},\qquad E_i(0)=0.$$
Its proper mass and signed charge are $c^2b/G_N$ and $Q_sc^2b/G_N$, respectively. The model density is positive everywhere, so its topological support, defined as the closure in $\mathbb R^3$ of $\{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb R^3:\rho(\mathbf{x})\ne0\}$, is all of $\mathbb R^3$.

items.title: Quantified dilute exact coupled family
items.design_state: Complete local definition or conditional proof authored with the exact planned claim and stated mathematical hypotheses.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $b>0$ have length units and let $\delta$ be dimensionless with $0<\delta\le1/10$. Put $a=\delta b$ and choose either charge sign $s\in\{-1,+1\}$ in the exact coupled family. For $\mathbf{x}=(x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^3$, define the Euclidean radius $r:=\sqrt{(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}$ and $h_0(\mathbf{x}):=b/\sqrt{r^2+b^2}$, so $H=1+\delta h_0$. Then
$$\left|g_{00}+\bigl(1-2\delta h_0\bigr)\right|\le3\delta^2\le\frac3{100},\qquad \left|g_{ij}-\bigl(1+2\delta h_0\bigr)\delta_{ij}\right|\le\delta^2\le\frac1{100},\qquad 0\le1-\frac{\rho}{\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}}\le3\delta\le\frac3{10},$$
where $\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}=3c^2\delta b^3/[4\pi G_N(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}]$. These are exact ideal-family bounds, not measured errors. On $\mathcal M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times\mathbb R^3$, the static dust velocity field is $U=cH\partial_0$. For each fixed $\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb R^3$ and $x^0_*\in\mathbb R$, define its static worldline by
$$\gamma_{\mathbf{x},x^0_*}:\mathbb R\to\mathcal M,\qquad \gamma_{\mathbf{x},x^0_*}(\tau):=(x^0_*+cH(\mathbf{x})\tau,\mathbf{x}).$$
This is a smooth future-directed timelike curve with $\dot\gamma=U$ and $g_H(\dot\gamma,\dot\gamma)=-c^2$; $\tau\in\mathbb R$, measured in seconds, is its proper-time parameter in the adopted length-coordinate convention. Here a static worldline is freely falling exactly when it is a geodesic, $\nabla_{\dot\gamma}\dot\gamma=0$, with $\nabla$ the connection of the exact family. Define the model's electromagnetic force per unit mass by $f^b:=(\sigma/\rho)F^b{}_cU^c$; this is defined everywhere for this profile since $\rho>0$. For this profile, $H_i=-\delta b x^i/(r^2+b^2)^{3/2}$, so when $r>0$ both $a^i$ and $f^i$ are nonzero and $a^i=f^i$. At $r=0$ both vectors vanish, and the central static worldline is geodesic.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an open subset of the smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N,o)$ of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and metric-selected Levi–Civita connection $\nabla$. The exact tensor types, formal matter systems, stress convention, observer conventions and smoothness levels below are those of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Use SI units with length coordinates $x^0=ct$ as in [[def-emg-geometry-units]]; no numerical value of the experimentally determined $\mu_0$ is treated as exact.

At a point $p\in\Omega$, an **observer** is a future-directed unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ satisfying $g(n,n)=-1$. A smooth field of such vectors is an **observer congruence**. A tetrad is a basis of a tangent space; an observer, a congruence, a tetrad and a coordinate chart are different objects. A **four-velocity field** $U$ is a $C^2$ future-timelike vector field with $g(U,U)=-c^2$; $n=U/c$ is its unit observer at each point. A **proper-time worldline segment** is a $C^2$ future-directed timelike curve $z:I\to\Omega$ on an interval $I$ of proper time $\tau$ in seconds, with $dz/d\tau=U$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$ along the segment. These are local model fields and curves; no global flow or completeness is included.

The matter variables are constitutive inputs of a selected model: rest-mass density $\rho$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, rest-charge density $\sigma$ in $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, rest-energy density $\epsilon$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and isotropic pressure $p$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. A smooth matter current $j^a$ has units $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, and a symmetric matter stress tensor $T_m^{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ in the stated length-coordinate convention. Their physical meanings are fixed only after a constitutive branch is selected:

- For charged dust, $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$ and $j^a=\sigma U^a$. Here $\rho\geq0$ is rest-mass density, not energy density.
- For a perfect fluid, $T_m^{ab}=(\epsilon+p)U^aU^b/c^2+pg^{ab}$. Its rest-frame entries are $(\epsilon,p,p,p)$. No equation of state is included by this tensor definition.
- An optional conducting-fluid current is $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$, where $q^aU_a=0$ and $q^a$ is a rest-space conduction-current density in $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. The separate constitutive choice $q^a=\chi E_U^a$ uses a scalar conductivity $\chi\geq0$ in $\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$ and is not part of the general definition.

For a smooth real electromagnetic two-form $F$ and positive $\mu_0$, define the electromagnetic stress by

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd}.$$

The components of $F$ in an orthonormal tetrad have tesla units. For an observer $n$, the observer electric field is $E_n^a:=cF^a{}_bn^b$ in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$; with $U=cn$, write $E_U^a:=F^a{}_bU^b=E_n^a$. The observer magnetic field is the spatial covector $B_{n,a}:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b$ in tesla, with the orientation and Hodge convention of [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. These observer fields depend on $n$; they are not global observer-independent three-vectors.

Define the matter-plus-field force density by $f^a:=F^a{}_bj^b$, in $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, and the matter exchange equation by $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=f^b$. This equation is a condition of a selected coupled model, not a consequence of the tensor definitions alone. For any unit observer $n$, define the measured energy density of a symmetric stress tensor $T_{ab}$ by $\mathcal E_n:=T_{ab}n^an^b$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. Define its spatial energy-current vector by $\mathcal S_n^a:=-h_n{}^a{}_cT^c{}_bn^b$, where $h_n{}^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$ projects to $n^\perp$; its orthonormal-frame physical energy flux is $c\mathcal S_n^i$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. These contractions are derived, observer-dependent quantities.

Within the selected Einstein–Maxwell formulation, the fields $g$ and $F$ may be dynamical unknowns in a coupled branch or prescribed data in a test branch. The matter variables $\rho,\sigma,\epsilon,p$ and any chosen conductivity or equation of state are independent constitutive input. The current, stress, force density, electromagnetic stress, observer fields and observer contractions are derived from those inputs by the displayed definitions. This definition makes no identification with Newtonian or thermodynamic quantities solely because units agree; it records no measurement and asserts no matter evolution, entropy law, or coupled Einstein–Maxwell solution.

items.statement:
On an open region $\Omega$ of the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime and SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-observables]], adopt the equation-based Einstein and smooth curved Maxwell systems of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] and [[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]], with the smooth matter quantities and electromagnetic stress of [[def-emg-matter-observables]]. Thus the coupled branch includes the adopted Einstein equation $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=(8\pi G_N/c^4)(T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab})$ and Maxwell equations $dF=0$, $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, using the fixed local SI signs, units and curvature convention of those suppliers. Their adopted equations remain physical assumptions; neither is deduced here from flat spacetime, variational stationarity, or mathematical structure.

Choose smooth $\rho,\sigma,U$ on $\Omega$, with $\rho\geq0$, $U$ future timelike, $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and $\sigma=0$ wherever $\rho=0$. Select the pressureless dust closure

$$T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b,\qquad j^a=\sigma U^a.$$

As the matter model, adopt the undivided smooth mass and Lorentz-force equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho U^a)=0,\qquad \rho U^a\nabla_aU^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c,$$

and charge-current conservation $\nabla_aj^a=0$. On each open region $\Omega_+:=\{p\in\Omega:\rho(p)>0\}$ define $\alpha:=\sigma/\rho$. Under the adopted mass continuity and charged-dust forms, [[thm-emg-charged-dust-projection]] gives the exact equivalence between charge-current conservation and transport $U^a\nabla_a\alpha=0$. The ratio is not defined and no division is made on $\rho=0$. This ratio statement is restricted to $\Omega_+$; no global coupled evolution theorem is asserted.

This is a selected classical pressureless continuum model with one four-velocity field $U$ on the stated smooth domain. It excludes viscosity, conduction, multistream averaging, spin, point sources, self-field products and a general dust action. The finely fixed charge-to-mass ratio used in the specific ECD solutions of Meinel and Hütten is not a law of this general model. The postulate asserts neither a global smooth continuation nor validity of a single-velocity description beyond the stated domain; it makes no coupled-solution existence, uniqueness, stability, or empirical claim.

items.statement:
On a smooth open state domain $\Omega$ in the spacetime and SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-observables]], choose $C^1$ rest-energy density $\epsilon>0$, pressure $p$, rest-charge density $\sigma$, and a $C^2$ future-timelike field $U$ with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. The equation-based coupled branch uses [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] and [[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]] with a smooth symmetric matter tensor and current supplied by this selected fluid model. Adopt the perfect-fluid tensor

$$T_m^{ab}=\frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}U^aU^b+pg^{ab}$$

and either the convective current $j^a=\sigma U^a$ or a separately specified conduction current $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$ with $q^aU_a=0$. Adopt charge continuity $\nabla_aj^a=0$ and the local matter-exchange balance $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$. The fields and derivatives are smooth enough for these equations to hold pointwise.

For an optional Ohmic branch, choose a smooth scalar conductivity $\chi\geq0$ in $\mathrm{S\,m^{-1}}$ and impose $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, where $E_U^a=F^a{}_bU^b$ is the rest-frame electric field in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$. This is a separate constitutive adoption, not a consequence of covariance or of the Maxwell equations. A smooth equation of state may be supplied on the chosen local state domain; no particular function, relativistic entropy law, causality assertion, or thermodynamic interpretation of $\epsilon,p$ is included here. The stress-projection and comoving work identities follow conditionally from [[thm-emg-charged-fluid-projections]], but no global fluid or conducting-fluid solution theory is asserted.

This postulate adopts a local classical matter branch. It does not presume an unspecified matter action or infer empirical validity from the source literature.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega_+\subseteq\Omega$ be an open positive-density region of the charged-dust model in [[post-emg-transported-charged-dust]]. Let $\rho,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega_+,\mathbb R)$ with $\rho>0$, let $U\in C^2(\Omega_+,T\Omega_+)$ be future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$, and let the smooth electromagnetic two-form and metric be those of that model. Set $a^b:=U^a\nabla_aU^b$, $T_m^{ab}:=\rho U^aU^b$, and $j^a:=\sigma U^a$.

On $\Omega_+$ the adopted charged-dust matter-exchange equation $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$ is equivalent to

$$\nabla_a(\rho U^a)=0,\qquad \rho a^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c.$$

Under the mass-continuity equation, $\nabla_aj^a=0$ is equivalent to transport of the charge-to-mass ratio $\alpha:=\sigma/\rho$ along the flow, $U^a\nabla_a\alpha=0$. These are model deductions on $\Omega_+$; the ratio and the divided force law are not defined at zero density. The result is local to its stated smooth positive-density domain and asserts neither a global smooth continuation nor validity of the single-velocity model beyond that domain. It supplies no Maxwell or Einstein solution or coupled-field existence theorem.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a smooth open state domain of [[post-emg-charged-fluid-balance]]. Assume $\epsilon,p,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega,\mathbb R)$, $U\in C^2(\Omega,T\Omega)$ is future timelike with $g(U,U)=-c^2$, $F$ is a smooth electromagnetic two-form, and the matter stress and current satisfy the selected fluid closure and exchange equation. Define

$$D:=U^a\nabla_a,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_aU^a,\qquad a^b:=DU^b,\qquad h^b{}_c:=\delta^b{}_c+\frac{U^bU_c}{c^2},\qquad f^b:=F^b{}_cj^c,\qquad E_U^a:=F^a{}_bU^b.$$

Then the longitudinal work and rest-space force equations are

$$D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\theta=-U_bf^b,\qquad \frac{\epsilon+p}{c^2}a^b+h^{ba}\nabla_ap=h^b{}_cf^c.$$

For the convective branch $j^a=\sigma U^a$, the comoving electromagnetic work $-U_bf^b$ is zero. For the optional smooth Ohmic branch $j^a=\sigma U^a+q^a$, $q^a=\chi E_U^a$, with $\chi\geq0$, it is

$$-U_bf^b=\chi\,g(E_U,E_U)\geq0.$$

Here $E_U$ is the rest-frame electric field and the induced metric on $U^\perp$ is positive definite. This is a conditional mechanical energy identity; it does not assert an entropy-production law, equation-of-state evolution, causal constitutive theory, or fluid existence.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega_+$ be a smooth positive-density region of the selected charged-dust model, and require $F,j,T_m$ to satisfy the smoothness hypotheses of the Maxwell-stress and Killing-current suppliers. Assume the dust fields satisfy the model equations and the conditional matter-exchange identity of [[pthm-emg-dust-mass-force-reduction]], and assume the smooth Maxwell equations of [[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]]. Define $T_{\mathrm{tot}}^{ab}:=T_m^{ab}+T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}$. Let $\xi$ be a smooth Killing field on $\Omega_+$, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, and set $J_\xi^a:=T_{\mathrm{tot}}^{ab}\xi_b$. For any finite smooth singular $4$-chain $C$ in $\Omega_+$ with boundary $\partial C=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$, define $\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma):=\int_\Sigma\iota_{J_\xi}\mathrm{vol}_g$. Then

$$\nabla_aT_{\mathrm{tot}}^{ab}=0,\qquad \nabla_aJ_\xi^a=0,\qquad \mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)-\mathcal Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)=-\mathcal Q_\xi(B).$$

The two slice charges are equal only when the side flux $\mathcal Q_\xi(B)$ vanishes. This is a matter-plus-electromagnetic stress current, not a local gravitational-energy tensor; no asymptotic or universal global energy is asserted.

There is also the following separate test-body clause. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure. On a local potential domain $V\subseteq\Omega_+$, let $A$ be a supplied smooth one-form with $F=dA$ and let $\chi$ be a smooth scalar such that $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\chi$. Let $z:[a,b]\to V$ be a finite $C^2$ future-timelike curve segment, parameterized by proper time $\tau$, with fixed-endpoint variations as in [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]]. If the segment is stationary for that adopted action, then [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]] gives $m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U)$ for its constant $m>0$, $q\in\mathbb R$, and $U=dz/d\tau$. Consequently

$$C_\xi:=m\,g(U,\xi)+q\bigl(A(\xi)-\chi\bigr)$$

is constant along the segment and is invariant under $A\mapsto A+d\lambda$, $\chi\mapsto\chi+\mathcal L_\xi\lambda$. This conditional test-body identity uses no self-field, global potential, trajectory-existence, or Einstein-solution claim.

items.statement:
Use the smooth electromagnetic stress, observer contractions and selected matter tensors of [[def-emg-matter-observables]], with $\mu_0>0$ and a future unit observer $n$. The electromagnetic tensor is symmetric and trace-free, and it satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC and DEC. In a positively oriented orthonormal rest tetrad, with the cross product taken in the oriented Euclidean rest space, its energy density and spatial energy-current components are

$$u=\frac{\epsilon_0|E_n|^2+|B_n|^2/\mu_0}{2},\qquad \mathcal S_n=\frac{E_n\times B_n}{\mu_0c}.$$

For charged dust with $\rho\geq0$, the matter tensor and its sum with the electromagnetic tensor satisfy all four conditions. For a selected perfect-fluid tensor with rest energy density $\epsilon$ and pressure $p$, the exact pointwise conditions on the matter tensor are

$$\mathrm{WEC}\iff \epsilon\geq0\text{ and }\epsilon+p\geq0,\qquad \mathrm{NEC}\iff\epsilon+p\geq0,$$

$$\mathrm{SEC}\iff\epsilon+p\geq0\text{ and }\epsilon+3p\geq0,\qquad \mathrm{DEC}\iff\epsilon\geq|p|.$$

If the perfect-fluid tensor satisfies any one of these conditions, adding the electromagnetic tensor preserves that condition. The inequalities are not assumed universally, and adding the electromagnetic tensor to arbitrary matter need not repair a violated condition.

items.title: Pure magnetic anisotropic stress and null-flux equality
items.physical_scope: Two exact pointwise electromagnetic-stress calculations in an orthonormal observer frame: a pure magnetic field has anisotropic principal stresses, and crossed equal-normalized electric and magnetic fields saturate the DEC flux bound. These are ideal local/test-background calculations, not measurements or full coupled Einstein–Maxwell solutions.

items.statement:
At a point in a Minkowski orthonormal observer frame, use the SI electromagnetic stress and observer conventions of [[def-emg-matter-observables]].

For a pure magnetic field $E=0$, $B=B_0e_3$ with $B_0\neq0$, the energy density is $u=B_0^2/(2\mu_0)$, the energy current is $(u,0,0,0)$, and the spatial principal stresses are $(u,u,-u)$. The tensor is trace-free, obeys WEC, NEC, SEC and DEC, and is not an isotropic perfect-fluid stress because $u\neq -u$.

For crossed fields $E=E_0e_1$, $B=(E_0/c)e_2$ with $E_0\neq0$, the energy density is $u=E_0^2/(\mu_0c^2)$ and the spatial energy current is $u e_3$. The observer energy-current four-vector is therefore null, so the DEC causal-flux inequality is saturated. Both calculations are exact ideal tensor evaluations at an observer event; they are not experimental reports or claims that the fields solve the full Einstein equation on an unchanged Minkowski metric.

items.statement:
On an open region of the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime and length-coordinate SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-observables]], adopt a prescribed-background Maxwell model. The metric $g$ is fixed input. Choose a real $C^2$ electromagnetic two-form $F$ and either adopt the source-free equations $dF=0$ and $d(\star_gF)=0$, or supply a $C^1$ current $j$ and adopt $dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, with the exact signs and units of that definition. The source current is prescribed independently of the probe; this postulate does not impose an Einstein equation, matter evolution equation, or field equation for the sources on the unchanged metric.

For a massive charged probe, use the adopted local action and finite-curve conditions of [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]]: $m>0$ and $q$ are constant, the path is a $C^2$ future-directed timelike segment parameterized by proper time, and its endpoints are fixed in variations supported in a local potential domain $V$ with a supplied $C^2$ one-form $A$ satisfying $dA=F$. The potential and metric are external data independent of the path. Under the exact hypotheses of [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]], action stationarity is equivalent to $m\nabla_UU=qF^\sharp(U)$; that theorem's $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption is inherited only when this equivalent force-law formulation is used. No global potential or trajectory is included.

The probe's own singular field and self-gravity are excluded. No radiation reaction, variable mass or charge, finite-body model, or backreaction estimate is adopted. In particular, calling $g$ or $F$ a test background records this model's omission of their response; it does not claim that the unchanged pair solves the coupled Einstein–Maxwell equations or is close to a coupled solution.

When geometric optics is invoked, it is restricted to the exact $C^4$ real phase, $C^3$ complex amplitudes, four pointwise ansatz constraints, and fixed compact-chart coefficient bounds of [[lem-emg-controlled-maxwell-wkb]]. That result supplies finite residual and leading-field estimates, local null rays, and a polarization quotient; it supplies no convergent series, global transport through caustics, exact-solution error estimate, or backreaction theorem.

This is a separately adopted physical model with no empirical premise. The Maxwell and probe assumptions are not deductions from one another, from mathematical axioms, or from source authority.

items.statement:
Use the fixed-background Maxwell test model of [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]] on a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and its adopted length-coordinate SI conventions. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Let $\theta\in C^4(U,\mathbb R)$ be dimensionless, set $k=d\theta$, and assume $k$ is nowhere zero and $g^{-1}(k,k)=0$. Let $a_0,a_1\in C^3(U;T^*M\otimes_\mathbb R\mathbb C)$, with covariant derivatives and contractions extended complex-linearly. Use $[k]=\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, $[a_0]=[a_1]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, and dimensionless $\epsilon$, as in [[lem-emg-controlled-maxwell-wkb]]. Define

$$ (\Box a)_b:=g^{ac}\nabla_a\nabla_c a_b,\qquad (Pa)_b:=(\Box a)_b-\operatorname{Ric}_b{}^c a_c,\qquad (La)_b:=2k^c\nabla_ca_b+(\nabla_ck^c)a_b. $$

Assume the four pointwise constraints $g^{-1}(k,a_0)=0$, $La_0=0$, $iLa_1+Pa_0=0$, and $ik^a(a_1)_a+\nabla^a(a_0)_a=0$. For $0<\epsilon\le1$, form the complex ansatz $A_\epsilon=\epsilon e^{i\theta/\epsilon}(a_0+\epsilon a_1)$ and its real potential $\widehat A_\epsilon:=\operatorname{Re}A_\epsilon$ with real field $\widehat F_\epsilon:=d\widehat A_\epsilon$. Use the fixed-chart component max norm $\|\cdot\|_{\infty,K}$ of [[lem-emg-controlled-maxwell-wkb]], which is zero on an empty compact set. On a nonempty compact coordinate set $K$, assume finite constants $K_0,D_0,C_0,B_0,B_1$ satisfy $\|k\|_{\infty,K}\le K_0$, $\|d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le D_0$, $\|Pa_1-\nabla d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le C_0$, $\|da_0+ik\wedge a_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_0$, and $\|da_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_1$. The real field obeys $d\widehat F_\epsilon=0$ and

$$ \|\nabla^a(\widehat F_\epsilon)_{ab}\|_{\infty,K}\le\epsilon K_0D_0+\epsilon^2C_0,\qquad \|\widehat F_\epsilon-\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\theta/\epsilon}ik\wedge a_0)\|_{\infty,K}\le\epsilon B_0+\epsilon^2B_1. $$

Each local integral curve of $k^\sharp$ is an affinely parameterized null geodesic. Along it $a_0$ is transported according to the supplied scalar transport amplitude, and the leading physical polarization is the class in $k^\perp/\operatorname{span}_\mathbb C\{k\}$, a two-dimensional complex space with positive induced Hermitian form. These are exact finite-order deductions under the displayed ansatz constraints. The residual is a component norm in the chosen chart, not an observer-independent tensor norm. The conclusion asserts no convergent WKB series, existence of amplitudes across caustics, exact Maxwell solution for a nonzero residual, solution-distance estimate, or coupled Einstein–Maxwell family.

items.statement:
Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, Levi–Civita connection $\nabla$, and length-coordinate SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-observables]] and the separately prescribed Maxwell test model of [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]]. Here $U$ is open, $g$ is the fixed metric, a field strength $F$ is a smooth real two-form, and a prescribed current $j$ is a smooth real vector field. The formal stress tensor and constants are

$$T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{ab}(g,F)=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F^{ac}F^b{}_c-\frac14g^{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{cd},\qquad \kappa=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}>0.$$

The adopted Maxwell alternatives are $dF=0$, $d(\star_gF)=0$ when source-free, or $dF=0$, $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ for a separately prescribed current. Let $g$ satisfy $G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=0$ on $U$, where $\Lambda$ is constant. Define the electromagnetic stress residual relative to this unchanged vacuum metric, with no matter stress included, by

$$\mathscr R_{ab}(g,F;\Lambda):=G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F).$$

First let $F_0$ be a smooth source-free Maxwell two-form on $U$. For real dimensionless $\delta$, $F_\delta:=\delta F_0$ remains source-free and

$$\mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)=-\kappa\delta^2T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F_0).$$

The same conclusion holds for an actual smooth sourced Maxwell pair: let $F_0$ be a smooth real two-form and $j_0$ a smooth real vector field on $U$ satisfying $dF_0=0$ and $\nabla_a(F_0)^{ab}=-\mu_0j_0^b$. With $F_\delta:=\delta F_0$ and $j_\delta:=\delta j_0$, the pair still satisfies the same sourced Maxwell equations, and

$$\mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)=-\kappa\delta^2T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F_0).$$

For a compact set $K$ in a fixed smooth coordinate chart contained in $U$ and a smooth covariant two-tensor $S$, define $\|S\|_{\infty,K}:=\max_{0\le a,b\le3}\sup_{p\in K}|S_{ab}(p)|$ when $K\ne\varnothing$, and set $\|S\|_{\infty,\varnothing}:=0$. In either Maxwell case,

$$\|\mathscr R(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)\|_{\infty,K}=\kappa\delta^2\|T^{\mathrm{EM}}(g,F_0)\|_{\infty,K}.$$

If $\delta\ne0$ and $F_0$ is nonzero at a point, its observer energy is positive there, so this electromagnetic/vacuum-background residual is nonzero. In the sourced case this does not test a full Einstein–Maxwell–matter equation, because no source-matter stress is included in $\mathscr R$. The residual is a consistency calculation, not an estimate of distance to a different metric solution.

Separately, on an open region where smooth charged-dust quantities have $\rho>0$, $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$, $j^a=\sigma U^a$, and the formal matter-exchange equation holds, replacing $(\rho,\sigma)$ by $(\eta\rho,\eta\sigma)$ for $\eta>0$ scales matter stress and current linearly, leaves $\sigma/\rho$ unchanged, and preserves the dust force equation when the prescribed $F,U$ are held fixed. Maxwell's sourced equation must still match the scaled current. If instead both $F$ and $j$ are scaled by $\eta$, the sourced Maxwell system is linear but electromagnetic stress scales as $\eta^2$ while dust stress scales as $\eta$; these degree differences provide no general coupled-solution family.

Finally, for a fixed $Q\ne0$ and $\ell>0$, prescribe only on the finite Minkowski annulus $\mathcal A_\ell=\{\mathbf x:\ell<|\mathbf x|<2\ell\}$ the radial electric field $\mathbf E=Q(4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2)^{-1}\mathbf e_r$, $\mathbf B=0$. Its field energy on that annulus is $Q^2/(16\pi\varepsilon_0\ell)$ and diverges as $\ell\downarrow0$. This calculation defines no field or source at the origin and supplies no point-charge construction or regularization theorem.
