items.statement:
Use the charged-probe action sector of the fixed-background model of [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]] and let $\alpha=q/m\ne0$, with constant $m>0$, constant charge $q$, length scale $L>0$, and speed constant $c>0$. When the Lorentz-force form is obtained from the adopted action, the inherited $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis of that exact action-equivalence theorem is assumed; no stronger choice axiom is used. In SI, $[\alpha]=\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $[L]=\mathrm m$, and $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; $\epsilon$, $X$, $\phi$, $\mathbf e$, and $\mathbf b$ are dimensionless. Choose a cutoff $0<\epsilon_*\le1$ sufficiently small in terms of the displayed uniform bounds below, as required by [[thm-emg-weak-slow-test-lorentz-limit]], and fix $0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_*$. On an open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, let $\mathcal K\Subset\Omega$ be compact and convex, use length coordinates $x^0=ct$, $x^i=LX^i$, and suppose the prescribed metric is smooth, stationary and Lorentzian on a neighborhood of $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times L\mathcal K$, with $\partial_0$ future timelike. For a smooth dimensionless $\phi$ and some fixed finite $C_g$, assume for every spatial multi-index $\beta$ with $|\beta|\le2$ that

$$|\partial_X^\beta r_{00}^{(\epsilon)}|+\max_{i,j}|\partial_X^\beta r_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}|\le C_g\epsilon^2,\qquad \max_i|\partial_X^\beta r_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}|\le C_g\epsilon^{3/2},$$

where $g_{00}^{(\epsilon)}=-(1+2\epsilon\phi)+r_{00}^{(\epsilon)}$, $g_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}=(1-2\epsilon\phi)\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}$, and $g_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}=r_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}$. Prescribe smooth stationary dimensionless fields $\mathbf e,\mathbf b$ with values and first derivatives bounded on $\mathcal K$, and a smooth real closed two-form $F^{(\epsilon)}$ on the same background neighborhood, with $dF^{(\epsilon)}=0$ and SI components $F_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}=-E_i^{(\epsilon)}/c$, $F_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k^{(\epsilon)}$ and

$$\alpha\mathbf E^{(\epsilon)}=\frac{\epsilon c^2}{L}\mathbf e,\qquad \alpha\mathbf B^{(\epsilon)}=\frac{\sqrt\epsilon c}{L}\mathbf b.$$

Closure $dF^{(\epsilon)}=0$ ensures local potentials, not a global potential: in each sufficiently small open coordinate ball $D$ about a curve point, use the smooth radial primitive of [[lem-emg-local-potential-construction]] as the supplied $A_D$ with $dA_D=F^{(\epsilon)}|_D$. Adopt fixed-endpoint action stationarity only on sufficiently short finite curve segments contained in such a ball, as in [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]] and [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]]. There is no assumption that the whole trajectory lies in a single potential domain, that $F^{(\epsilon)}$ is globally exact, or that the local potentials are stationary. No inhomogeneous Maxwell or Einstein equation is imposed on this prescribed background. The dimensionless comparison trajectory satisfies $\mathbf X_N'=\mathbf W_N$, $\mathbf W_N'=-\nabla_X\phi(\mathbf X_N)+\mathbf e(\mathbf X_N)+\mathbf W_N\times\mathbf b(\mathbf X_N)$ on $[0,S_*]$, where primes denote $S$ derivatives, $S_*>0$, and $S=\sqrt\epsilon ct/L$. Write $\| (\mathbf X,\mathbf W)\|_1$ for the sum of the absolute values of the six components and $\|Df\|_{1\to1}$ for its induced operator norm, as in [[thm-emg-weak-slow-test-lorentz-limit]]. Let the six-component comparison vector field $f$ have derivative norm at most $L_f<\infty$ on a compact convex state set $\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathcal K\times\mathbb R^3$ containing both scaled trajectories throughout $[0,S_*]$.

Suppose a $C^2$ future-directed proper-time worldline exists through this finite interval, obeys this local action model (equivalently the external Lorentz law on each such segment), has coordinate speed $|\mathbf w|\le C_v\sqrt\epsilon c$, has its scaled state remain in $\mathcal Q$, and has the same initial scaled data as the comparison trajectory. Set $\mathbf X_\epsilon=\mathbf x/L$ and $\mathbf W_\epsilon=\mathbf w/(\sqrt\epsilon c)$. Then for some finite $C_r$ depending only on the displayed uniform bounds, the exact scaled motion obeys

$$\mathbf X_\epsilon'=\mathbf W_\epsilon,\qquad \mathbf W_\epsilon'=-\nabla_X\phi(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf e(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf W_\epsilon\times\mathbf b(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf r_\epsilon(S),\qquad \|\mathbf r_\epsilon(S)\|_1\le C_r\epsilon,$$

and consequently

$$\sup_{0\le S\le S_*}\bigl(\|\mathbf X_\epsilon-\mathbf X_N\|_1+\|\mathbf W_\epsilon-\mathbf W_N\|_1\bigr)\le C_r\epsilon S_*e^{L_fS_*}.$$

This is a finite-duration conditional model prediction. It does not construct the trajectories, prove common compact containment, solve Maxwell's equations for the prescribed field, or establish a coupled Einstein–Maxwell family. The magnetic scaling may violate a coupled stress hierarchy unless additional matter scales are supplied.

row.title: Separately adopted fixed-background Maxwell and charged probes — Examples

items.title: Electrostatic test-energy first integral
items.physical_scope: A finite-segment charged test probe in a prescribed, stationary electrostatic potential on Minkowski spacetime. The conserved energy is conditional on the adopted Lorentz-force law and excludes self-field, self-gravity, radiation reaction, and any coupled source claim.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2
references.locator: Equations (6.9)–(6.10), PDF pp. 61–63, state the charged test-particle Lorentz law in curved spacetime. The stationary potential and energy integral are computed here under the local model conventions.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes (2019)
references.locator: §1.2.3, equation (1.20), PDF pp. 23–24, gives the charged-particle potential action and its electrostatic potential term. The item uses the local SI action sign and proves its conservation directly.

items.statement:
On Minkowski spacetime with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, time orientation $\partial_0$, and length coordinates $x^0=ct$, let $\phi(\mathbf x)$ be a $C^2$ time-independent scalar potential on an open spatial region and set $A=-\phi(\mathbf x)\,dx^0/c$. Use SI units $[\phi]=\mathrm V$, $[q]=\mathrm C$, $[m]=\mathrm{kg}$, and $[c]=\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ future-timelike proper-time segment satisfying the charged-probe law of [[post-emg-background-maxwell-test]], define $\mathbf w=d\mathbf x/dt$ and $\gamma=(1-|\mathbf w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. Then

$$E_{\mathrm{test}}=\gamma mc^2+q\phi(\mathbf x)$$

is constant along the segment. The field and metric are prescribed data; this is neither a measurement nor a coupled point-source solution.

items.title: Exact finite-frequency transverse Maxwell wave
items.physical_scope: An exact real, source-free plane-wave solution of the prescribed Minkowski Maxwell test model at every stated positive epsilon, with transverse electric/magnetic components. Its nonzero stress prevents it from solving the source-free coupled Einstein–Maxwell equation with Lambda=0 on the unchanged Minkowski metric. This is an ideal solution, not an experiment or photon-energy claim.

references.title: A. I. Harte, Gravitational lensing beyond geometric optics: I. Formalism and observables, arXiv:1808.06203v2 (2018), complete 38-page article
references.locator: §§3.1–3.3, PDF pp. 10–13, discusses transverse leading electromagnetic fields and polarization; Appendix A, PDF pp. 33–34, treats finite truncation residuals. This constant-amplitude plane wave is checked exactly here.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2
references.locator: Equations (6.12)–(6.14), PDF pp. 63–64, give the null geometric-optics ray calculation. The finite-frequency field equations and coupled-solution distinction are verified locally using the listed item suppliers.

items.statement:
On Minkowski spacetime in standard positively oriented inertial coordinates $(x^0,x,y,z)$, with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and future unit observer $n=\partial_0$, choose constants $\kappa>0$ with units $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, $A_*\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ with units $\mathrm{T\,m}$, and dimensionless $0<\epsilon\le1$. Define

$$A_\epsilon=\epsilon A_*\cos\!\left(\frac{\kappa(x^0-z)}{\epsilon}\right)dx.$$

The real field $F_\epsilon=dA_\epsilon$ is an exact source-free Maxwell wave for every such $\epsilon$. Its nonzero components are

$$F_{0x}=-\kappa A_*\sin\!\left(\frac{\kappa(x^0-z)}{\epsilon}\right),\qquad F_{zx}=\kappa A_*\sin\!\left(\frac{\kappa(x^0-z)}{\epsilon}\right).$$

For the inertial observer $n=\partial_0$, the SI convention gives $E_x=c\kappa A_*\sin(\kappa(x^0-z)/\epsilon)$ and $B_y=\kappa A_*\sin(\kappa(x^0-z)/\epsilon)$, with all other components zero. At points where the sine is nonzero, the field energy is positive. The field is an exact test-background wave, but it is not an exact source-free coupled Einstein–Maxwell field with $\Lambda=0$ on the unchanged Minkowski metric.

items.title: Constant-magnetic-field slow test-orbit comparison
items.physical_scope: An exact finite-time comparison of a relativistic charged test orbit and its Newton–Lorentz slow-motion trajectory in a prescribed constant magnetic field on Minkowski space. It excludes self-field, radiation reaction, and any small-field backreaction theorem or fully coupled flat Einstein–Maxwell solution.

references.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes, §6.2
references.locator: Equations (6.9)–(6.10), PDF pp. 61–63, give the curved charged test-particle equation; the finite magnetic orbit and error bound are computed here.

references.title: Eric Poisson, Adam Pound and Ian Vega, The Motion of Point Particles in Curved Spacetime, author manuscript arXiv:1102.0529v3 (2011), complete 162-page review
references.locator: §18.1, equations (18.3)–(18.10), PDF pp. 96–98, states the charged test-particle force equation and the singular self-field caveat. The present orbit uses only a separately prescribed smooth field.

items.statement:
On Minkowski spacetime with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and time orientation $\partial_0$, set $\phi=0$, $\mathbf E=0$, and prescribe a constant magnetic field with $\alpha\mathbf B=\sqrt\epsilon(c/L)b_0\mathbf e_z$, where $\alpha=q/m\ne0$ has units $\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$, $b_0\ne0$ is dimensionless, $L>0$ has units metres, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $0<\epsilon\le1$ is dimensionless. Choose initial velocity $\mathbf w_0=\sqrt\epsilon c\mathbf W_0$ with $\mathbf W_0\cdot\mathbf e_z=0$ and $\epsilon|\mathbf W_0|^2\le1/2$. Let $\mathbf X=\mathbf x/L$, $\mathbf W=\mathbf w/(\sqrt\epsilon c)$, and $S=\sqrt\epsilon ct/L$. With matched initial position, the exact relativistic and Newton–Lorentz comparison trajectories satisfy

$$|\mathbf W(S)-\mathbf W_N(S)|\le |b_0|\epsilon|\mathbf W_0|^3S,\qquad |\mathbf X(S)-\mathbf X_N(S)|\le\frac12|b_0|\epsilon|\mathbf W_0|^3S^2$$

on every fixed finite interval $0\le S\le S_*$. This is an exact ideal test-background comparison; it is not a coupled flat Einstein–Maxwell solution or a backreaction estimate.

row.title: Exact smooth coupled counterpoised dust and observables

items.title: Exact smooth coupled counterpoised dust and observables
items.physical_scope: Exact smooth solutions of the selected static SI Einstein–Maxwell–charged-dust model for positive superharmonic conformastatic profiles, together with one regular spherical profile and its induced-volume and dilute observables. The finely fixed charge-to-mass ratio belongs only to this family. No empirical realization, arbitrary-data coupled evolution, formation, or stability claim is made.

references.title: Reinhard Meinel and Moritz Hütten, On the black hole limit of electrically counterpoised dust configurations, arXiv:1105.3807v3 (2011), §2, equations (1)–(7), PDF pp. 2–3
references.locator: The selected static ECD ansatz and model-equation context. Its c=G=1 Gaussian conventions and fixed source sign are not imported; the local SI equations are checked under exact mathematical suppliers.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: §1.4.1 dust stress, §3.4 curvature contractions, and Ch. 4 Einstein-matter and electromagnetic-stress conventions; all conformastatic components and SI normalizations are supplied or checked locally.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III, Michaelmas 2019, complete 290-page author-hosted lecture notes
references.locator: §§3.2.2, 3.4.1, 4.5.2–4.5.4, and 4.5.7: independent curvature, Einstein-matter, Maxwell/perfect-fluid tensor, and energy-condition treatments; no source proof or c=1 convention is silently imported.

items.statement:
Assume the indexed Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]], recorded as the mathematical premise [A2]. Use the selected smooth SI Einstein–Maxwell charged-dust model of [A1], with length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres, positive constants $c,\mu_0,G_N$, $\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$, and $\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. Use the positive-root convention of [[def-emg-explicit-power-regimes]] to set $Q_s:=\sqrt{4\pi\epsilon_0G_N}>0$ (units $\mathrm{C\,kg^{-1}}$). For an open $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, let $H\in C^\infty(D,(0,\infty))$ be dimensionless and satisfy the Euclidean condition $\Delta H:=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i^2H\le0$. On $\mathcal M:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$, use the coordinate metric, orientation, and time orientation
$$g_H=-H^{-2}(dx^0)^2+H^2\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2,\qquad n:=H\partial_0\text{ future},\qquad e_i:=H^{-1}\partial_i.$$
Use the coordinate orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.
Define the smooth potential, field, dust velocity, rest-mass and rest-charge densities, current, and matter stress by
$$A:=s\frac c{Q_s}H^{-1}dx^0,\qquad F:=dA,\qquad U:=cH\partial_0,\qquad \rho:=-\frac{c^2\Delta H}{4\pi G_NH^3},\qquad \sigma:=sQ_s\rho,\qquad j^a:=\sigma U^a,\qquad T_m^{ab}:=\rho U^aU^b,$$
where $s\in\{-1,+1\}$ and the electromagnetic stress $T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}$ is the one adopted in [A1]. Then $g_H$ is smooth Lorentzian, $n$ is a future unit observer, $U=cn$ is future timelike with $g_H(U,U)=-c^2$, all displayed fields are smooth, and $\rho\ge0$. This tuple satisfies every equation of the selected dust branch: $dF=0$, $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, $\nabla_a(\rho U^a)=0$, $\rho U^a\nabla_aU^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c$, $\nabla_aj^a=0$, $\nabla_aT_m^{ab}=F^b{}_cj^c$, and the adopted Einstein equation with $\Lambda=0$. These are exact conditional model deductions. On $\{\rho>0\}$ the ratio $\sigma/\rho=sQ_s$ is constant along $U$; no division by $\rho$ is made on $\{\rho=0\}$. The observer electric components are $E_i:=cF(e_i,n)=-s c^2H_i/(Q_sH^2)$, where $H_i:=\partial_iH$, and the coordinate acceleration is $a^0=0$, $a^i=-c^2H_i/H^3$.

Here $\rho$ is rest-mass density in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $\sigma$ is rest-charge density in $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$, and the stress components have energy-density units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. The orthonormal components of $F$ have tesla units and $E_i$ has units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, under the SI convention of [A1].

The total stress $T_{ab}:=T_{m,ab}+T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}$ satisfies the weak, null, dominant, and strong energy conditions pointwise: respectively $T(v,v)\ge0$ for every future timelike $v$; $T(\ell,\ell)\ge0$ for every nonzero future null $\ell$; $-T^a{}_bv^b$ is future causal or zero for every future timelike $v$; and the weak condition holds for $T_{ab}-\tfrac12(g^{cd}T_{cd})g_{ab}$.

For the spherical specialization on all $\mathbb R^3$, let $a,b>0$ be lengths,
$$r^2:=\sum_{i=1}^3(x^i)^2,\qquad \Psi:=\sqrt{r^2+b^2},\qquad H:=1+\frac a\Psi.$$
Then $\Delta H=-3ab^2/(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}<0$ and $\rho=3c^2ab^2/[4\pi G_NH^3(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}]>0$ everywhere. On a slice $\Sigma=\{x^0=\mathrm{constant}\}$ the induced spatial metric is $h=H^2\delta_{ij}dx^idx^j$ and its volume measure is $dV_h=H^3d\lambda_3$, where $\lambda_3$ is Euclidean Lebesgue measure. Define the proper matter mass and signed charge by $M_{\mathrm{prop}}:=\int_\Sigma\rho\,dV_h$ and $Q_{\mathrm{prop}}:=\int_\Sigma\sigma\,dV_h$. Both are finite, with
$$M_{\mathrm{prop}}=\frac{c^2a}{G_N},\qquad Q_{\mathrm{prop}}=sQ_s\frac{c^2a}{G_N}.$$
The scalar curvature, meaning the trace of the Ricci tensor in the adopted convention, is $S_g=-2\Delta H/H^3>0$. These proper integrals are not identified with an ADM mass or a measurement.

For $a=\delta b$ with $0<\delta\le1$, put $h_0:=b/\Psi$ and define the positive linear density profile
$$\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}:=\frac{3c^2\delta b^3}{4\pi G_N(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}}.$$
The same exact coupled solutions satisfy the entrywise Cartesian-coordinate bounds
$$\left|g_{00}+\bigl(1-2\delta h_0\bigr)\right|\le3\delta^2,\qquad \left|g_{ij}-\bigl(1+2\delta h_0\bigr)\delta_{ij}\right|\le\delta^2,\qquad 0\le1-\frac{\rho}{\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}}\le3\delta.$$
All these are ideal model statements, not observed data. The result does not assert physical realization, stability, formation, or a coupled initial-value theorem.

row.title: Exact smooth coupled counterpoised dust and observables — Examples

items.title: Everywhere regular counterpoised sphere
items.physical_scope: Central values and proper integrals in one exact smooth coupled charged-dust model profile. This is an ideal conditional calculation, not an observation, particle-composition claim, or stability result.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Take $a=b>0$ and $s=+1$ in the exact A-page family. With $r^2=\sum_i(x^i)^2$, $\Psi=\sqrt{r^2+b^2}$, and $H=1+b/\Psi$, the center has $H(0)=2$, $\nabla H(0)=0$, and $\Delta H(0)=-3/b^2$. Its central rest-mass density and scalar curvature are
$$\rho(0)=\frac{3c^2}{32\pi G_Nb^2},\qquad S_g(0)=\frac{3}{4b^2}.$$
The observer electric field vanishes at the center. The complete model remains smooth with strictly positive density for every finite $r$ and has infinite spatial extent. Its proper mass and signed proper charge are $c^2b/G_N$ and $Q_sc^2b/G_N$. There is no point source at the center; no stability, real-particle composition, or empirical realization is asserted.

items.title: Quantitative dilute comparison of actual coupled solutions
items.physical_scope: Exact coordinate metric and density inequalities in a restricted dilute subfamily of the smooth coupled model. Bounds compare ideal mathematical fields and are not experimental or numerical measurements.
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Fix $b>0$ and $0<\delta\le1/10$, and set $a=\delta b$. With $r^2=\sum_i(x^i)^2$, let $h_0:=b/\sqrt{r^2+b^2}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}:=3c^2\delta b^3/[4\pi G_N(r^2+b^2)^{5/2}]$. The exact coupled fields of the A-page theorem satisfy, entrywise in this Cartesian chart,
$$\left|g_{00}+\bigl(1-2\delta h_0\bigr)\right|\le\frac3{100},\qquad \left|g_{ij}-\bigl(1+2\delta h_0\bigr)\delta_{ij}\right|\le\frac1{100},$$
and
$$0\le1-\frac{\rho}{\rho_{\mathrm{lin}}}\le\frac3{10}.$$
These fractions bound discrepancies in an ideal exact model family. They are not measured errors and imply no stability or small-data existence theorem.

row.title: Geometric electrovac equations and flux normalization

items.title: Finite exact rational electrovac tensor verification
items.design_state: Authored draft; current supplier status and exact uses are recorded in batch-21 dependency inputs.
items.statement:
**Inputs.** Fix the integral domain
$P=\mathbb Q[r,y,M,a,q]$ on the ordered variables $(r,y,M,a,q)$ and its field of fractions
$K=\operatorname{Frac}(P)$. A run receives a symmetric $4\times4$ matrix
$g=(g_{ij})$ and a covector $A=(A_i)$ with entries in $K$, represented by
finite sparse polynomial numerator-denominator pairs, together with a specified
polynomial $w\in P$. It also receives the chart hypothesis that $\det g$ is
nonzero in $K$ and that on the real open chart under consideration all input
denominators are nonzero and $w=\sqrt{|\det g|}>0$. The coordinate derivations
are $\delta_0=\delta_3=0$, $\delta_1=\partial_r$, and $\delta_2=\partial_y$.
The chart hypothesis is input; the procedure does not prove Lorentz signature
or check the volume identity. For geometric interpretation use the curvature
convention $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$,
with $R^a{}_{bcd}$ the coefficient of $R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b$ and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=R^a{}_{bad}$. Expanding this definition yields the
coordinate Ricci schedule in Instruction 3.

**Outputs.** Return the finite tables of: the sixteen entries of
$gg^{-1}-I$; the six independent components of
$F_{ij}:=\delta_iA_j-\delta_jA_i$; all sixteen raised components
$F^{ij}$; the four Maxwell-density residuals
$\sum_i\delta_i(wF^{ij})$; all sixty-four Christoffel entries; the sixteen
Ricci entries
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ij} =\sum_k\left(\delta_k\Gamma^k{}_{ij}-\delta_j\Gamma^k{}_{ik}\right) +\sum_{k,l}\left(\Gamma^k{}_{kl}\Gamma^l{}_{ij} -\Gamma^k{}_{jl}\Gamma^l{}_{ik}\right);$$
the scalar $F_{ij}F^{ij}$; the sixteen entries of
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ij} -2\left(F_{ik}F_j{}^k-\frac14g_{ij}F_{kl}F^{kl}\right);$$
the scalar curvature and the Ricci-square. For every output rational function,
return its numerator-denominator pair, its exact numerator-zero flag, and the
finite list of all divisor polynomials used.

**Instructions.**

1. Represent a polynomial by its finite set of exponent-vector/coefficient
   pairs. Addition merges equal exponent vectors, multiplication enumerates
   every pair of input monomials and collects equal exponent vectors, and
   $\partial_r,\partial_y$ differentiate each monomial by the integer-power
   rule of [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]]. Represent a rational function by $(p,d)$ with $p,d\in P$ and
   $d\ne0$. Addition and multiplication use cross-products, and division
   replaces $(p,d)/(u,v)$ by $(pv,du)$ only when $u\ne0$ in $P$.
   Differentiation uses $(p'd-pd',d^2)$.

2. Compute $\det g$ by its twenty-four signed permutation products and form
   $g^{-1}$ from cofactors divided by $\det g$. Record and check all sixteen
   entries of $gg^{-1}-I$.

3. All indices in this instruction range over $\{0,1,2,3\}$, and
   $g^{ij}:=(g^{-1})_{ij}$. Compute every $F_{ij}$, then raise indices by
   $F_j{}^k:=\sum_l g^{kl}F_{jl}$ and
   $F^{ij}:=\sum_{k,l}g^{ik}g^{jl}F_{kl}$. Compute all four
   $\sum_i\delta_i(wF^{ij})$. Compute every Christoffel entry by
   $\Gamma^i{}_{jk}=\frac12\sum_lg^{il}
   (\delta_jg_{lk}+\delta_kg_{jl}-\delta_lg_{jk})$, then all sixteen Ricci
   entries by the displayed formula, with no symmetry-based component omitted.
   Compute $F_{ij}F^{ij}$, every Einstein residual, $g^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}$
   and $g^{ik}g^{jl}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{kl}$ by their
   full finite contractions.

4. Record every polynomial divisor introduced by inversion, division, or a
   rational derivative in the admissibility list. Do not remove a divisor from
   that list when a later cancellation removes its factor from the displayed
   numerator or denominator. Return failure if any required divisor is the
   zero polynomial or an input denominator is zero.

A zero flag means exactly that the polynomial numerator is the zero element of
$P$. No floating-point tolerance, parameter sample, convergence test, or
choice of roots is part of the procedure. This is a finite mathematical
procedure; its operational correctness, termination, and resource bounds are
separate proved claims.

For every admissible input of [[alg-emg-rational-electrovac-verification]], every returned rational numerator-denominator pair represents the corresponding displayed inverse, Maxwell, Christoffel, Ricci, scalar, or Einstein-residual expression in
$K=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb Q[r,y,M,a,q])$. Its numerator-zero flag is true if and only if that rational function is identically zero in $K$. items.statement: For an input of [[alg-emg-rational-electrovac-verification]] with $N_{\mathrm{in}}$ input coefficient/exponent records, suppose the expanded fixed schedule has $K$ polynomial operations and every intermediate polynomial support has at most $R$ monomials. The algorithm terminates. Under elementary rational-coefficient arithmetic, sparse addition, multiplication, differentiation and sorted-list insertion perform at most $K(2R^2+2R)$ coefficient operations and at most that many ordered exponent-vector insertions; sorted-list insertion uses at most $R$ support comparisons per insertion. If every intermediate support is retained, memory is at most $(K+N_{\mathrm{in}})R$ coefficient/exponent records. These are algebraic-operation and record bounds in terms of actual intermediate support; the statement gives no polynomial input-size bound, bit-complexity bound, practical runtime estimate or optimality claim.

items.title: Geometric electrovac equations and flux normalization
items.design_state: Authored draft; current supplier status and exact uses are recorded in batch-21 dependency inputs.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $o$ is the manifold orientation, $N$ is a smooth future timelike field, and the metric volume form is chosen to agree with $o$. Let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection, let $\mathcal F$ be a smooth real two-form on $M$, and use the curvature convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$.
Define
$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where both raised indices use $g^{-1}$. A **geometric electrovac datum with zero cosmological constant** is the tuple $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ satisfying
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$$
at every point of $M$. Here $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$; on two-forms $\star_g^2=-1$. No material current, matter tensor, global potential, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, horizon, or extension condition is part of this definition.

For flux integration, an **oriented embedded smooth sphere** means a compact smooth two-dimensional manifold $S$ without boundary, homeomorphic to the unit sphere $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:x\cdot x=1\}$, with a specified orientation in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] and a smooth inclusion $i:S\hookrightarrow M$. Here smooth embedding means an injective immersion that is a homeomorphism onto its image with the subspace topology ([[def-smooth-embedding]]); identify $S$ with that image. The sphere orientation is specified independently of the spacetime orientation; for coordinate spheres used below it is the stated outward orientation.

For a smooth two-form $\eta$ on a neighborhood of $i(S)$, use the pullback convention of [[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]],
$$(i^*\eta)_p(v,w)=\eta_{i(p)}(di_pv,di_pw),\qquad p\in S,\quad v,w\in T_pS.$$
By [[prop-pullback-of-forms-is-smooth-functorial-and-preserves-wedges]], this is a smooth top form on $S$. Its support is the closure in $S$ of its nonzero locus ([[def-compactly-supported-differential-form]]), hence is closed in compact $S$ and compact by [[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]. Thus $i^*\eta\in\Omega_c^2(S)$.

Write $\mathcal I_S$ for [[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-top-form-on-an-oriented-manifold]]: for a subordinate smooth partition $(\rho_j)$ and connected charts $\phi_j$, it sets $\mathcal I_S(\omega)=\sum_j I_{\phi_j}(\rho_j\omega)$, where $I_{\phi_j}$ is the signed chart integral of the compactly supported coefficient. Only finitely many terms are nonzero. The value is independent of charts, partition and refinement by [[thm-global-form-integration-is-independent-of-the-atlas-partition-and-refinement]]. Define the surface notation by
$$\int_S\eta:=\mathcal I_S(i^*\eta).$$
This agrees with [[prop-integration-over-an-oriented-embedded-submanifold]]; a reparametrization here means an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $F:T\to S$ of oriented smooth two-manifolds (a smooth bijection with smooth inverse and orientation-preserving differential). For such $F$, the same value is $\mathcal I_T((iF)^*\eta)$.
The integration definition and its independence theorem assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, already retained in the geometric background below. For $\eta=\mathcal F$ and $\eta=\star_g\mathcal F$, smoothness of the given field and Hodge map makes both pulled-back top forms admissible; their integrals are finite real numbers. Define the geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.

items.title: Dyonic Reissner-Nordström metric and field domains
items.design_state: Authored draft; current supplier status and exact uses are recorded in batch-21 dependency inputs.
items.statement:
Let $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters and put
$Q^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2$. Let $J\subset(0,\infty)$ be open and require
$$f(r):=1-\frac{2M}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2}\ne0\qquad(r\in J).$$
On the smooth product $\mathcal M_J:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J_r\times S^2$,
use $S^2=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb R^3:X^2+Y^2+Z^2=1\}$ with its subspace
topology ([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]). Specify the smooth
structure by the sphere atlas of [[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]],
Definition (b): for $\varepsilon=\pm1$, delete $p_\varepsilon=(0,0,\varepsilon)$
and use $\sigma_\varepsilon(X,Y,Z)=(X,Y)/(1-\varepsilon Z)$.
For $u=(u_1,u_2)$ and $h=u_1^2+u_2^2$, its inverse is
$\sigma_\varepsilon^{-1}(u)=(2u_1,2u_2,\varepsilon(h-1))/(1+h)$;
the transition is $u\mapsto u/h$ on $h>0$. These rational maps are smooth
on their domains. The product atlas consists of
$(x^0,r,p)\mapsto(x^0,r,\sigma_\varepsilon(p))$ on
$\mathbb R\times J\times(S^2\setminus\{p_\varepsilon\})$;
its transitions leave $x^0,r$ fixed and apply the displayed sphere transition.
The product is Hausdorff and second countable by the subspace topology from
$\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^3$, whose rational balls give a countable basis.
These charts specify its maximal smooth atlas, including when $J$ is empty.
The inclusion of $S^2$ into $\mathbb R^3$ is smooth with injective differential
in these parametrizations; its induced unit round metric is $\gamma_{S^2}$
([[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]]).
Orient $S^2$ by its outward unit normal: for $p\in S^2$ and
$u,v\in T_pS^2$, define
$$ (\omega_{S^2})_p(u,v):=\det(p,u,v). $$
Thus $\omega_{S^2}$ is the positive area form of $\gamma_{S^2}$, and in the
polar chart $X=\sin\theta\cos\phi$, $Y=\sin\theta\sin\phi$,
$Z=\cos\theta$ it is $\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$. The **dyonic RN
datum** is
$$g=-f(r)\,dx^0\otimes dx^0+f(r)^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2}, \qquad \mathcal F=-\frac{q_e}{r^2}\,dx^0\wedge dr+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$
Here $x^0$ and $r$ have units of metres, angles on $S^2$ are dimensionless,
and $M,q_e,q_m$ have units of metres. The metric components are dimensionless
in length coordinates; the nonzero coordinate components of $\mathcal F$ have
units inherited from their coordinate Jacobians. Use the orientation
$dx^0\wedge dr\wedge\omega_{S^2}$.

The set $J$ may have several connected components. On $\{f>0\}$ choose the
time orientation $\partial_{x^0}$; on $\{f<0\}$ choose $\partial_r$. These
are smooth timelike fields on their respective open subsets because
$g(\partial_{x^0},\partial_{x^0})=-f<0$ when $f>0$ and
$g(\partial_r,\partial_r)=f^{-1}<0$ when $f<0$. Since $f$ has no zero on
$\mathcal M_J$, this defines a smooth time orientation on the whole product.
The sphere area form and the displayed two-form are global on $S^2$.

Let $N,S$ denote the north and south poles. On
$U_N:=S^2\setminus\{S\}$ and $U_S:=S^2\setminus\{N\}$, respectively,
local potential one-forms are
$$\mathcal A_N=-\frac{q_e}{r}\,dx^0+q_m(1-\cos\theta)\,d\phi,\qquad \mathcal A_S=-\frac{q_e}{r}\,dx^0-q_m(1+\cos\theta)\,d\phi.$$
Each displayed potential extends smoothly over its named included pole:
$(1-\cos\theta)d\phi$ is smooth at $N$ and
$(1+\cos\theta)d\phi$ is smooth at $S$. Direct differentiation gives
$d\mathcal A_N=d\mathcal A_S=\mathcal F$ on the respective patches. Their
overlap difference is $2q_m\,d\phi$; it is local potential data, not a global
real gauge function on the entire sphere. The definition assumes no $U(1)$
bundle or charge quantization. To verify pole smoothness, use local coordinates
$u=X,v=Y$ near each pole. There
$d\phi=(u\,dv-v\,du)/(u^2+v^2)$. Near $N$,
$1-\cos\theta=(u^2+v^2)/(1+Z)$, so
$(1-\cos\theta)d\phi=(u\,dv-v\,du)/(1+Z)$ is smooth. Near $S$,
$1+\cos\theta=(u^2+v^2)/(1-Z)$, so
$(1+\cos\theta)d\phi=(u\,dv-v\,du)/(1-Z)$ is smooth. The denominators are
nonzero on the respective named patches.

items.title: Kerr-Newman metric and potential on the exact Boyer-Lindquist domain
items.design_state: Authored draft; current supplier status and exact uses are recorded in batch-21 dependency inputs.
items.statement:
Use the smooth covariant metric and signature conventions of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and the smooth real form spaces $\Omega^k(U)$ of [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. Geometric electric flux-length normalization means the convention in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; its field equations are not hypotheses in this coordinate definition.

Let $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$ have units of metres. Write
$$\Sigma(r,\theta):=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta,\quad \Delta(r):=r^2-2Mr+a^2+q^2,\quad R(r):=r^2+a^2,\quad B(\theta):=\sin^2\theta.$$
Let $U$ be an open subset of the Boyer-Lindquist coordinate region
$\{(x^0,r,\theta,\phi):\Sigma>0,\ \Delta\ne0,\ 0<\theta<\pi\}$.
Coordinates $x^0,r$ have units of metres and $\theta,\phi$ are dimensionless.
On $U$ define
$$g=-\frac{\Delta}{\Sigma}(dx^0-aB\,d\phi)^2 +\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2 +\frac{B}{\Sigma}(R\,d\phi-a\,dx^0)^2,\qquad \mathcal A=-\frac{qr}{\Sigma}(dx^0-aB\,d\phi),\quad\mathcal F:=d\mathcal A.$$
The metric is the exact real symmetric tensor given by this display; no value
on $\Delta=0$, the axes $\theta=0,\pi$, or $\Sigma=0$ is part of this
definition. The scalar $q$ is a geometric electric flux-length parameter; no
SI conversion is fixed in this Definition.

**Well-definedness on the stated patch.** In the coordinates
$(x^0,r,y,\phi)$ with $y=\cos\theta$ and $b=1-y^2$, the coordinate change is
a smooth diffeomorphism because $dy/d\theta=-\sin\theta\ne0$. The metric
matrix has
$$g_{00}=-\frac{\Delta-a^2b}{\Sigma},\quad g_{03}=-\frac{ab(R-\Delta)}{\Sigma},\quad g_{33}=\frac{b(R^2-a^2\Delta b)}{\Sigma},\quad g_{11}=\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta},\quad g_{22}=\frac{\Sigma}{b}.$$
The inverse has nonzero entries
$$g^{00}=-\frac{R^2-a^2\Delta b}{\Sigma\Delta},\quad g^{03}=-\frac{a(R-\Delta)}{\Sigma\Delta},\quad g^{33}=\frac{\Delta-a^2b}{\Sigma\Delta b},\quad g^{11}=\frac{\Delta}{\Sigma},\quad g^{22}=\frac{b}{\Sigma}.$$
Multiplying the $0,3$ blocks and the reciprocal $1,1$ and $2,2$ entries
gives $gg^{-1}=I_4$.
The $t,\phi$ block determinant is $-\Delta b$, and the full determinant is
$-\Sigma^2$ in these coordinates. If $\Delta>0$, the $t,\phi$ block has one
positive and one negative eigenvalue while the $r,\theta$ entries are positive.
If $\Delta<0$, $g_{33}>0$ and the $t,\phi$ block has positive determinant,
hence is positive definite, while $g_{11}<0$ and $g_{22}>0$. Thus $g$ is
nondegenerate of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on every component of $U$. Since this
is a coordinate patch, a smooth time orientation may be supplied locally;
the coordinate tensors and their closedness do not depend on that choice.

The potential is a smooth real one-form on $U$ because $\Sigma>0$, so $\mathcal F$
is a smooth real two-form. The coordinate formula in [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]] defines $\mathcal F=d\mathcal A$ componentwise. Applying it again pairs each second partial of a potential coefficient with its reversed-order partial and opposite wedge sign. They cancel by [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], since every coefficient is smooth; hence $d\mathcal F=d^2\mathcal A=0$. This definition is
only on the pole-free Boyer-Lindquist patch and asserts no global potential,
axis extension, horizon extension, or global topology.

items.title: Exact Reissner-Nordström Ricci and curvature identities
items.design_state: Authored draft; current supplier status and exact uses are recorded in batch-21 dependency inputs.
items.statement:
Let $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$, and let $J\subset(0,\infty)$ be open with
$f(r)=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2\ne0$ on $J$. For the dyonic RN datum of
[[def-emg-xs-rn-data]], in a spherical-polar chart its Ricci components are
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=f\left(\frac{f''}{2}+\frac{f'}r\right)=\frac{fQ^2}{r^4},\quad \operatorname{Ric}_{11}=-\frac1f\left(\frac{f''}{2}+\frac{f'}r\right)=-\frac{Q^2}{fr^4},$$
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{22}=1-f-rf'=\frac{Q^2}{r^2},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{33}=(1-f-rf')\sin^2\theta=\frac{Q^2\sin^2\theta}{r^2},$$
and all mixed components vanish. The scalar curvature is zero and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{ab}=4Q^4/r^8$. The Kretschmann scalar is
$$R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=f''^2+\frac{4(f')^2}{r^2}+\frac{4(1-f)^2}{r^4} =\frac{48M^2}{r^6}-\frac{96MQ^2}{r^7}+\frac{56Q^4}{r^8}.$$
All formulas hold on every component of $J$, including $f<0$.

items.title: Full-sphere exterior extension of the Kerr-Newman datum
items.design_state: Authored draft; current supplier status and exact uses are recorded in batch-21 dependency inputs.
items.statement:
Let $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$ have units of metres, choose $R_0>4|M|$, and
set
$$\mathcal X:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(R_0,\infty)_r\times S^2,\qquad R=r^2+a^2,\quad b=1-Z^2,\quad \Sigma=r^2+a^2Z^2,\quad \Delta=r^2-2Mr+a^2+q^2,$$
where $S^2=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb R^3:X^2+Y^2+Z^2=1\}$ has its induced
unit round metric $\gamma$ and outward area form $\omega$.
Specify the sphere smooth structure by [[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]],
Definition (b): on $S^2\setminus\{(0,0,\varepsilon)\}$ use
$\sigma_\varepsilon(X,Y,Z)=(X,Y)/(1-\varepsilon Z)$, $\varepsilon=\pm1$.
With $h=u_1^2+u_2^2$, the inverse is
$u\mapsto(2u_1,2u_2,\varepsilon(h-1))/(1+h)$, and the transition
on $h>0$ is $u\mapsto u/h$. These maps are smooth on their domains.
Give $\mathcal X$ the maximal atlas generated by the product charts
$(x^0,r,p)\mapsto(x^0,r,\sigma_\varepsilon(p))$;
its transitions leave $x^0,r$ fixed and apply the displayed sphere transition.
The product is Hausdorff and second countable as a subspace of $\mathbb R^5$,
using rational balls for a countable basis. The inverse parametrizations
make the sphere inclusion smooth with injective differential, so
$\gamma_p(u,v)=u\cdot v$ and $\omega_p(u,v)=\det(p,u,v)$
are smooth tensors with the stated outward orientation. Write
$$\lambda:=X\,dY-Y\,dX,\qquad \bar g:=-\frac{\Delta-a^2b}{\Sigma}(dx^0)^2 +\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\gamma +\frac{a^2(R+\Sigma-\Delta)}{\Sigma}\lambda^2 -\frac{2a(R-\Delta)}{\Sigma}\,dx^0\odot\lambda,$$
$$\bar{\mathcal A}:=-\frac{qr}{\Sigma}(dx^0-a\lambda),\qquad \bar{\mathcal F}:=d\bar{\mathcal A}.$$
Here $\lambda^2=\lambda\otimes\lambda$ and
$u\odot v=(u\otimes v+v\otimes u)/2$. This is the **full-sphere exterior
extension** of the pole-free datum in [[def-emg-xs-kn-data]]. The coordinates
$x^0,r$ and parameters $M,a,q$ have units of metres; sphere coordinates
are dimensionless. The field $\bar{\mathcal F}$ is the geometric
length-normalized two-form and no SI conversion is part of this definition.

items.design_state: Authored draft; current supplier status and exact uses are recorded in batch-21 dependency inputs.
items.statement:
Let $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$ and use the electric Kerr-Newman datum on a
Boyer-Lindquist chart with $\Sigma>0$, $\Delta\ne0$, $0<\theta<\pi$. Set
$y=\cos\theta$, $b=1-y^2$, $R=r^2+a^2$, and use the rational procedure of
[[alg-emg-rational-electrovac-verification]] with volume polynomial $w=\Sigma$.
Its exact component table is: the metric and inverse entries and determinant
in [[def-emg-xs-kn-data]]; the field components
$$\mathcal F_{10}=\frac{q(r^2-a^2y^2)}{\Sigma^2},\quad \mathcal F_{20}=\frac{2qra^2y}{\Sigma^2},\quad \mathcal F_{13}=-\frac{abq(r^2-a^2y^2)}{\Sigma^2},\quad \mathcal F_{23}=-\frac{2qraR\,y}{\Sigma^2};$$
the Ricci table and exact residuals recorded in Proof steps 2.2-3.1; and the exact contractions
$$\mathcal F_{ij}\mathcal F^{ij} =-\frac{2q^2(r^4-6a^2r^2y^2+a^4y^4)}{\Sigma^4},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ij}\operatorname{Ric}^{ij}=\frac{4q^4}{\Sigma^4}, \qquad g^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=0.$$
The exact rational calculation returns zero numerator flags for all four
Maxwell-density residuals and all sixteen Einstein residuals.

For arbitrary $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$, put $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$ and
$f(r)=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2$. On every open $J\subset(0,\infty)$ with $f\ne0$, the
dyonic RN datum of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] is a geometric electrovac datum of
[[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] on
$\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J\times S^2$. In particular, its global two-form is
smooth, $d\mathcal F=d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$, and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$ everywhere on that domain.

For arbitrary formal $c,\mu_0,G_N>0$, set $\alpha=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}$, $F=\mathcal F/\alpha$, and $T_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_g(F)_{ab}$. Then the same datum satisfies

$$dF=d(\star_gF)=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}T_{ab},$$

where $S$ is scalar curvature and $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\frac12Sg_{ab}$. This is the formal SI-to-geometric tensor normalization of [[lem-emg-maxwell-observer-stress]](d). It asserts neither measured parameter values nor a bundle realization for arbitrary flux. When the separate fixed-sector action hypotheses hold, $T$ is also the electromagnetic Hilbert tensor of that supplier.

items.design_state: Authored draft; current supplier status and exact uses are recorded in batch-21 dependency inputs.
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ be a smooth geometric electrovac datum with zero
cosmological constant, and let $\beta\in\mathbb R$ be constant. Define
$$\mathcal F_\beta:=\cos\beta\,\mathcal F+\sin\beta\,\star_g\mathcal F.$$
Then $d\mathcal F_\beta=d(\star_g\mathcal F_\beta)=0$ and
$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F_\beta)=Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$, so the same metric satisfies
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F_\beta)$. This is a classical
two-form identity; it asserts no charge quantization or empirical existence
of magnetic monopoles.

items.title: RN curvature invariants and the C2 extension obstruction
items.design_state: Authored draft; current supplier status and exact uses are recorded in batch-21 dependency inputs.
items.statement:
On the dyonic RN datum with real length parameters $M,q_e,q_m$, let
$Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$ and $r>0$, $f(r)\ne0$. Then the scalar curvature is
$S=0$, while
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{ab}=\frac{4Q^4}{r^8},\qquad R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=\frac{48M^2}{r^6}-\frac{96MQ^2}{r^7}+\frac{56Q^4}{r^8}.$$
If $Q\ne0$, the Ricci-square diverges as $r\downarrow0$; if $Q=0$ and
$M\ne0$, the Kretschmann scalar diverges there. Consequently no $C^2$
nondegenerate metric extension can add an approached $r=0$ point in either
case. For $M=Q=0$ the metric is flat and these invariants give no obstruction.
No distributional source at $r=0$ is asserted.

$\Sigma>0$, $\Delta\ne0$, $0<\theta<\pi$, its scalar curvature is zero and
$$\mathcal F_{ab}\mathcal F^{ab} =-\frac{2q^2(r^4-6a^2r^2\cos^2\theta+a^4\cos^4\theta)}{\Sigma^4}, \qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{ab}=\frac{4q^4}{\Sigma^4}.$$

nondegenerate metric extension can add a point approached with $\Sigma\to0$.

coordinate map to the ring $X^2+Y^2=a^2,\ Z=0$. If $q=0$, these charged
invariants give no obstruction; no vacuum Kerr Weyl-singularity claim is
made.

items.statement:
Let $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$ and choose an auxiliary length $\ell_*>0$. Use the
full-sphere exterior extension
[[def-emg-xs-kn-full-sphere-exterior]] with parameters $(M,a,q)$ on an annulus
$r\in(R_0,R_1)\subset(0,\infty)$ where $\Delta>0$. For example, take
$R_0=4|M|+\ell_*$. For every $r>R_0$, $1-2M/r>1/2$ and
$(a^2+q^2)/r^2\ge0$, so $\Delta/r^2>1/2$. For constant
$\beta\in\mathbb R$,
the dual-rotated field $\mathcal F_\beta=\cos\beta\,\mathcal F+
\sin\beta\,\star_g\mathcal F$ has flux parameters
$$q_e=q\cos\beta,\qquad q_m=q\sin\beta.$$
The metric depends on these two parameters only through
$q_e^2+q_m^2=q^2$. The unrotated electric field has zero magnetic sphere flux
and electric sphere flux $4\pi q$. Flux conservation is asserted only between
finite homologous exterior spheres; no quantization or noncompact side-flux
claim is made.

items.title: Selected ingoing RN extension and time orientation
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters. Set
$Q^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2$ and
$$f(r):=1-\frac{2M}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2}.$$
The selected ingoing RN manifold is
$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}:=\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2,$$
where $v,r$ have units of metres, $S^2$ has unit round metric $\gamma$ and
outward area form $\omega$, and the signature is $(-,+,+,+)$. Orient the
product by $dv\wedge dr\wedge\omega$. Define
$$g_{\mathrm{in}}=-f(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\gamma,\qquad \mathcal F_{\mathrm{in}}=-\frac{q_e}{r^2}\,dv\wedge dr+q_m\omega.$$
These are smooth on every $r>0$, including every positive root of $f$; the
domain excludes $r=0$. This is an extension of the static RN metric and field,
not a maximal extension or a specification of a source at the excluded
centre.

For the time orientation, define the global smooth fields
$$\ell:=-\partial_r,\qquad n:=\partial_v+\frac{f(r)}2\partial_r,\qquad N:=\ell+n=\partial_v+\left(\frac{f(r)}2-1\right)\partial_r.$$
The chosen future timelike field is $N$; the future cone is the component of
the timelike cone containing it. The well-definedness proof shows that $N$ is
timelike and that $\ell,n$ are future null. On $f\ne0$, the substitution
$v=t+r_*(r)$ with $r_*'=1/f$ identifies the metric and two-form with the
static dyonic RN formulas of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]]. This coordinate
identification does not assert agreement of time orientations on the
interior static components: on $f>0$ the selected orientation agrees with
$\partial_t$, while on $f<0$ it is the opposite of the separate choice
$\partial_r$ made by that static definition.

items.title: Dyonic RN gauges and global exactness obstruction
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $J\subset(0,\infty)$ be nonempty and open, and suppose
$f(r)=1-2M/r+(q_e^2+q_m^2)/r^2\ne0$ on $J$. On the static dyonic RN
product $\mathbb R_t\times J\times S^2$, orient by $dt\wedge dr\wedge\omega$
and use the field $\mathcal F=-q_e r^{-2}dt\wedge dr+q_m\omega$. For every
sphere $S_r$,
$$\int_{S_r}\mathcal F=4\pi q_m,\qquad \int_{S_r}\star_g\mathcal F=4\pi q_e.$$
On the north and south patches it has smooth potentials
$$\mathcal A_N=-\frac{q_e}{r}dt+q_m(1-\cos\theta)d\phi,\qquad \mathcal A_S=-\frac{q_e}{r}dt-q_m(1+\cos\theta)d\phi,$$
with $d\mathcal A_N=d\mathcal A_S=\mathcal F$ and
$\mathcal A_S-\mathcal A_N=-2q_m d\phi$ on the overlap. A global smooth
real one-form potential on this sphere-containing product exists exactly
when $q_m=0$. No circle-bundle normalization or charge quantization is
imposed.

items.title: RN roots, Killing horizons and surface gravity
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2>0$, and use
$f(r)=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2$ on the selected ingoing RN model. If $M^2\ge Q^2$,
the positive roots
$$r_\pm=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-Q^2}$$
are null constant-$r$ hypersurfaces. For the Killing field $\xi=\partial_v$
normalized by the displayed coordinate for which
$g(\xi,\xi)\to-1$ as $r\to\infty$, each is a Killing horizon in the
local sense of
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]], with signed surface
gravity
$$\kappa_\pm=\frac{f'(r_\pm)}2 =\frac{r_\pm-r_\mp}{2r_\pm^2}.$$
At extremality $M^2=Q^2$, the coincident root is $r_H=M$ and
$\kappa_H=0$. If $M^2<Q^2$, $f$ has no positive root and no constant-$r$
null hypersurface of this form. These are local properties of the selected
metric; they do not classify event horizons in a maximal spacetime.

items.title: Regular RN crossings and local bifurcation extension
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2>0$, and $M^2\ge Q^2$ in the selected ingoing
RN model [[def-emg-xs-ingoing-rn]]. Every positive root $r_H$ of $f$ is a
regular crossing: the metric is nondegenerate and the two-form is smooth
there. If $M^2>Q^2$, set
$$r_+=M+\sqrt{M^2-Q^2},\qquad \kappa:=\frac12 f'(r_+)>0.$$
For every auxiliary length $\ell_*>0$, there is a smooth local extension
chart on $(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)^2\times S^2$ with dimensionless
coordinates $U,V$ and
$$UV=-K(r),\qquad K(r):=\frac{r-r_+}{\ell_*}e^{2\kappa h(r)},\qquad K'(r_+)=\ell_*^{-1},$$
where $h$ is smooth. The metric and two-form have smooth coefficients on
the whole chart, including both null axes. The sphere $U=V=0$ is a regular
bifurcation sphere: the extended Killing field $\partial_v$ vanishes there.
On the dense set $UV\ne0$, the source-free RN equations of the current
[[thm-emg-xs-rn-verification]] draft apply; their residual tensors therefore
vanish on the axes as well, conditionally on that exact draft interface and
its proof status. At extremality $M^2=Q^2$, the ingoing chart remains regular
at $r_H=M$, but the simple-root construction is not asserted because
$\kappa=0$.

items.title: Regular ingoing KN metric, field and sphere axes
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$ have units of metres. Set
$$\Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta,\quad \Delta=r^2-2Mr+a^2+q^2,\quad R=r^2+a^2,$$
and let $S^2=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb R^3:X^2+Y^2+Z^2=1\}$ have unit round
metric $\gamma$ and outward area form $\omega$. Define the global one-form
$\beta:=X\,dY-Y\,dX$ and the product
$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}:=\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2,$$
oriented by $dv\wedge dr\wedge\omega$. On this product define
$$\begin{aligned}g_{\mathrm{in}}={}&-\left(1-\frac{2Mr-q^2}{\Sigma}\right)dv^2+2\,dv\,dr-2a\,dr\,\beta-2a\frac{2Mr-q^2}{\Sigma}dv\odot\beta+\Sigma\gamma+a^2\left(1+\frac{2Mr-q^2}{\Sigma}\right)\beta^2,\\\mathcal A_{\mathrm{in}}={}&-\frac{qr}{\Sigma}(dv-a\beta),\qquad \mathcal F_{\mathrm{in}}:=d\mathcal A_{\mathrm{in}},\end{aligned}$$
where $u\odot w=(u\otimes w+w\otimes u)/2$. The time-orientation field
is $$f_0:=1-\frac{2Mr-q^2}{\Sigma},\qquad N:=\partial_v-\frac{1+f_0^2}{2}\partial_r.$$
These formulas define smooth Lorentzian metric and field data on the whole
sphere for every $r>0$, including each positive root of $\Delta$; no
maximal extension, $r=0$ locus, or global uniqueness is asserted. On the
dense pole-free set where $\Delta\ne0$, they are related to the
Boyer-Lindquist data by the advanced coordinate change proved below.

The source-free geometric electrovac equations extend across $\Delta=0$
conditionally on the exact current interface of
[[thm-emg-xs-kn-verification]]: its geometric pole-free equations are used
on the dense complement of the roots and axes, and smoothness then extends
their residuals. That supplier is a current draft theorem and is not claimed
as independently accepted here.

items.title: KN Killing generators, surface gravity, area and potential
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ and $M^2\ge a^2+q^2>0$ in the selected ingoing KN model.
For either $r_H=r_\pm=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-a^2-q^2}$ set
$R_H=r_H^2+a^2$, $\Sigma_H=r_H^2+a^2\cos^2\theta$, and
$$\chi_H=\partial_v+\Omega_H\Psi,\qquad \Omega_H=\frac{a}{R_H},$$
where $\Psi=X\partial_Y-Y\partial_X$ is the smooth rotation field on
$S^2$. The surface $r=r_H$ is a null hypersurface and $\chi_H$ is its
future null normal and Killing generator. Under the specified normalization
$d(g(\chi_H,\chi_H))=-2\kappa_H\chi_H^\flat$ in
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]],
$$\kappa_H=\frac{\Delta'(r_H)}{2R_H} =\frac{r_H-r_{\mathrm{other}}}{2R_H},\qquad \operatorname{Area}(S_H)=4\pi R_H,\qquad -\mathcal A_{\mathrm{in}}(\chi_H)=\frac{q r_H}{R_H}.$$
At the double root $\kappa_H=0$. These are local geometric calculations on
the specified model; they assert no maximality or uniqueness.

items.title: Specified time Killing stationary-limit set and geodesic constants
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Let $M>0$ and $M^2\ge a^2+q^2>0$ in the selected ingoing KN model.
For the specified stationary field $T=\partial_v$,
$$g(T,T)=-\frac{r^2-2Mr+q^2+a^2\cos^2\theta}{\Sigma},\qquad \Sigma=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta.$$
Define its ergoregion by $g(T,T)>0$ and its stationary-limit set by
$g(T,T)=0$, using the specified terminology in
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]]. At each angle where
the discriminant is nonnegative, the stationary-limit radii are
$$r_{E\pm}(\theta)=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-q^2-a^2\cos^2\theta}.$$
Only positive values of these algebraic roots belong to the selected $r>0$ model; in particular a zero lower root is excluded.
If $a\ne0$, then $g(T,T)=a^2\sin^2\theta/\Sigma_H>0$ at every nonpolar
point of the outer horizon $r_+=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2-q^2}$, and
$r_{E+}(\theta)>r_+$. The outer stationary-limit set meets the outer
horizon on the rotation axis. For each affinely parameterized geodesic,
$g(T,\dot\gamma)$ and $g(\Psi,\dot\gamma)$ are constant, where
$\Psi=X\partial_Y-Y\partial_X$ generates rotations. These statements
refer to the specified fields and model.

items.title: Charged KN ring regularity obstruction
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
For the electric KN datum with real $M,a,q$ and $q\ne0$, let
$\mathcal U$ be its Boyer-Lindquist domain $\Sigma>0$, $\Delta\ne0$,
$0<\theta<\pi$. Suppose a sequence $x_n\in\mathcal U$ and a proposed
$C^2$ Lorentzian extension $(\widetilde M,\widetilde g)$ are given, with a
smooth isometric embedding $j:\mathcal U\to\widetilde M$ onto an open
subset, $j(x_n)\to p\in\widetilde M$, and $\Sigma(x_n)\to0$.
Then no such extension exists. When $a\ne0$, the limiting coordinate locus
$r=0$, $\theta=\pi/2$ maps under
$$X=\sqrt{r^2+a^2}\sin\theta\cos\phi,\quad Y=\sqrt{r^2+a^2}\sin\theta\sin\phi,\quad Z=r\cos\theta$$
to $X^2+Y^2=a^2$, $Z=0$. When $q=0$, this charged Ricci-invariant
argument yields no obstruction and makes no vacuum Kerr claim.

items.title: Smooth causal-cone collar barrier with screen directions
items.design_state: Authored conditional draft; exact direct suppliers and unresolved interfaces are recorded in batch-22.dependency-inputs.json.
items.statement:
Consider either (i) the selected ingoing RN model with $M>0$, $Q^2>0$,
$M^2\ge Q^2$, and
$r_H=M+\sqrt{M^2-Q^2}$, or (ii) the selected ingoing KN model with $M>0$,
$M^2\ge a^2+q^2>0$, and
$r_H=M+\sqrt{M^2-a^2-q^2}$. In each case $r_H>0$. There is
$\delta>0$ and a collar
$$\mathcal C=\mathbb R_v\times(r_H-\delta,r_H+\delta)\times S^2$$
on which $\tau:=v-r$ is a smooth temporal function in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]: its gradient is past
timelike and $d\tau(Z)>0$ for every nonzero future causal vector $Z$. There
is a finite $C\ge0$ such that
$$dr(Z)\le C|r-r_H|\,d\tau(Z)$$
for every future causal $Z$ over the collar. On $r=r_H$ one also has
$dr(Z)\le0$. This is a local cone estimate on the two specified metrics; it
is not an event-horizon theorem.

Let $M>0$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2>0$, and $M^2\ge Q^2$. In the selected

reaches arbitrarily large $r$, using the specified definition
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]]. Then
$$\mathcal E=\{(v,r,\omega):r>r_H\},\qquad \partial_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}}\mathcal E=\{r=r_H\}.$$
This is the boundary of the stated escape observable on the selected
manifold. It makes no claim about conformal infinity, a maximal RN extension,
collapse, or cosmic censorship.

items.title: Positive harmonic conformastatic electrovac data
items.design_state: Full local definition or conditional proof authored with the planned claim, exact mathematical hypotheses, and warnings preserved.
items.statement:
Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $H\in C^\infty(D,(0,\infty))$ be independent of time. Write $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ for length coordinates, set $x^0=ct$ when a time variable is used, and require $H$ to be dimensionless. The ordinary Euclidean Laplacian is $\Delta_\delta H:=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_i^2H$; call $H$ harmonic when $\Delta_\delta H=0$. Take $\mathcal M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$, with orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and future direction selected by $N_H=H\partial_{x^0}$.

For a sign $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$ define the metric and global potential one-form

$$g_H=-H^{-2}(dx^0)^2+H^2\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2,\qquad \mathcal A_\sigma=\sigma(H^{-1}-1)\,dx^0.$$

The associated two-form is

$$\mathcal F_\sigma:=d\mathcal A_\sigma=-\sigma\sum_{i=1}^3\frac{H_i}{H^2}\,dx^i\wedge dx^0,\qquad H_i:=\partial_iH.$$

The **positive harmonic conformastatic electrovac data** are the tuple $(\mathcal M,g_H,N_H,o,\mathcal F_\sigma)$ for these choices with the additional condition $\Delta_\delta H=0$ on $D$. The displayed metric, potential and two-form remain defined for every smooth positive $H$, but only the harmonic choices are given this name. The metric is the chart tensor of [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]] and is Lorentzian with the stated future direction by [[lem-emg-conformastatic-chart-is-lorentzian]]. The term “electrovac data” names a candidate for the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; this definition by itself does not assert that the equations hold. The field components have inverse-length units in length coordinates, so the Ricci and quadratic-field components both have inverse-length-squared units.

items.title: Constant-radius Bertotti-Robinson product data
items.design_state: Full local definition or conditional proof authored with the planned claim, exact mathematical hypotheses, and warnings preserved.
items.statement:
Let $S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:|n|=1\}$ carry its induced unit round metric $\gamma_{S^2}$ and outward area form $\omega_{S^2}$. Let $L>0$ have length units. Choose either (i) $f(z)=z^2$ on an open $J\subset(0,\infty)$, or (ii) $f(z)=1+z^2$ on an open $J\subset\mathbb R$. The coordinate $z$ and $\tau$ are dimensionless. On $\mathcal M_{L,f}=\mathbb R_\tau\times J_z\times S^2$, orient by $d\tau\wedge dz\wedge\omega_{S^2}$ and define

$$g_{L,f}=L^2\bigl(-f(z)d\tau^2+f(z)^{-1}dz^2+\gamma_{S^2}\bigr),\qquad \mathcal F_L=-L\,d\tau\wedge dz.$$

The smooth field $N=(L\sqrt{f})^{-1}\partial_\tau$ is unit timelike; it selects the future direction. This explicit metric-field tuple is the **Bertotti-Robinson product data** for this library. “Electrovac” refers to the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and is not asserted by this definition. The product has sphere radius $L$ at every base point.

items.title: Smooth null electrovac wave candidate data
items.design_state: Full local definition or conditional proof authored with the planned claim, exact mathematical hypotheses, and warnings preserved.
items.statement:
Use length coordinates $(u,v,x,y)$ on $\mathbb R^4$. Let $a,b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth profiles with inverse-length units, and let $h:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth dimensionless function satisfying $h_{xx}+h_{yy}=0$ at every $(u,x,y)$. Define the dimensionless function

$$P(u,x,y)=-(a(u)^2+b(u)^2)(x^2+y^2)+h(u,x,y).$$

With orientation $du\wedge dv\wedge dx\wedge dy$, define

$$g=-2\,du\,dv+dx^2+dy^2+P\,du^2,\qquad \mathcal A=-(a(u)x+b(u)y)\,du,\qquad \mathcal F=d\mathcal A=a(u)\,du\wedge dx+b(u)\,du\wedge dy.$$

The vector field $N=\partial_u+\frac{P+1}{2}\partial_v$ has $g(N,N)=-1$ and selects the future direction. The $u,v$ block of $g$ has determinant $-1$, so together with the two positive transverse directions this is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\sqrt{|\det g|}=1$. The tuple $(\mathbb R^4,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ is the **null-wave candidate data** for the equations of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; no field-equation claim is part of this definition. The metric coefficients are dimensionless, and $\mathcal F_{ui}$ has inverse-length units.

items.title: Full harmonic Majumdar-Papapetrou Einstein-Maxwell verification
items.design_state: Full local definition or conditional proof authored with the planned claim, exact mathematical hypotheses, and warnings preserved.
items.statement:
Every datum of [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]] satisfies the source-free geometric Einstein-Maxwell equations of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]:

$$d\mathcal F_\sigma=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F_\sigma)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F_\sigma),\quad Q_{ab}(F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}.$$

More explicitly, with $q_H:=\sum_iH_i^2$, the only nonzero independent raised field components are $\mathcal F^{i0}_\sigma=\sigma H_i/H^2$ and the quadratic-field components are

$$\mathcal F_{\sigma,ab}\mathcal F_\sigma^{ab}=-\frac{2q_H}{H^4},\qquad Q_{00}=\frac{q_H}{2H^6},\qquad Q_{0i}=0,\qquad Q_{ij}=\frac{\delta_{ij}q_H-2H_iH_j}{2H^2}.$$

$$e^0=L\sqrt f\,d\tau,\quad e^1=L f^{-1/2}dz,\quad e^2=L\,d\theta,\quad e^3=L\sin\theta\,d\phi,$$

the Ricci and quadratic Maxwell tensors are

$$\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}=L^{-2}\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,1)_{AB},\qquad Q_{AB}(\mathcal F_L)=\frac1{2L^2}\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,1)_{AB}.$$

All mixed base-sphere entries vanish. The statement is on the chosen open chart domains; it makes no maximal-extension or asymptotic-flatness claim.

items.title: Finite positive multicenter MP exterior and fluxes
items.design_state: Full local definition or conditional proof authored with the planned claim, exact mathematical hypotheses, and warnings preserved.
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$ be an integer, let $a_1,\ldots,a_N\in\mathbb R^3$ be distinct, let $m_A>0$ have length units, and let $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$. On $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{a_1,\ldots,a_N\}$ define

$$H(x)=1+\sum_{A=1}^N\frac{m_A}{|x-a_A|}.$$

Then $H$ is smooth, positive and Euclidean harmonic on $D$, so [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]] and [[thm-emg-xs-mp-verification]] give a smooth source-free geometric electrovac datum on $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$. For each $A$, every coordinate sphere $S_A(r)=\{x:|x-a_A|=r\}$ whose closed ball contains no other center has electric flux $q_e(S_A(r))=\sigma m_A$ and magnetic flux $q_m(S_A(r))=0$. If a coordinate sphere $S_R=\{x:|x|=R\}$ strictly encloses all centers, its fluxes are $q_e(S_R)=\sigma\sum_A m_A$ and $q_m(S_R)=0$. No center is included in the manifold; these are fluxes through regular spheres, not matter-source, horizon-extension, stability, or completeness claims.

items.design_state: Full local definition or conditional proof authored with the planned claim, exact mathematical hypotheses, and warnings preserved.
items.statement:
For every null-wave electrovac datum of [[def-emg-xs-null-wave]] and [[thm-emg-xs-null-wave-verification]],

$$\mathcal F_{ab}\mathcal F^{ab}=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{ab}=0,\qquad R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=0.$$

In the displayed coordinates the only potentially nonzero independent Riemann components are

$$R_{uiuj}=-\frac12P_{ij},\qquad i,j\in\{x,y\}.$$

If $a(u_0)^2+b(u_0)^2>0$ at any $u_0$, then the Riemann tensor is nonzero there; the metric is not flat. Here $R_{abcd}$ and $S$ use the convention in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]].

items.title: Single-center MP is extremal Reissner-Nordström exterior
items.design_state: Full local definition or conditional proof authored with the planned claim, exact mathematical hypotheses, and warnings preserved.
items.statement:
Let $m>0$ have length units, let $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$, put $\rho=|x|$ on $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, and use $H=1+m/\rho$ in [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]]. Under the radial diffeomorphism $R=\rho+m$ from $\rho>0$ to $R>m$, the full metric and field data equal the dyonic Reissner-Nordström datum of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] with

$$M=m,\qquad q_e=\sigma m,\qquad q_m=0,\qquad f(R)=\left(1-\frac mR\right)^2.$$

The parameters satisfy $|q_e|=M$; this is the extremal parameter relation in the displayed RN convention. By [[thm-emg-xs-mp-verification]] and the geometric clause of [[thm-emg-xs-rn-verification]], these identical exterior data satisfy the source-free geometric electrovac equations. The identification is only between the open exteriors $\rho>0$ and $R>m$; no horizon extension or global completeness follows.

items.title: Extremal RN to Bertotti-Robinson in C-infinity local scaling
items.design_state: Full local definition or conditional proof authored with the planned claim, exact mathematical hypotheses, and warnings preserved.
items.statement:
Fix $L>0$ and take the extremal RN datum with $M=q_e=L$, $q_m=0$, on $r>L$ in [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]]. For each dimensionless $\lambda>0$, define

$$\Phi_\lambda(T,R,\omega)=(x^0=T/\lambda,\ r=L+\lambda R,\ \omega),\qquad (T,R,\omega)\in\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2.$$

Writing $g_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda^*g$ and $\mathcal F_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda^*\mathcal F$, one has

$$g_\lambda=-\frac{R^2}{(L+\lambda R)^2}\,dT^2+\frac{(L+\lambda R)^2}{R^2}\,dR^2+(L+\lambda R)^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_\lambda=-\frac{L}{(L+\lambda R)^2}\,dT\wedge dR.$$

As $\lambda\downarrow0$, these tensors converge in $C^\infty_{\rm loc}$ on $\mathbb R_T\times(0,\infty)_R\times S^2$ to

$$g_0=-\frac{R^2}{L^2}dT^2+\frac{L^2}{R^2}dR^2+L^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_0=-\frac1L\,dT\wedge dR.$$

Under $T=L\tau$, $R=Lz$, the limiting datum is exactly the $f(z)=z^2$, $z>0$ product in [[def-emg-xs-br-products]], and it is a geometric electrovac datum by [[thm-emg-xs-br-verification]]. Here $C^\infty_{\rm loc}$ means uniform convergence of every coordinate derivative on every compact subset in a finite smooth atlas. The convergence is only on $R>0$; no extension or convergence across $R=0$ is asserted.

items.title: SI and geometric solution parameter identifications
items.physical_scope: A model-local map from SI mass, angular-momentum, electric-charge, and magnetic-flux inputs to the length parameters in the selected four-dimensional, zero-cosmological-constant Einstein–Maxwell solution families. It fixes no global ADM or Komar identification, magnetic-charge convention, charge quantization, empirical value, observed black-hole claim, or field law.
items.design_state: Authored draft; dependencies and current supplier interfaces are recorded in batch-24 notes and cross-batch evidence.
items.statement:
Use the SI quantities, coordinate convention, and primitive/derived distinction of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], and the zero-cosmological-constant geometric electrovac flux normalization of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. This definition is the model-local parameter map for the RN and KN ansatz families; it is not a claim that nature contains an object with these parameters.

Take $G_N>0$, $c>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ as the gravitational and electromagnetic constants used by this coupled model, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Let $m_*>0$ be a selected SI mass parameter in kg, $J\in\mathbb R$ a selected angular-momentum parameter in kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, $Q_e\in\mathbb R$ a selected electric charge parameter in C, and $\Phi_B\in\mathbb R$ a selected magnetic flux in Wb through an oriented sphere. These are the chosen SI inputs of this parametrization; this role is local to the solution families and is not a universal ontology for mass, angular momentum, or charge.

For the geometric flux integrals below, retain the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention explicitly stated by [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and defined by [[def-countable-choice]]. No arbitrary-index choice principle or magnetic-charge quantization is added.

Set

$$\alpha:=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad \mathcal F:=\alpha F,$$

where $F$ is the SI electromagnetic two-form of [[def-emg-geometry-units]] and $\mathcal F$ is its geometric normalization. In length coordinates $F_{ab}$ has unit T, $\mathcal F_{ab}$ has unit m$^{-1}$, and $\alpha$ has unit T$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$. For an oriented sphere $S$, write the geometric flux parameters as

$$q_e:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$

The SI electric-flux convention is $Q_e=\varepsilon_0c\int_S\star_gF$, and the magnetic quantity used here is the flux $\Phi_B=\int_S F$. Thus

$$q_e=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c}Q_e=\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}\,Q_e,\qquad q_m=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi}\Phi_B.$$

The second equality in the electric formula uses the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$. Both $q_e$ and $q_m$ have units of length; $q_m$ is a flux parameter and is not assigned a universal SI magnetic-charge convention. If one separately chooses the convention $Q_m:=\Phi_B/\mu_0$ with unit A m, then the same definition reads $q_m=\sqrt{G_N\mu_0/(4\pi c^4)}\,Q_m$; this optional relabeling adds no new physical assumption or quantization rule.

For the metric parameters, set

$$M:=\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\qquad a:=\frac{J}{m_*c},\qquad Q_{\mathrm{geom}}^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2.$$

Here $M$, $a$, $q_e$, and $q_m$ are derived length parameters, while $m_*$, $J$, $Q_e$, $\Phi_B$, $G_N$, $c$, and $\mu_0$ are the selected inputs of this map. The dimensionless metric coefficients use $M/r$, $a/r$, and $Q_{\mathrm{geom}}^2/r^2$. Horizon radii, areas, angular velocities, and surface gravities are further derived quantities of a specified solution, not additional primitive inputs.

These parameter identifications do not establish that $M$ equals an ADM or Komar mass, or that $J$ equals an ADM or Komar angular momentum; such identifications need their own global hypotheses and proofs. They supply no empirical values for $G_N$ or $\mu_0$, no measured black-hole parameters, no global potential in a nonzero magnetic-flux sector, and no claim of charge quantization. The source treatments use differing signatures, charge normalizations, and natural or Gaussian unit conventions; the SI formulas above are fixed by the stated local conventions and are not copied without conversion.

items.physical_scope: Conditional source-free RN model deduction for the equation-based smooth Einstein–Maxwell branch with zero cosmological constant and no material stress or current, on positive-radius static coordinate domains away from the roots. Let $m_*>0$ be an SI mass parameter, $Q_e\in\mathbb R$ an SI electric charge parameter, and $\Phi_B\in\mathbb R$ an SI magnetic flux through an oriented sphere. Use [[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]] to set

$$M=\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\qquad q_e=\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}\,Q_e,\qquad q_m=\frac{\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}}{4\pi}\Phi_B.$$

Thus $M,q_e,q_m$ are real length parameters. Let $J\subset(0,\infty)$ be a nonempty open set on which $f(r)=1-2M/r+(q_e^2+q_m^2)/r^2$ has no zero, and use the exact dyonic RN metric and smooth two-form of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] on $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J\times S^2$, with $x^0=ct$. Write $\alpha=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}$, $F=\mathcal F/\alpha$, and

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),\qquad \kappa_E:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}.$$

In the equation-based physical model of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]], specialize to $\Lambda=0$, $j=0$, and $T^m=0$ on this domain. Conditional on the exact current draft statements and hypotheses of [[thm-emg-xs-rn-verification]] and [[lem-emg-maxwell-current-forms]], the RN datum satisfies the adopted source-free equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF^{ab}=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}.$$

This is a conditional model deduction, not a claim that nature contains an RN object. The coordinate domain excludes $r=0$; the conclusion does not assign a regular source there or require a global potential when $q_m\ne0$.

items.statement:
Take a pure-electric KN seed with SI inputs $m_*>0$, $J\in\mathbb R$ and $Q_0\in\mathbb R$, zero magnetic flux, and parameters
$$M=\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\qquad a=\frac{J}{m_*c},\qquad q_0=\gamma_e Q_0,\qquad \alpha=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad \gamma_e:=\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}.$$
For a fixed real duality angle $\beta$, rotate its geometric field by
$$\mathcal F_\beta:=\cos\beta\,\mathcal F_0+\sin\beta\,\star_g\mathcal F_0,$$
where $\mathcal F_0=\alpha F_0$ is the seed's geometric field. On the seed's
stated Boyer–Lindquist domains, the dual-rotated geometric field is source-free
and has unchanged geometric stress, conditional on [[lem-emg-xs-duality]];
thus $F_\beta:=\mathcal F_\beta/\alpha$ and the same metric solve the same
equation-based SI model, conditional on [[pthm-emg-xs-kn-model]]. On the
full-sphere exterior $\mathcal X:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(R_0,\infty)_r\times S^2$ of [[def-emg-xs-kn-full-sphere-exterior]], with $R_0>4|M|$, the
resulting geometric flux parameters and matching SI inputs are
$$q_e=q_0\cos\beta,\qquad q_m=q_0\sin\beta,\qquad Q_e^{\mathrm{out}}=Q_0\cos\beta,\qquad \Phi_B^{\mathrm{out}}=\mu_0cQ_0\sin\beta.$$
In particular $q_e^2+q_m^2=q_0^2$, so the metric is unchanged. On each sphere-containing full-sphere exterior region, $\int_{S_r}\mathcal F_\beta=4\pi q_m$; hence a global smooth real one-form potential for $\mathcal F_\beta$ there is impossible if $q_m\ne0$, by finite-chain Stokes. In the nonrotating case $a=0$, the corresponding dyonic RN field also has the explicit north/south patch potentials and exact global-potential criterion of [[prop-emg-xs-rn-local-gauges]]. items.title: Stationary RN observer frequency ratio
items.physical_scope: Conditional phase-frequency ratio for a local future null eikonal phase crossing two static observers in a source-free RN model region. Ideal-clock and geometric-optics readings are adopted assumptions; no emitted or received measurement, apparatus model, or empirical agreement is asserted.

items.statement:
Let $m_*>0$, $Q_e,\Phi_B\in\mathbb R$, and use [[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]] and [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] for the dyonic RN metric on $\mathcal M_J=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J_r\times S^2$, where $J$ is a connected open interval with $f(r)=1-2M/r+(q_e^2+q_m^2)/r^2>0$. The coordinate $x^0=ct$ and $r$ have units of metres. Put $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$; it is the future static Killing field on this region. Let $I_\gamma\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $\gamma:I_\gamma\to\mathcal M_J$ be a $C^2$ curve, and let $W$ be an open neighborhood of $\gamma(I_\gamma)$ carrying a dimensionless $C^2$ phase $\theta:W\to\mathbb R$. Set $k=d\theta$ and $K=k^\sharp$. Assume the eikonal equation $g^{-1}(d\theta,d\theta)=0$ holds throughout $W$, and that $K$ is nowhere zero and future directed along $\gamma(I_\gamma)$. Parameterize the phase ray by $\gamma'(\lambda)=K(\gamma(\lambda))$, which fixes its affine parameter normalization. For each spatial point $(r,\omega)\in J\times S^2$ and nonempty open interval $I\subset\mathbb R$, define the static observer curve $\sigma_{r,\omega}:I\to\mathcal M_J$ by $\sigma_{r,\omega}(s)=(s,r,\omega)$, where $s=x^0$ has units of metres. It is smooth and regular with tangent $\xi$, and it is future timelike because $g(\xi,\xi)=-f(r)<0$. Its proper-time parameter satisfies $d\tau/ds=\sqrt{f(r)}/c$ under the metric proper-time definition, so its normalized four-velocity is
$$U(r):=\frac{c}{\sqrt{f(r)}}\,\xi,\qquad g(U,U)=-c^2,\qquad \nu_U:=-\frac{k(U)}{2\pi}.$$
Here $U=d\sigma_{r,\omega}/d\tau$ is normalized by the SI proper-time convention of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]], and $\nu_U$ is the phase frequency in cycles per unit ideal-clock time under [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. If $\gamma$ intersects static observer curves $\sigma_{r_E,\omega_E}$ and $\sigma_{r_R,\omega_R}$ at events $E$ and $R$, respectively, with $r_E,r_R\in J$, then the conditional model prediction is
$$\frac{\nu_R}{\nu_E}=\sqrt{\frac{f(r_E)}{f(r_R)}}.$$
The phase data and source-free RN model are conditional inputs; the formula is not a reported observation or a claim of measured precision.

items.statement:
Let $m_*>0$, $Q_e\in\mathbb R$, and $\Phi_B\in\mathbb R$ be the SI mass, electric-charge, and magnetic-flux inputs of [[pthm-emg-xs-rn-model]]. Put $M=G_Nm_*/c^2>0$, $q_e=\sqrt{G_N/(4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4)}Q_e$, $q_m=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}\Phi_B/(4\pi)$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$, and $f(r)=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2$. Use the selected ingoing product $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2$ and its metric, field, and future orientation from [[def-emg-xs-ingoing-rn]].

For $Q^2>0$ and $M^2\ge Q^2$, let $r_\pm=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-Q^2}$. Each positive root is a regular null hypersurface and a Killing horizon generated by $\xi=\partial_v$, with the convention

$$\kappa_H:=\frac{f'(r_H)}2=\frac{r_H-r_{\mathrm{other}}}{2r_H^2}.$$

Thus $\kappa_+=0$ at extremality and $\kappa_\pm$ has unit m$^{-1}$; the associated SI acceleration convention is $c^2\kappa_\pm$. At a simple outer root, $\kappa_+>0$, the selected ingoing extension has a local bifurcation chart with dimensionless coordinates $U,V$ satisfying $UV=-K(r)$ and an auxiliary coordinate length $\ell_*>0$. At extremality the ingoing chart is regular but this simple-root chart is not asserted.

Use the exact path and relative-boundary convention of [[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]]: the path is continuous, future causal, and piecewise $C^1$ with a finite subdivision on each compact parameter segment; one such path must reach arbitrarily large $r$.

Define $\mathcal E$ on this product to be the set of points from which a future piecewise $C^1$ causal path has unbounded radial coordinate. Conditional on the exact draft mathematical interface of [[thm-emg-xs-rn-escape]], for $Q^2>0$ and $M^2\ge Q^2$,

$$\mathcal E=\{(v,r,\omega):r>r_+\},\qquad \partial_{\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}}\mathcal E=\{r=r_+\}.$$

For $Q^2=0$, the only positive root is $2M$, it is a regular simple crossing with $\kappa=1/(4M)$, and the same explicit escape observable has boundary $r=2M$. For $Q^2>M^2$, there is no positive root and every point of $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}$ belongs to $\mathcal E$. These are statements about the selected metric and escape observable, not an event-horizon assertion requiring a conformal completion.
